title: Il popolo salva il popolo: la risposta popolare al terremoto e al fascismo
content:
Abbiamo tradotto un reportage di Colombia Informa, agenzia di stampa alternativa colombiana in merito a quanto sta accadendo a livello sociale e politico in seguito al devastante terremoto avvenuto nel Paese qualche settimana fa.


CI.-

Comunità e organizzazioni sociali di tutto il paese si sono unite per sostenere le persone colpite dal terremoto in Chocó, Risaralda, Valle del Cauca, Caldas e altri territori dell’occidente colombiano. Di fronte a loro, però, c’è l’assenza del governo di De la Espriella, di sindaci e governatori che ignorano il lavoro di migliaia di soccorritori, cercano di bloccare la ricerca dei sopravvissuti sotto le macerie e suscitano indignazione con la presenza di militari israeliani.


La Rete di Fratellanza e Solidarietà con la Colombia (Redher), insieme ai giornalisti di Colombia Informa, ha attraversato Chocó, Risaralda, Caldas e Valle. Insieme alle organizzazioni sociali di questi territori, raccontiamo la resistenza con cui le comunità stanno assistendo solidalmente le migliaia di vittime del terremoto del 10 agosto scorso.


Ricostruire a Manizales. Barrio Bajo Andes. 13 agosto 2026


Il popolo salva il popolo: un quadro d’insieme


Come in una nuova ondata di mobilitazione popolare, milioni di colombiani, senza alcun sostegno del governo, si sono uniti per salvare vite e sostenere i soccorsi. Sono arrivate squadre di soccorritori — i cosiddetti “topos” — dalla Colombia, dal Messico e da altri paesi, insieme a cani da salvataggio messi a disposizione dai loro addestratori. Altri hanno raccolto e trasportato aiuti, allestito cucine comunitarie come quella del parco Olaya di Pereira, dotata di spazi di assistenza per tutti, comprese le stesse comunità sopravvissute al sisma. Si raccolgono donazioni, si offre assistenza medica e sostegno psicosociale, con l’aiuto di internazionalisti impegnati ad assistere le migliaia di persone colpite dal terremoto di magnitudo 7,4 sulla scala Richter, che ha distrutto vite e case.


Solidarietà nel sindacato di Sinaltrainal. Dosquebradas, 14 agosto 2026.


Ingegneri, architetti, professionisti delle terapie psicosociali, operatori per l’infanzia e tecnici incaricati di verificare l’agibilità delle abitazioni sopravvissute al sisma si sono uniti a questo sforzo.


Sindacalisti, studenti, giovani della Prima Linea, organizzazioni come il Processo delle Comunità Nere e altri gruppi afrodiscendenti, indigeni, femministi, delle diversità sessuali e contadini, oltre al Congresso dei Popoli, al Coordinamento Nazionale Agrario (CNA) e a Sinaltrainal, tra molte altre, hanno messo in piedi in tempi record un’infrastruttura popolare per sostenere le proprie comunità in Chocó, Risaralda, Valle del Cauca e Caldas.


Pentola comunitaria nel quartiere Bajo Andes de Manizales.


Terremoto e De la Espriella: una tragedia umanitaria


Paradossalmente, gli stessi movimenti e comunità che fin dalle prime ore si sono dedicati a soccorrere feriti e vittime hanno subìto la persecuzione della violenza paramilitare, da sempre alleata dello Stato e delle élite colombiane. Queste élite, dopo elezioni contestate, hanno portato alla vittoria Abelardo De la Espriella, lo stesso che aveva promesso di “sventrare la sinistra”.


Centro di raccolta presso l’università di Caldas a Manizales. 13 agosto 2026


Dopo la tragedia del 10 agosto, quando il terremoto ha stravolto la vita di migliaia di persone in Chocó, Risaralda, Valle del Cauca, Caldas e altri territori, migliaia di persone nella zona colpita e in tutto il paese lottano per far fronte alla catastrofe, arrivata pochi giorni dopo l’insediamento di De la Espriella, avvenuto senza un vero passaggio di consegne con il governo precedente.


Militarizzazione. Centro di Pereira. 14 agosto 2026


Sono diventate subito virali le denunce dei vigili del fuoco volontari, esclusi — a loro dire — dai soccorsi dal comune di Pereira e da altre autorità. A queste si sono aggiunte le proteste per la ripetuta sospensione, durata ore, delle attività di ricerca. A Pereira diverse persone hanno denunciato la morte di sopravvissuti, deceduti per negligenza delle autorità: sepolti sotto migliaia di tonnellate di terra e cemento, sono morti senza alcun aiuto da parte del governo.


Centro di Pereira. 14 agosto 2026


Foto e indifferenza


Lo stesso De la Espriella si è recato nelle zone del disastro “solo per farsi fotografare”, denunciano le persone sul posto. Se n’è poi andato in mezzo a un caos istituzionale, con scontri persino tra le stesse …

author: By L. Cam Anderson, Contributor and Niko Georgiades, Unicorn Riot
title: Palestinians Condemn Israel’s Interceptions of Global Freedom Flotilla
content:
Gaza City, Gaza – New boats have

set sail

 in another attempt to break Israel’s nearly two-decade-long siege on Gaza. This comes after Israeli forces intercepted

at least 70 boats

 in multiple flotillas carrying aid to Gaza and

detained

,

beat

 and

abused

 international activists in late April and mid-May. Those attacks by Israel were quickly condemned by Palestinians in Gaza who held multiple press conferences on the shores of the Mediterranean Sea in solidarity with the flotillas.


“We are protesting here today to strongly condemn the Israeli act of violence, aggression and its piracy against the flotilla,” Sujud Shanawra, a 27-year-old Palestinian activist, told Unicorn Riot on May 1.


She called on the international community to “end its complicity and its impunity that it gives to the Israeli occupation.”


On May 18, Israel intercepted the last boat in the latest flotilla, which was 72 vessels strong at its peak. The flotilla carried a cumulative load of humanitarian aid

weighing more than 11,000 kilograms

.


Before that, one of Israel’s largest single attacks against the flotilla came on May 1, when the country’s military arrested 181 members of the flotilla crew off the coast of Greece, transporting them to Greek custody on the island of Crete.


The interceptions, which began more than 600 nautical miles from Gaza on April 29, did not blindside activists. In fact it was expected, according to Nasr Hajjo, organizer of a protest on May 1 in the Al-Shati refugee camp west of Gaza City. 


“You have risked your lives to break the siege of Gaza,” Hajjo said in message directed at the flotilla’s crew. “We are waiting for the siege on Gaza to be broken, and the suffering children of Gaza are waiting for the siege to be broken and for you to come to the Gaza Strip to break the siege and bring in aid and supplies.”


The Freedom Flotilla Coalition (FFC) has been attempting to break Israel’s blockade of Gaza since it was established in 2010, raising awareness internationally of the blockade’s effects on the people of Gaza.


In 2025, the FFC joined other Palestinian human rights initiatives to form

the Global Sumud Flotilla

, which was intercepted by Israel in international waters following a series of drone attacks against the civilian crews.


After this year’s flotilla attacks, the International Centre of Justice for Palestinians (ICJP) submitted testimonies to

the International Criminal Court

 from flotilla crew members who allege Israel subjected them to excessive force and mistreatment while in custody.


“Israel’s repeated disregard for international law, including Law of the Sea in relation to Gaza Flotilla incidents, reflects a pattern of percieved impunity that has gone largely unchecked by many Western governments, despite the involvement of their own citizens as flotilla participants and reported cases of mistreatment, including allegations of physical abuse and unlawful detention,” the ICJP wrote.


The United Nations established the Convention on the Law of the Sea in 1994 to set an international legal framework for all maritime activities. Part of the framework establishes a country’s “territorial sea” up to 12 nautical miles where the state can set laws and regulate the body of water’s use. A further 12 nautical miles marks the “contiguous zone,” where the country’s ability to control and regulate is much more limited. Beyond that, a country is prohibited from exercising sovereignty and enforcing its own laws on passing vessels.


Vessels in international waters are subject to the laws of the flag it is flying. No Israeli flag flew above any of the flotilla boats.


The United States and Israel are not parties to the Law of the Sea, which has a total of 172 signatory countries.


Freedom Flotilla and Global Sumud Tracker


The 2025 Global Sumud Flotilla made it closer to Gaza than any other attempt, coming within about 70 nautical miles of the country’s border. None have made it within the 12 nautical miles of Israel’s coast that would allow the country to enforce its laws on the flotillas under international law.


During a May 6 rally at Gaza Port, a number of popular organizations came together to show support and express solidarity with the flotilla crews.

author: cindy milstein
title: Nicht einfach tatenlos zusehen: 20 Dinge, die du tun kannst, um dem Faschismus entgegenzuwirken
content:
Jüdische Anarchist*innen äußern sich dazu, wie sich Menschen in diesem sich wandelnden Umfeld organisieren und engagieren können.


von: https://itsgoingdown.org/dont-just-do-nothing-20-things-you-can-do-to-counter-fascism/; 21.11.2024


Hier das pdf des Zines [englisch]:

https://itsgoingdown.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/DontJustDoNothing_CounterFascism_IMPOSED.pdf


von Cindy Milstein (they)


Du bist nicht verpflichtet, das Werk zu vollenden, aber du bist auch nicht frei, davon Abstand zu nehmen. —Pirkei Avot (2:21)


Da der Christofaschismus die Zügel der Macht in den USA übernimmt und damit den gesamten Kontinent und die ganze Welt beeinflusst, sollte es mittlerweile völlig klar sein, dass der Appell an den Staat – an jeden Staat – eine verlorene Strategie ist. Die Welt hatte bereits verloren, als die „Wahl“ im November dieses Jahres zwischen zwei Varianten des Faschismus stand.


Wir bieten euch diese Auswahl an Ideen an und ermutigen euch, selbstständig und gemeinsam zu denken und zu handeln – denn genau das ist die einzige erfolgreiche Strategie. Wenn jede einzelne dieser Ideen für sich genommen nicht ausreichend erscheint – nun, das ist sie auch nicht.


Das Zitat aus den Pirkei Avot, die vielleicht bekannteste und am häufigsten zitierte Lehre aus jüdischen Texten, wurde vor etwa zweitausend Jahren verfasst. So viele Formen des Despotismus – Reiche, Monarchien und Staaten – sind in dieser Zeit entstanden und untergegangen. Wir sind nicht allein, als Anarchist*innen und Jüd*innen, in unserem ethischen Imperativ, uns mit jeder Art von Autorität auseinanderzusetzen.


Vorfahren im Laufe der gesamten Menschheitsgeschichte – Menschen aller Hautfarben, Geschlechter und Kulturen dieser Erde – haben gemeinsam gekämpft, um sich der Auferlegung von Zwang und hierarchischer Gewalt zu widersetzen. Entscheidend ist, dass sich die Menschen seit Jahrtausenden autonom organisiert, verteidigt und unzählige Formen der gegenseitigen Hilfe, der kollektiven Fürsorge und der Selbstverwaltung praktiziert haben – was oft als „präfigurative Politik“ bezeichnet wird. Sie haben die Welten, die sie sich wünschen, nicht aufgeschoben, sondern direkt so gehandelt, als wären sie bereits frei.


Als Rebellen in der Diaspora lehrt uns unser Judentum, auf Solidarität über alle Grenzen hinweg zu vertrauen. Unsere Lehren zwingen uns, uns auf die Gemeinschaft anderer zu stützen, um ein lebenswertes Leben zu führen – ganz gleich, ob wir trauern oder feiern oder uns immer wieder damit auseinandersetzen, wie Befreiung aussehen sollte und könnte. Wenn wir jede Woche den Schabbat beginnen – fünfundzwanzig Stunden, in denen wir „die kommende Welt“ praktizieren – und ihn mit der Hawdala beenden – wenn wir uns wieder in diese brutale „Welt, wie sie ist“ zurückbegeben –, tun wir dies mit geflochtenen Opfergaben (Brot bzw. eine Kerze). Solche Geflechte unterstreichen in diesen Zeiten die Notwendigkeit der Verflechtung, der Verbundenheit zwischen jedem Einzelnen von uns, aus allen Lebensbereichen, die den Faschismus zerstören und befreiende gesellschaftliche Veränderungen herbeiführen wollen.


Mögen alle freiheitssuchenden Menschen Seite an Seite auf diese Ziele zusteuern, indem sie einander mehr lieben und füreinander sorgen.


Hier sind zwanzig Dinge, die du tun kannst, um dem Faschismus entgegenzuwirken – ja, du! Ja, jetzt! Erfinde und setze auch noch viele, viele weitere Dinge in die Tat um. Dies ist nur ein Anfang.


1. Praktiziere „Doikayt“ (Präsenz) in deinen persönlichen Beziehungen. Wie würde es aussehen, wenn du dich bei jedem deiner Liebsten entsprechend eurer aktuellen Lebensumstände erkundigst und einander liebevoll mitteilst, wie ihr euch die Welt vorstellt, die ihr aufbauen wollt? Finde heraus, welche „Bodenverbesserungen“ in Gedanken, Worten und Taten notwendig sind, damit diese Samen gedeihen können.


2. Kocht Suppe für andere und hört nicht auf, sie zum Suppeessen einzuladen! Seid ein Grund zum Leben.


3. Baut ein Unterstützungsnetzwerk auf. Schließt euch mit Gleichgesinnten zusammen und setzt auf Qualität statt Quantität; ein paar engagierte Mitstreiter können mehr bewirken als eine große, aber leidenschaftslose Gruppe. Schafft Kunst dazu. Euer Unterstützungsnetzwerk, die Liebe eurer Freunde und Familie, kann immer noch größer werden; baut es mit Sorgfalt und Absicht weiter aus. Schafft noch mehr Kunst dazu. author: anred
title: «Israel es clave para entender a las nuevas extremas derechas»
content:
Pablo Stefanoni


Entrevista a Pablo Stefanoni sobre la salida de su nuevo libro, 

Un fantasma recorre el mundo

, y el ascenso de unas extremas derechas que combinan rebeldía antiprogresista, defensa del orden y radicalización conservadora. Antiwokismo, crisis de las izquierdas, debate sobre el fascismo y el lugar de Israel en la recomposición reaccionaria global.

Por Jacobin Latinoamérica.


Entrevista por Mariano Schuster

[1]


En 

Un fantasma recorre el mundo

. Cómo funciona la máquina de guerra reaccionaria (y qué podemos hacer para enfrentarla)

 (Siglo XXI, Buenos Aires-Madrid, 2026), Pablo Stefanoni vuelve sobre las extremas derechas en un momento en que estas se han consolidado en el Norte global y se han expandido con fuerza en América Latina. El ensayista argentino reconstruye los lenguajes, fantasmas y dispositivos de las «batallas culturales» en curso: la circulación transnacional de repertorios reaccionarios, la utilidad y los límites de la categoría de fascismo para entender las nuevas amenazas, y el modo en que el «antiwokismo» se convirtió en un pegamento para fuerzas ultras muy diversas. A su vez, el libro avanza sobre la forma en que la defensa de Israel se volvió una vía de legitimación para numerosas extremas derechas occidentales que, después de 1945, habían cargado con el peso del antisemitismo y hoy encuentran en el «anti-antisemitismo» un certificado de respetabilidad y un arma contra musulmanes, palestinos e izquierdas. En esta conversación para Jacobin con Mariano Schuster, Stefanoni analiza esas derivas reaccionarias y, al mismo tiempo, interroga las dificultades de unas izquierdas que buscan volver a disputar el sentido común, las emociones políticas y la idea misma de futuro.


MS


En tu reciente libro 

Un fantasma recorre el mundo: Cómo funciona la máquina de guerra reaccionaria (y qué podemos hacer para enfrentarla)

 volvés sobre algunos temas que ya habías trabajado en 

¿La rebeldía se volvió de derecha?

, pero en un contexto distinto. Figuras que hace pocos años parecían excéntricas, marginales o propias de internet hoy gobiernan, influyen sobre gobiernos o disputan el centro de la escena pública. ¿Qué cambió desde entonces? ¿Qué aprendimos de las nuevas derechas desde que dejaron de ser una rareza cultural y se convirtieron en una fuerza política efectiva?


PS


Cuando escribí 

¿La rebeldía se volvió de derecha?

, publicado a comienzos de 2021, algunos de los personajes aparecían como unos chiflados; figuras grotescas, marginales. En ese universo estaba incluido el propio Javier Milei, que aún no era un dirigente político sino un economista de televisión que difundía una prédica antikeynesiana y anticolectivista a los gritos, e incluso de manera soez.


Es cierto que las derechas radicales y extremas ya se habían expandido por Europa y Estados Unidos, pero en América Latina seguían apareciendo como fuerzas exóticas, relativamente ajenas a la dinámica de los sistemas políticos nacionales. Países como Argentina se sentían al margen de ese fenómeno. Lo novedoso es la rapidez con que se integraron a esos mapas políticos. Hoy pueden ganar o perder elecciones, pero ya no constituyen un fenómeno marginal, exterior o pasajero. No son una ola imparable, pero son una marca de la época. Puede perder Trump y, al mismo tiempo, crecer la AfD en Alemania o Marine Le Pen en Francia. Netanyahu podría eventualmente dejar el gobierno, pero la derecha israelí seguiría siendo muy importante. Viktor Orbán fue finalmente derrotado, pero para ganarle a la derecha la izquierda húngara debió apoyar a un conservador y quedarse casi sin diputados; eso también dice algo sobre los desplazamientos políticos.


El cambio más importante es que estas derechas forman parte de la competencia política de una manera inédita desde la posguerra y que, en buena parte del mundo occidental, han logrado darles el sorpasso a las derechas tradicionales. Dejaron de ser una anomalía del sistema para convertirse en una de sus posibilidades. Por eso no conviene analizarlas como una moda pasajera ni tampoco como una fuerza destinada inevitablemente a imponerse, sino como un componente ya integrado de la política contemporánea, capaz de reorganizar lenguajes, adversarios y límites de lo políticamente aceptable.


MS

title: Wer in Sachsen-Anhalt regieren wird – Die Symbiose von Posterboys und völkischen Nationalisten
content:
In Sachsen-Anhalt könnte schon bald die Alternative für Deutschland regieren. Aktuell gilt die Partei in Umfragen als Favoritin und dürfte Anfang September als stärkste Kraft aus der Wahl hervorgehen. Damit würde Sachsen-Anhalt als erstes Bundesland von der AfD regiert werden. Doch wer führt die AfD in Sachsen-Anhalt?


von Mathias H.


Nach Informationen aus dem Umfeld der AfD werden schon seit Monaten Mitarbeiter gesucht, um bis zu 200 Beamte auszutauschen

1

. Zunächst sollen sie die Umsetzung eines Sofortprogramms ermöglichen, das in den ersten 100 Tagen einer AfD-geführten Landesregierung greifen soll. Wie sich der Landesverband diese ersten Monate vorstellt, zeigt ein entsprechender Flyer. Versprochen werden unter anderem das Ende von Regenbogenflaggen an Schulen, sofortige Abschiebungen und der Start der Kampagne

#deutschdenken

 als Gegenprojekt zur bisherigen Landeskampagne

#moderndenken

. Diese symbolischen Vorhaben geben einen ersten Eindruck davon, welche Richtung eine AfD-Regierung einschlagen könnte. Diesen Eindruck prägt auch einen Großteil der Berichterstattung im Vorfeld der Landtagswahl am 6. September in Sachsen-Anhalt. Naheliegend erscheint denen die Annahme, dass hinter diesem Kurs ein geschlossen völkisch geprägter Landesverband steht – doch dieser Eindruck greift zu kurz. Ein genauer Blick auf die heutige AfD in Sachsen-Anhalt zeichnet ein anderes Bild. An der Spitze des ostdeutschen Landesverbands stehen derzeit zwei prägende Figuren: Ulrich Siegmund und Hans-Thomas Tillschneider. Sie übernehmen unterschiedliche Rollen innerhalb der Partei und verkörpern verschiedene Führungsstile. Was sie jedoch verbindet, ist ihre Nähe zur extremen Rechten.


Ein Blick in den Wahlkampf der AfD in Sachsen-Anhalt vermittelt den Eindruck, dass der Spitzenkandidat Ulrich Siegmund der tonangebende Politiker in der Partei sein könnte. In den Medien erscheint er als „AfD-Popstar“

2


und als „gelassene Frontfigur einer wütenden Partei“

3

, spricht bei Markus Lanz und gibt sich bürgernah. In der Partei fungierte er bisher vor allem als Fraktionsvorsitzender im Landtag und sorgte für eine geordnete Führung der Partei. Zusammen mit Tobias Rausch gehört Siegmund zum sogenannten Münzenmaier-Netzwerk innerhalb der AfD. Dieses bildete sich in Folge des Bundesparteitags der AfD 2022, der wegen Unstimmigkeiten vorzeitig beendet werden musste, und sorgt sich vor allem um das Organisieren und Professionalisieren der Partei. In dieser Tradition übernehmen auch Rausch und Siegmund ihre Aufgaben in Sachsen-Anhalt. Während Rausch bisher für die parlamentarische Koordination verantwortlich war, tritt Siegmund als Gesicht des Landesverbands auf. Er gibt der AfD ein moderates Erscheinungsbild und inszeniert sie als regierungsfähig, ohne sich vom rechten Parteiflügel abzugrenzen. Beispielsweise lehnt er Zuwanderung ab, fordert Abschiebehaft und Remigration, spielt aber den Bestürzten, wenn er in einer Talkshow auf die Verbindungen zur extremen Rechten angesprochen wird.


Ulrich Siegmund pflegt jedoch Verbindungen in die extreme Rechte und arbeitet mit entsprechenden Akteuren zusammen. So nahm er im November 2023 an dem konspirativen Treffen in Potsdam teil, bei dem der österreichische Rechtsextremist Martin Sellner seinen

Masterplan zur Remigration

 vorstellte. Darüber hinaus stützt sich Siegmund im aktuellen Wahlkampf auf Personen und Organisationen aus dem rechten Vorfeld. Sein Wahlkampfshop wird von der

Identitären Bewegung

Ein Prozent

6

Nach außen tritt Ulrich Siegmund also als Gesicht und Frontfigur der AfD auf. Die Führung der Partei erschöpft sich jedoch nicht darin – die ideologische Ausrichtung wird von einem breiteren Netzwerk innerhalb der Parteispitze getragen. Zu diesem gehören der Landesvorsitzende Martin Reichardt, der zuletzt mit einem mutmaßlichen Hitlergruß für Schlagzeilen sorgte, sowie der stellvertretende Vorsitzende Hans-Thomas Tillschneider und der Beisitzer Oliver Kirchner. title: Almanya: AfD'nin Saksonya-Anhalt’ta tek başına iktidar olasılığına karşı toplumsal seferberlik
content:
Almanya Demokratik Cumhuriyeti'nin (Doğu Almanya) çökmesinden sonra Federal Almanya'ya katılan en eski doğu eyaletlerinden Saksonya-Anhalt'ta 6 Eylül’de yapılacak Eyalet Meclisi seçimlerine üç haftadan az kala seçim yarışı alışılmışın ötesine geçti.


Protofaşist AfD’nin ilk kez bir eyalette tek başına hükümet kurma olasılığı karşısında geniş ve heyecanlı bir toplumsal hareketlilik başladı.


AfD Saksonya-Anhalt'ta açık farkla önde


Son Politix araştırmasında Almanya İçin Alternatif (AfD) yüzde 43 ile geleneksel sağ parti Hristiyan Demokratlar'ın (CDU) yüzde 23 önünde yol alıyor. Sol Parti yüzde 13, SPD yüzde 7, Yeşiller yüzde 5'te. Infratest dimap’ın temmuz sonu araştırması da AfD’yi yüzde 41’de gösteriyordu.


AfD’nin salt çoğunluğu kazanıp kazanmayacağı, yalnızca kendi aldığı oya bağlı değil. SPD ve Yeşiller'in ve diğer küçük partilerin yüzde 5 barajını aşıp aşmayacakları da bunda rol oynayacak.  


Bu durumda seçim yaklaştıkça soru “AfD birinci parti mi olacak"tan “AfD tek başına iktidar mı olacak"a kayıyor.


“Gerçek vatan sevgisi”ni AfD’ye bırakmıyorlar


Son girişim, kendisini bağımsız ve partilerüstü olarak tanımlayan "Mehr als uns trennt  (Bizi ayırandan fazlası)" derneğinin başlattığı “Wahre Heimatliebe ist…” – “Gerçek vatan sevgisi…” kampanyası çevresinde yürüyor.


Sandra Hüller, Christian Friedel, Anna Schudt ve Max Simonischek gibi tanınmış oyuncuların yanı sıra spor, bilim ve iş dünyasından ünlüler de kampanyaya katıldı. Spor Klübü SC Magdeburg Başkan Yardımcısı René Bethke, iş insanı Karl Gerhold, arkeolog Harald Meller, eski üniversite rektörü Anne Lequy ve BMW motor sporları ekip yöneticisi Torsten Schubert de destekçiler arasında. 


Kampanyanın hedefi yalnızca “AfD’ye oy vermeyin” demekle kalmıyor. Afişler ve videoklipler, AfD’nin iktidar programının uygulamaya geçtiğinde  bakım hizmetlerinden kültüre, ekonomiden eğitime kadar gündelik hayatta yaratacağı sonuçları göstermeye çalışıyor. Kampanyanın bir etkinliğinde eyaleti dolaşacak bir otobüsteki aktivistler, yurttaşlardan “Gerçek vatan sevgisi...” cümlesini kendi sözleriyle tamamlamalarını isteyecekler.  


Kampanya bu yolla, AfD’nin uzunca zamandır tekelinde tutma gayretinde olduğu “Heimat – vatan/yurt” kavramını da siyasal mücadelenin konusu haline getiriyor. 


Ünlülerden de geniş bir cephe


Oluşan hareketlilik, bir “ünlüler kampanyası”nın ötesine taşınıyor. Alman Sendikalar Birliği DGB, “X Saksonya-Anhalt Biziz: Aktif ve dünyaya açık” kampanyasını destekliyor. Katolik Magdeburg Piskoposluğu’nun “Bilinçli oy ver” girişimi insan onuru, komşuluk ve dayanışmayı öne çıkarıyor. Kültür kurumları “Çeşitlilikten gurur duyuyoruz” kampanyası yürütüyor. Campact ise AfD’nin sandalye çoğunluğunu engellemek amacıyla SPD ve Yeşiller’in barajı geçmesini doğrudan sağlayacak "stratejik oy" çağrısı yapıyor. 


Karşı seferberliğin belki de en dinamik ayağını ünlüler değil, AfD iktidarından doğrudan etkileneceklerini düşünen göçmenler oluşturuyor. 


Saksonya-Anhalt Mülteciler Konseyi ve göçmen örgütleri 26 Ağustos’ta “ırkçılığa ve dışlanmaya karşı grev” çağrısı yaptı. Magdeburg ve diğer kentlerde göçmen kökenli esnafın 10.00-15.00 arasında dükkânlarını gönüllü olarak kapatması, ardından Eyalet Meclisi önünde miting düzenlenmesi planlanıyor. Çağrının sloganı kendisini anlatıyor: "Bugün kapılarımızı kapatıyoruz ki, yarın özgür ve demokratik toplumun kapıları kapanmasın.” 


Kaygı doğuran yalnız AfD'nin göç politikası değil


Hareketliliği güdüleyen yeni öge, AfD’nin eyalet için hazırladığı programın seçim kampanyalarında olağan sayılan sert sağ söylemin ötesine geçtiği değerlendirmesi. 


Saksonya-Anhalt Anayasayı Koruma Dairesi (Verfassungsschutz) AfD eyalet örgütünü “kesinleşmiş aşırı sağcı” olarak sınıflandırırken, AfD’nin “hükümet programı” metni özellikle kültür, eğitim, üniversiteler, kamu yayıncılığı ve siyasal eğitim alanlarında doğrudan kurumsal dönüşüm öngörüyor. Yükseköğretim Geliştirme Merkezi'nin (Centrum für Hochschulentwicklung) program üzerine yaptığı incelemeye göre AfD’nin üniversite politikası öğrenci ve çalışanların yönetime katılımını azaltmayı, araştırma ve öğretime daha fazla siyasi müdahale getirmeyi, Bologna sisteminden çıkmayı ve üniversitelerin uluslararası bağlarını zayıflatmayı hedefliyor. Kurumun görüşü, bunun bilim özgürlüğünü ve üniversite özerkliğini ciddi biçimde sınırlayacağı sonucuna varıyor.

author: Jasmine Mithani
title: She Defended Herself From Domestic Abuse. She’s on Trial for Murder Next Week.
content:
Keshia Golden’s advocates say the legal system is stacked against both Black women and survivors of domestic violence.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

Keshia Golden, a Black mother from the West Side of Chicago, turned down a plea deal months ago even though it put her at risk of at least 20 years in prison.

In October 2022, Golden was eight months pregnant and had just celebrated her baby shower. She says her boyfriend, Calvin Sidney, attacked her in the kitchen, slamming her head into the counter — her attorneys say that kind of violence was typical of their relationship, and resulted in dozens of police calls and multiple arrests. One of her public defenders said the fight moved into another room, and that’s when Golden defended herself. “I just wanted him to stop,” Golden told the Chicago Sun-Times, reflecting on the moment when she said she grabbed a kitchen knife and stabbed Sidney in the leg. The blade hit his femoral artery, and he died in a hospital. Golden was charged with first-degree murder shortly after.

Prosecutors offered her a chance to plead guilty to second-degree murder, also a felony, and avoid prison time by agreeing to probation for two years. But the cost was still too high.

With a felony on her record in Illinois, Golden would lose opportunities to get back on her feet as a survivor of domestic abuse. She would be ineligible for public housing, lose access to child care funds and be barred from working in health care, her chosen field. She wouldn’t be eligible for student loans to help her start another career. All this would hurt her ability to provide for her 3-year-old daughter, Ky’liyah, whose baby shower she had been celebrating.

Golden’s trial is scheduled to begin Monday, and as a Black woman charged with killing her abuser the odds are stacked against her. A plea deal would risk her livelihood, but a trial could result in her being separated from her child for decades. Organizers are rallying for prosecutors to drop all charges instead of what they see as a decision to punish a Black mother for trying to save her own life. The people demanding her freedom say if she had not acted, her life — and that of her daughter — would be on the line instead.

“What is a woman’s right to defend herself against her abuser? And why is her abuser entitled to harm her? Why have we normalized that?” asked Holly Krig, director of organizing at Moms United Against Violence and Incarceration, who has been advocating on Golden’s behalf.

Leigh Goodmark runs the Gender, Prison and Trauma Clinic at the University of Maryland’s law school, and specializes in supporting criminalized survivors. “What’s happening to Keisha is not all that different than what happens to many women who fight back against their abusive partners,” she told The 19th.

She said the charges and plea deal offered to Golden aren’t surprising. There are many factors stacked against survivors of domestic violence accused of murder.

Goodmark said survivors tend to tell the truth about what happened, thinking that authorities will understand the abuse they have suffered and that they acted in self-defense. But in reality, that just makes a defendant who easily confessed. Prosecutors typically only look at a single incident, not the holistic circumstances of prolonged abuse.

Sierra Bartlett’s job as a mitigation specialist is to learn about the history of clients being represented by public defenders in Cook County, which covers Chicago. When she interviewed Golden, it became clear that there had been too many prior incidents of domestic violence for her to coherently recall them all. Bartlett tracked down hospital records for Golden to get a better sense of the scope, and saw she was admitted to the emergency room when she was 18 weeks pregnant after being strangled. Strangulation can become deadly very quickly, but this wasn’t even one of the incidents Golden had remembered. It’s also a predictor of intimate partner homicide.

Three months before Sidney was killed, records viewed by The 19th show he was served a protective order mandating no contact with Golden. He allegedly punched her in the face; she was in her second trimester at the time.

The defense commissioned an outside domestic violence expert to weigh in on Golden’s experiences. Bartlett said the expert evaluated Golden over four separate meetings, and using the Danger Assessment, a tool widely used to …

title: 8 kez uzaklaştırmaya rağmen bıçaklandı: Adana'da kadınlar Ayşe Katırcı için adalet istedi
content:
Adana’nın Yüreğir ilçesinde yaşayan 52 yaşındaki üç çocuk annesi Ayşe Katırcı, yaklaşık 10 yıl önce 25 yıllık evliliğini sonlandırdığı Arif Tanrıkulu’nun boşanmanın ardından da tehdit ve şiddetine maruz kaldı. Hakkında 8 kez uzaklaştırma kararı aldıran ve KADES üzerinden ihbarlarda bulunan Katırcı, eski eşinin kendisine kefen gönderdiğini, “sana mezarlık alacağım” diyerek tehdit ettiğini, silah ve bıçakla korkuttuğunu anlattı. Buna rağmen 9-10 Ağustos’ta Tanrıkulu, Katırcı’nın evine girerek onu 8 yerinden bıçaklayıp ağır yaraladı. Olayın ardından kaçan Tanrıkulu Pozantı’da yakalanarak 11 Ağustos’ta tutuklandı. Yoğun bakımda tedavi gören Katırcı ise hayati tehlikeyi atlattı. 17 Ağustos’ta hastanede konuşan Katırcı, eski eşinin serbest bırakılması halinde kendisini öldürmesinden korktuğunu belirterek en ağır cezanın verilmesini istedi.

Yaşanan saldırının ardından Adana Kadın Platformu, kentte artan erkek şiddeti ve kadın cinayetlerine dikkat çekmek amacıyla İnönü Parkı’nda basın açıklaması yaptı. Platform adına açıklamayı Seren Canbolat okudu.

Canbolat, Ayşe Katırcı’nın yaşadıklarının ülkedeki cezasızlık politikalarının somut örneklerinden biri olduğunu belirterek, kadınların yaşamlarını sürdürebilmek için verdikleri mücadeleye rağmen yeterince korunmadığını söyledi.

Canbolat, Katırcı hakkında daha önce alınan uzaklaştırma kararlarının neden etkin biçimde uygulanmadığını sordu. Tanrıkulu’nun Katırcı’yı tehdit etmesine rağmen bugüne kadar neden tutuklanmadığını da soran Canbolat, “Kadınların uzaklaştırma kararlarını neden etkin uygulamıyorsunuz?” diye sordu.

Kadın cinayetlerinin münferit olaylar olarak değerlendirilemeyeceğini belirten Canbolat, geçtiğimiz temmuz ayında bir hafta içerisinde üç kadının birlikte oldukları erkekler tarafından öldürüldüğünü söyledi.

Kadınların yaşam hakkının korunması yerine ataerkil aile yapısını güçlendiren politikaların gündeme getirilmesini eleştiren Canbolat, kadınların ve çocukların korunması, güçlendirilmesi ve toplumsal eşitsizliğin ortadan kaldırılması için kadın odaklı politikaların uygulanması gerektiğini ifade etti.

Canbolat, yetkililerin sorumluluğunun kadınların yaşamlarına ilişkin kararlar almak değil, onları şiddetten korumak olduğunu vurgulayarak, “Bu ülkede her gün en az üç kadın öldürülürken işiniz kadınların nasıl doğum yapacağı değil, işiniz cinayet mahalli ataerkil aileleri güçlendirmek hiç değil” dedi.

Açıklamanın sonunda 6284 sayılı Kanun’un etkin uygulanması çağrısı yapan Canbolat, “Göreviniz kadınları ve çocukları korumak, güçlendirmek ve eşitsizliği ortadan kaldıracak kadın odaklı politikalar yürütmektir. Göreviniz 6284 sayılı kanunu etkin uygulamak. Göreviniz uzaklaştırma kararlarını uygulamak” ifadelerini kullandı.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: Women in Istanbul protest against sexual violence in Turkish deportation centers
content:
Following allegations of torture made by German activist Paula Maier, women in Istanbul protested against sexual violence in Turkish deportation centers, police custody and prisons. The Women Strong Together Alliance (Kadınlar Birlikte Güçlü) stated that the violence described by Maier was not an isolated incident, but part of a state practice used particularly against migrant women and politically active women.


During the protest at Tünel Square, participants carried a banner reading, “End sexual torture against women in deportation centers and police custody.” They chanted slogans including, “We will not remain silent, we are not afraid, we will not obey,” “End harassment and rape in police custody—the male-dominated state will be held accountable,” and “Jin, Jiyan, Azadî” [Woman, Life, Freedom].


The protest was prompted by the testimony of Paula Maier. The German activist and member of the Caravan for the Defense of Humanity had traveled to Turkey in January this year to take part in international solidarity work with the Democratic Autonomous Administration of North and East Syria, which at the time was under attack by the Syrian transitional government. Following her arrest, she was held in a deportation center. After returning to Germany, she publicly stated that she had been subjected to sexual violence and torture there by a male staff member.


“Deportation centers have become torture centers”


Simay Ada Kart, who read out the statement on behalf of the women’s alliance, placed the case in a broader context. She said that since their establishment, Turkey’s deportation centers had developed into places where policies targeting refugees and women intersect with racism and torture. Migrants are subjected to various forms of pressure intended to force them to leave the country or submit to deportation, she noted.


According to the alliance, sexual violence committed by state officials should not be regarded as a series of isolated abuses. The group also recalled accounts of sexual violence during detention made public by Anna, a participant in the Sumud Flotilla in solidarity with Palestine, and Alma of the Caravan for the Defense of Humanity.


“In prisons, police stations and deportation centers, strip searches, sexual harassment and sexual violence have virtually become routine practices aimed at breaking the will of women who resist and struggle, and at punishing them,” Kart said.


“Strip searches are not a procedure but torture”


Women Are Strong Together pointed to reports of abuse at various locations within Turkey’s detention and policing system—from the Istanbul Police Department on Vatan Street and Bakırköy Women’s Prison to police stations and deportation centers. Kart said that the control of and violence against women’s bodies were intended to intimidate women and deter them from political and social engagement.


Strip searches, she said, should therefore not be downplayed as an administrative “procedure”: “Strip searches are torture.”


The alliance also echoed Maier’s call not to allow the violence women have experienced to silence them. “It is the responsibility of all of us to turn these experiences into a story of resistance,” the activist had said. The organization announced that it would continue to strengthen international solidarity among women.


Who will hold those responsible accountable?


At the end of the protest, the alliance addressed a series of specific questions to the Turkish authorities and government: “Will the torture centers referred to as deportation centers be shut down? Will those responsible for harassing and raping women in prisons and police stations, as well as the state officials who turn a blind eye to such acts, be held accountable? Will acts of sexual violence in police custody and prisons be effectively investigated?”


The protest concluded with participants chanting slogans.

content:

Uruguay: new steps towards transforming access to justice in response to sexual violence

From 11 to 14 August, Equality Now, together with


CLADEM Uruguay

 and


Proyecto Ikove

, carried out

advocacy, capacity-building and institutional coordination activities to drive reforms and improve the response to sexual violence in Uruguay

, as part of


the Regional Day of Solidarity with Victims and Survivors of Sexual Violence

, which is observed every 9 August.


Uruguay has taken significant steps to prevent and respond to gender-based violence. However, for many girls, adolescents and women who are survivors of sexual violence, accessing justice continues to involve overcoming legal, institutional and geographical barriers.


The numbers highlight the scale of the challenge: approximately


one in three people under the age of 18 has experienced some form of sexual violence

, and in


seven out of ten cases of sexual violence reported to the police, the victim is a child or adolescent

.


Against this backdrop, the new alliance between Equality Now and local organisations seeks to drive legislative and institutional change to improve access to justice for victims and survivors of sexual violence in Uruguay.


A roadmap to strengthen access to justice


The week began on 11 August at the Legislative Palace with the event

‘Barriers to access to justice in cases of sexual violence’

, which brought together national authorities, female legislators from different political parties, members of the judiciary, public prosecutors, civil society organisations and survivors.


During the opening session, the Vice-President of the Republic, Carolina Cosse, expressed Parliament’s commitment to continuing to drive this agenda forward: “You can count on Parliament to promote laws that enable better access to justice.”


At the event, together with our national partners, we presented


Strengthening Access to Justice for Survivors of Sexual Violence in Uruguay

, a document that analyses the extent to which international standards have been incorporated into the country’s legislation and institutions, identifies the main challenges and proposes recommendations to move towards a more effective state response, with a focus on human rights, gender and intersectionality.


The analysis acknowledges the significant regulatory and institutional progress made in Uruguay, but also identifies structural deficits and regulatory gaps that continue to limit effective access to justice for women, girls and adolescents who are survivors of sexual violence.


As


Sofía Quiroga

, Advocacy Officer at Equality Now, explained during the opening of the event, the challenge has two closely connected dimensions: improving the implementation of existing laws and continuing to align the legal framework with international human rights standards. In this sense, the document seeks to acknowledge the progress made in Uruguay, while also encouraging discussion around the challenges that remain, including the need to ensure timely, specialised justice that is free from stereotypes and discrimination for victims and survivors of sexual violence.


Consent must be at the centre


Currently, the Uruguayan Criminal Code does not define sexual offences on the basis of the absence of consent, but rather on the basis of the use of violence or threats, or of certain circumstances in which the law presumes violence. Uruguayan legislation has already taken significant steps by establishing that silence, a lack of resistance or the victim’s sexual history cannot be interpreted as indications of consent. However, lack of consent does not yet constitute the central element of criminal classification.


Gabriela Kletzel,

Senior Legal Advisor

at Equality Now, emphasised that incorporating consent as the cornerstone of the legislation would not mean introducing a paradigm entirely foreign to the Uruguayan legal system. On the contrary, it would allow for the deepening of transformations that have already begun in other areas of the law and bring them into line with international standards.

author: Yi Ling Pan
title: Queerness, neu zensiert
content:
Die Serie „The Untamed“ zählt zu den weltweit erfolgreichsten chinesischen Serien der letzten Jahre. Trotz Zensur bleibt die Liebe zwischen den beiden männlichen Protagonisten Wei Wuxian und Lan Wangji aus der „Boys Love“-Romanvorlage spürbar.

Vor sieben Jahren klickte meine Mutter beim Mittagessen erstaunlich schnell auf „Play“. Normalerweise muss sie immer kurz überlegen, wenn ich sie als Expertin für chinesische Popkultur nach neuen Serientipps frage. Diesmal war sie sich sicher, dass „陈情令“ („Chén Qíng Lìng”), „The Untamed”, unser neues Mahlzeiten-Entertainment werden sollte. Die Serie gehe in China gerade komplett durch die Decke, erzählte sie, vor allem wegen der Beziehung zwischen den beiden Protagonisten Wei Wuxian und Lan Wangji. In einer Xianxia-Welt zwischen Altem China und Fantasy, eleganten Kostümen, Martial Arts und Dämonen, streben beide als sogenannte Kultivierende nach spiritueller Vollkommenheit. Das ungleiche Duo freundet sich an und durchsteht zusammen jahrzehntelange Clan-Kämpfe.

In der beliebten Onlineroman-Vorlage „魔道祖师“ („Mó Dào Zǔ Shī”), „Grandmaster of Demonic Cultivation”, erklärte meine Mutter, sind die beiden ein Paar. Es war also explizit eine „Danmei“-Story. 耽美 („dān měi“), wörtlich übersetzt „sich der Schönheit hingeben“, bezeichnet Boys-Love-Geschichten aus China. In Japan als Genre entstanden und in Ostasien schon lange beliebt, inspirierte es zuletzt auch zunehmend westliche Produktionen, Stichwort „Heartstopper“ und „Heated Rivalry“.

Die Drehbuchautor*innen von „The Untamed“ jedoch mussten das Skript umschreiben. Denn zu dem Zeitpunkt war LGBTQ+-Content in China schon explizit verboten. Ende 2015 wurden Darstellungen von Homosexualität aus dem Fernsehen verbannt, 2017 auch aus dem Internet. So wurden aus Wei Wuxian undLan Wangji statt Liebhaber Seelenverwandte.

Neugierig geworden, schaute ich die erste Folge. Nach nicht einmal der Hälfte brach ich ab. Mir waren die Gesichter zu weiß und makellos, die Ästhetik zu glatt, erklärte ich meiner Mutter. Sie schaute allein weiter, leicht enttäuscht. Rückblickend war das nicht mein einziger Grund. Eine queere Story, in der Queerness zensiert wird: Das konnte ja nicht gutgehen, dachte ich mir.

Erst Jahre später schaue ich alle 50 Folgen. Und beginne, mich selbst zu hinterfragen. Ob nicht mein kritisches Urteil zu voreingenommen war von einer westlichen Sozialisation; einer dogmatischen Vorstellung von Queerness, für die diktatorische Mittel wie Zensur der Tod bedeuteten.

Ich grabe mich durch Fanforen, um den Erfolg der Serie besser zu verstehen. Schon 2021 knackte die Serie zehn Milliarden Views auf dem chinesischen Streamingdienst „Tencent TV“; auf „Douban“ hält sie ein Rating von 7,7, auf „IMDb“ 8,7, und ist mittlerweile auch auf „Netflix“ ein Hit. An Chi aus Peking erzählt mir auf dem chinesischen sozialen Medium „Rednote“, dass sie noch immer mit Fans aus ganz China an Drehorten wandern gehen und den Titelsong anstimmen, sobald sie sich sehen. Und: Fans weltweit feiern die Liebesgeschichte trotz der Zensur. Oder sogar gerade deswegen. Die Kanadierin Debbiesunfish schwärmt auf „Reddit“: „Wären es einfach nur zwei Männer, die intim miteinander werden, würde mich das nicht so sehr ansprechen wie die sehnsüchtigen Blicke, die stillen Momente, in denen im Hintergrund eine Flöte spielt, während die Kamera langsam wegschwenkt.“ Sie fügt hinzu: „Ich bin queer, und für mich ist es ein Genuss, queere Liebe auf diese für mich neue, ‚zensierte‘ Art zu erleben.“

Beim Schauen merke ich, wie ich selbst immer mehr in die Liebesgeschichte hineingesogen werde. Die Spannung zwischen beiden Männern ist von Anfang an angelegt, da sie absolut gegensätzlich scheinen: Wei Wuxian als sorgloser Regelbrecher, Lan Wangji hingegen als eine Art wandelndes Regelwerk, der, wenn er redet, meistens Wei Wuxian ermahnt. Dass Wei Wuxian schließlich den dämonischen statt des rechtschaffenen Pfades der Kultivierung wählt, dem hell gekleideten Lan Wangji fortan in Schwarz begegnet, vergrößert diese Spannung nur noch. Trotzdem wartet Lan Wangji sechzehn Jahre lang auf den gestorbenen Freund, was für viele Fans die Romantik der Serie ausmacht. So schreibt Drama_Llama auf dem Blog „The BL Xpress“: „Anstatt der Beziehung etwas zu nehmen, verleiht ihr die Zensur eine nuancierte Komplexität, die sich intimer anfühlte als tatsächliche körperliche Intimität. author: Bulatlat Contributors
title: Balik-Tanaw | When women rise, God’s mercy breaks in the boundaries
content:
By Klein Fausto Emperado Iglesia Filipina Independiente/Aglipay Central Theological Seminary

Isaiah 56:1, 6-7 Psalm 67:2-3, 5, 6, 8 Romans 11:13-15, 29-32 Matthew 15:21-28

The Canaanite woman came to Jesus carrying the suffering of her daughter. She cried, persisted, and refused to be silenced. Yet the disciples wanted her sent away. Her voice was treated as a disturbance. Her struggle was seen as someone else’s problem.

Women continue to face discrimination, violence, abuse, and the denial of their dignity. Patriarchy has become so deeply woven into our society and even our churches, that it is sometimes treated as normal. We silence women, question their leadership, and even deny their calling. Sometimes, women themselves become bearers of patriarchy and misogyny.

Yet the Canaanite woman would not leave.

Her persistence challenges a Church that is tempted to silence those who disturb our comfort. Her cry echoes in the voices of mothers, wives, and sisters of victims of the so-called drug war who continue to demand justice despite threats and harassment. It echoes in the courageous voice of an Aeta woman chieftain who stood before an inquiry on the proposed US-led Pax Silica, declaring that her people will not surrender their ancestral land, the land that sustains their life, culture, and future.

These are not merely voices of protest. They are voices of life.

The late Muriel Orevillo-Montenegro, a pioneer Asian theologian and author of “The Jesus of Asian Women” reminds us to encounter a Jesus understood through the lived struggles of the women of the Philippines and Asia, a Christ who accompanies people in their struggle against poverty, patriarchy, discrimination, and oppression, and who seeks life to flourish.

This is the Jesus we meet in the Canaanite woman’s struggle.

Isaiah declares that God’s house is for all peoples.

Psalm 67 proclaims God’s blessing among all nations.

Romans remind us that God’s mercy embraces all. The Gospel reveals that God’s mercy cannot be imprisoned

by boundaries created by human beings.

So where does the Church stand?

We cannot proclaim God’s inclusive mercy while silencing those who cry for justice.

We are called to journey with women, listen to the marginalized, amplify their voices,

defend their dignity, and stand with communities resisting oppression.

The Church must not become another instrument of empire, patriarchy, or exclusion.

When women rise and speak for healing and justice , the Church must listen. When the oppressed cry, the Church must stand. When people struggle for life, the Church must struggle with them.

This is the way of Christ: to serve the people, to seek justice,

and to make God’s liberating mercy visible in the world.

Let us join our voices in this prayer:

Pray with Me for a World of Mercy

Pray with me for a world where no one is turned away, where every table has room for the poor , and every person knows the abundance of God’s blessing.

Pray with me for the courage of the Canaanite woman, who would not be silenced, whose cry for mercy crossed every boundary and opened the way to healing.

Pray with me for those whose voices are drowned by power for women seeking justice, for Indigenous peoples defending their land, for the poor and oppressed whose dignity is denied.

Pray with me for a Church that listens, that welcomes, that stands with those at the margins, and refuses to send them away.

May our prayers become courage, our courage become solidarity, and our solidarity becomes action.

May God’s mercy reach every people, until justice flows freely and no one is left behind. Siya Nawa!

Balik-Tanaw is a group blog of Promotion of Church People’s Response. The Lectionary Gospel reflection is an invitation for meditation, contemplation, and action. As we nurture our faith by committing ourselves to journey with the people, we also wish to nourish the perspective coming from the point of view of hope and struggle of the people. It is our constant longing that even as crisis intensifies, the faithful will continue to strengthen their commitment to love God and our neighbor by being one with the people in their dreams and aspirations. The Title of the Lectionary Reflection would be Balik –Tanaw , isang PAGNINILAY . It is about looking back (balik) or revisiting the narratives and stories from the Biblical text and seeing, reading, and reflecting on these with the current context (tanaw).

title: Asuman Bayrak’la son romanı üzerine: Yaşıyorsak yazalım bari
content:
Hüzün. Her kitap bittiğinde hüzünleniyorum. Uzun süre birlikte yaşadığım, her şeyi paylaştığım kahramanlarımdan ayrılmak, kelimenin tam anlamıyla hüzünlendiriyor. Umarım kitabın yolu açık olur.


Asuman Bayrak, Çarşambanın Kötüsü romanıyla ilgili “hüzün” derken kitaplarının okurla buluşmasından önceki son durağındaki hissini paylaşıyor. Romana veda kahramanlarının hayata karışması, bizlerle buluşmasının heyecanını yaşamak olsa gerek. Veda hem gitmek hem de gidememek değil mi? Hem gönüllülük hem de gönülsüzlük. Roman için bir yandan bitirmek, bir yandan da yeni bir başlangıç galiba.


Bayrak ilk kitabı “Kayıp Taşlar”da Habil'le Kabil'in kız kardeşleri Aklima ile Lebuda'nın hikayesini anlattı. Devamla “Eğrelti Otları Şarkı Söyler Mi?” anneler ve kızları hakkında. “Yalnız Kadın Cinayetleri” polisiye bir çalışmayla karşımıza çıktı. Şimdi de Çarşambanın Kötüsü.


Aynı zamanda 

bianet’

te

, kitaplarla, sinemayla, geçmiş ve gelecekte dolaşarak yazılar yazıyor. Şanslıyız, teşekkürlerle.


Çarşambanın Kötüsü üzerine, önceki romanlarında uğrayarak birkaç soru sorduk Bayrak’a.


"Bu memlekette gazetecilik yapamayacağımı anlayınca edebiyat dünyasına daldım"


Gerçekle kurgunun iç içe geçtiği bir üslupla yazıyorsun. Yazdıklarının hangisi gerçek, hangisi kurgu?


Edebiyat hayattan doğmalı ve hayatın içinde dolaşmalı bence. Yazarken gerçeklerden kopamıyorum. Bir önceki kitabım Yalnız Kadın Cinayetleri’nde, 1997 yılında geçen olayları anlatmıştım. O kitabım epey farklıydı.


Bu kez, özel olan politiktir, diyerek yola çıkıp bir fotoğraf çekmek istedim. Geçmişi deşip kurcaladım, bende kalanları ortaya döktüm. Arşiv taradım. Eski notlarımı düzenledim.


2007 Nisan’ında üç günü yazdım. Kadın dergisi çalışanlarından pazarda tezgah kuranlara, belgesel film yönetmeninden, dört duvar arasında yaşamak zorunda kalanlara hayat hikayeleri derledim.


Bir kadının boğazı kesilerek öldürülmesinin yanı sıra Hrant Dink, Önder Babat, Zirve Yayınevi katliamı gibi siyasi cinayetleri ele alırken devletin rolüne, güçlülerin ayak oyunlarına dikkat çekiyorsun. Çarşambanın Kötüsü daha politik bir roman...


Evet. Siyasi cinayetlerin yanı sıra, memleket devasa bir kadın mezbahası. Barajlarda, yol kenarlarında kadın cesetleri bulunuyor, ya da ceset asla bulunmuyor, bazıları kimsesizler mezarlığına gömülüyor, bazıları teneke bidonlarda yakılıp yok edilmeye çalışılıyor.


Neler olup bittiğini genellikle adliye ve polis muhabirleri biliyor, en tepeden en aşağıya suç örgütlerini, suçları, çürümeyi onlar görüyor, gösteriyor. Neticede ben de eski gazeteciyim. Kayıtsız kalamazdım. Şiddet ve cinayetler üzerine yazmak istedim.


On, on beş yıl gazetecilik yaptıktan sonra, her şeyi bırakıp Urla’da köyüne çekildin.


Yalnızlığı seviyorum. Yazan biri için yalnızlık şans. Kelimeler ise dostum, düşmanım; onlarsız yapamam. Ursula Le Guin “biz kelimeci bir türüz” der. Kelimeler insanı büyüler, başka diyarlara götürür; ancak, onların gizemine, güzelliğine saplanıp kalmamaya çalışıyor, ayağımı toprağa, hayata basmak istiyorum, o yüzden de yaşadıklarımı, hayatın bende bıraktığı izleri takip ediyorum.


Gazeteciliğe başlayınca ilk şefim Cemal Süreya’ydı. Yazdıklarımı önce onun okuması ve eleştirmesi şansım oldu. Yazıp yazıp silmeyi öğrendim. Bu memlekette gazetecilik yapamayacağımı anlayınca edebiyat dünyasına daldım. Roman yazmaya başladım. Başucu kitaplarım oldu. Bilge Karasu’yla yaşarken tanışamadığım için hayıflandım. Yazının olmazsa olmaz dinamiklerini onun kitaplarında keşfettim. Brezilya’dan bir dost buldum: Clarice Lispector.


"Kendi romanlarım üzerine konuşmakta zorlanıyorum"


Brezilya edebiyatının yıldızı. Edebiyatta devrim yaptığından bahsediliyor.


Doğru. Kural dışı/sıra dışı metinler yazan bir kadın. Büyüleyici, hatta büyücü. Sanki kelimeleri iğne oyası gibi işliyor. Tül gibi, arka tarafı/içeriyi net göstermiyor, sezdiriyor. Zaman zaman sert; mekik oyası gibi. Dik duruyor. Batıyor, çıkıyor. Tavizsiz. “Sözüm sana” diyor. Karşımda oturduğunu hissediyorum.


Senin yazdıklarına gelirsek...


Kendi romanlarım üzerine konuşmakta zorlanıyorum. Onlar orada, kitapçı raflarında, yani beni terk ettiler. Terk etmek doğru tanım olmadı. Ben onları yolcu ettim. Uzunca bir süre birlikte yaşadık. Yazdığım herkes, yazdığım sürece sabah akşam yirmi dört saat benimle birlikte olur.


Aynı evde yaşarız. Onlarla bazen kavga ederim. Bazen şaşırtırlar, istemediğim yollara girer, beni zor durumda bırakırlar. Derken maceramız biter ve ben haydi “güle güle” derim.

and my take today is that framing misogynistic writing as an “inability to write female characters” subconsciously takes away most of the blame, implying that women are an alien creature compared to men and that it is no fault of the writer because it’s out of their skill set. it’s not an inability, not a lack of expertise, it’s the simple refusal to consider women as individual people and give them the same depth and grace that comes easily to the writer when they write male characters. it’s not that christopher nolan, stephen king, james cameron (and frankly anyone using the argument, both professional and hobbyist; yes, that includes fanfic writers) etc can’t write women, it’s that they just won’t. at that point in time it is a conscious decision driven by the laziness to unpack their misogynistic biases, and should be addressed as such

author: Mosha Folger
title: Sanirajak man sentenced to four and a half years for sex crimes
content:
After a series of delays, Simeonie Issigaitok has received a four-and-a-half year sentence in a federal penitentiary for sexually touching children under the age of 16.


Court staff brought the 73-year-old Sanirajak man from into an Iqaluit courtroom Tuesday in a wheelchair. Through an interpreter, he listened expressionless, occasionally nodding his head, as Justice Christian Lyons read his sentence.


“Vulnerability of Inuit children and, in particular Inuit girls, is demonstrated by the persistent and troublingly high per capita rate of child sexual abuse in Nunavut,” Lyons said. “A problem that Mr. Issigaitok has repeatedly and substantially contributed to for decades.”


Issigaitok pleaded guilty in December 2025 to two counts of sexual interference. The first offence occurred in Sanirajak sometime between 1987 and 1989. Issigaitok assaulted a girl in her early teens at her home while her parents were asleep.


The second incident occurred in April 2021. Issigaitok was captured on security video during a community event touching a boy while he was seated with a group of children.


On Tuesday, Lyons said aggravating factors included Issigaitok’s history of convictions for sex crimes dating back to  which dates back to 1988, his 2014 designation as a dangerous offender, and that his victims were Inuit children.


He also said that he considered the fact that Issigaitok attended residential school, where he was sexually abused, a mitigating factor, as well as Issigaitok’s guilty plea, which meant the victims did not have to testify.


Another mitigating factor was that one of the crimes occurred before the first of his 27 lifetime convictions. Therefore, the court could treat it as a first offense.


“This is attenuated somewhat by the fact that Mr. Issigaitok was abusing other children during the period of the offense and had committed a serious sexual assault a few years prior, for which he was sentenced in 1997,” Lyons said.


Crown prosecutors had sought a 10-year sentence, while defence lawyer Alan Regel argued that his sentence should be for time served in jail while his case worked its way through the legal system. Judges usually credit defendants with one and a half days for every day they spend in pre-trial custody. That means Regal was asking for a sentence of about 21 months.


Lyons sentenced Issigaitok to three years for the crime committed in 1988 and one and a half years for the crime committed in 2021.


Issigaitok will remain at the Aaqqigiarvik Correctional Healing Facility in Iqaluit while he awaits his transfer to a federal penitentiary to serve the two years and nine months left in his sentence.


The sentencing saw two delays. In June, Lyons

delayed the proceeding

 to allow time for one victim to submit a statement. In July, Issigaitok was medevaced to Ottawa because of respiratory problems.


There was one more delay, of about an hour, on Tuesday. The scheduled court interpreter was not in town, and court staff needed to videoconference a new one.

author: Giovanna DeStefanis
title: Idaho Abortion Ban Blocked When Pregnancy Threatens Patient’s Health
content:
On August 13, 2026, a federal district court ruled in Idaho that the 14th Amendment protects the right to abortion when a pregnant person’s life or health is seriously threatened, blocking Idaho from enforcing its abortion bans in those circumstances.

The ruling invalidates two Idaho laws to the extent that they prohibit doctors from providing abortion care to patients facing serious medical conditions, including mental health conditions that put them at risk of suicide or overdose.

Following a six-day trial in June, the court determined that abortion care to prevent serious and lasting harm to a pregnant person’s health is deeply rooted in American history and tradition. The decision is the first federal court ruling since the overturning of Roe in 2022 to recognize that the federal Constitution continues to protect abortion access in certain circumstances.

The case was brought by the Lawyering Project and Legal Voice on behalf of Dr. Stacy Seyb, an Idaho maternal-fetal medicine specialist who argues that the state’s abortion bans prevented him from providing necessary care to patients.

The court’s ruling is particularly significant for patients experiencing serious mental health conditions. Idaho’s abortion bans previously prohibited abortion even when a pregnancy places a patient at risk of death from self-harm.

According to Idaho’s Maternal Mortality Review Committee, mental health conditions were the most common underlying cause of pregnancy-related death in the state between 2018 and 2024.

While this is a win, it’s important to note that the ruling does not establish a broader constitutional right to abortion. The court declined to block Idaho’s abortion bans when a fetus has a life-threatening condition unless the condition also poses a serious threat to the pregnant person’s health.

The decision comes as Idaho voters prepare to consider Proposition 1 or the “Reproductive Freedom and Privacy Act Initiative” in November. This would establish a broader right to reproductive freedom, including access to abortion before fetal viability. Proposition 1 would go into effect on and after January 1, 2027.

This ruling is an important step toward protecting pregnant people from the devastating consequences of abortion bans. No one should be forced to carry a pregnancy that places their life or health in serious danger, and no doctor should face criminal punishment for providing medically necessary care. Pregnancy people must be able to make decisions about their own bodies and health without government interference.

If you are an Idaho resident, make sure you are registered to vote to make your voice heard on Proposition 1 this November!

author: Jeremy Kohler
title: Missouri GOP Attempts to Restore Abortion Ban With Anti-Trans Ballot Initiative
content:
Critics say the measure deploys misleading language while folding in restrictions on gender transition care for minors.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

Two years ago, abortion opponents in Missouri tried to defeat Amendment 3, a ballot initiative to enshrine reproductive rights in the state constitution, by falsely telling voters that it would allow gender transition surgeries for minors — even though it wouldn’t.

Voters approved Amendment 3 anyway, overturning the near-total abortion ban enacted by Missouri’s GOP-dominated legislature that had taken effect after the U.S. Supreme Court struck down Roe v. Wade in 2022.

Now Republican leaders in the state are trying to repeal those rights again, using the same issue. They placed a new amendment on the November ballot, also called Amendment 3, that would restore Missouri’s abortion ban while allowing limited exceptions but also constitutionally prohibit gender transition care for minors — though the state has banned surgeries and new prescriptions of puberty blockers and hormones by law since August 2023.

For the Missouri GOP, Election Day can often seem like Groundhog Day. The party holds a supermajority in the legislature and controls every statewide office, yet voters have repeatedly used the initiative petition process to enact policies Republican leaders oppose. By gathering enough signatures, citizens have placed proposals directly on the ballot, then persuaded voters to expand Medicaid, legalize marijuana, raise the minimum wage and restore abortion rights.

This month, that disconnect became an electoral humiliation for Republican leaders. More than 80% of voters rejected their attempt to make it nearly impossible for citizens to amend the state constitution. It was even worse for Gov. Mike Kehoe’s plan to phase out the state income tax: More than 83% voted no.

Missouri Republicans have become “drunk with power,” said Ken Warren, a professor emeritus of political science at Saint Louis University and associate director of the SLU/YouGov Poll. “Because they control everything, they think they can do what they want — and they can’t.”

The new Amendment 3 on the November ballot shows how Republicans, using misleading language, a carefully chosen distraction and even a recycled name, are trying to undo one of those defeats. In 2024, a yes vote on Amendment 3 protected abortion rights. In November, voters will again be asked to vote yes on Amendment 3 — this time to take them away.

Republican leaders say voters never intended to approve a nearly unlimited right to abortion. They argue that Missourians would prefer an abortion ban with limited exceptions for rape, incest, medical emergencies and fetal anomalies — particularly when it is paired with restrictions on gender transition care for minors.

It would not take much to reverse the 2024 result. Abortion rights passed 51.6% to 48.4% — meaning a shift of about 48,000 voters would have defeated the measure.

Critics call the inclusion of gender care “ballot candy,” a way to make an unpopular proposal easier to swallow. They say the tactic is especially cynical because it promises voters a prohibition that, in large part, Missouri already has. State law already bans gender transition surgery for minors and, through August 2027, bars minors from starting puberty blockers or cross-sex hormones for gender transition. Amendment 3 would place the restrictions in the state constitution without an expiration date.

The two provisions bundled together differ enormously in scope. Repealing reproductive rights would affect the healthcare options available to a state with about 6.3 million people. The restrictions on gender transition care concern a small number of minors receiving highly specialized treatment.

Yet supporters want voters focused on the specter of children being used as lab guinea pigs, not the abortion rights the amendment would repeal. A new billboard in the St. Louis suburbs urges them to vote yes and “ban transgender surgeries for minors.”

A website for the political action committee behind the campaign, Her Health, Her Future — whose treasurer is Missouri first lady Claudia Kehoe — declares “OUR CHILDREN are not LAB EXPERIMENTS.” It says Amendment 3 would protect children from “harmful, sterilizing medical procedures” and restore “common sense health and safety standards” for women’s health clinics.

author: TGEU
title: The rise of binary laws and their impact on trans communities in Europe and Central Asia
content:
Across Europe and Central Asia, governments are increasingly introducing laws and policies that reinforce a strict gender binary, restricting the rights, healthcare and public lives of trans and gender diverse people.  


These developments are not isolated. Across very different political contexts, governments are adopting increasingly similar legal approaches, often justified through claims about protecting ‘children’, ‘women and families’, ‘national security’ and ‘traditional values’.


TGEU’s recent policy brief analyses this growing trend, asks how these policies are connected, and what they mean for trans communities and democracy more broadly.


get the policy brief


Why is this happening? 


The expansion of these policies is taking place alongside the growing influence of anti-gender, conservative and nationalist movements across the region. Political developments in the United States, the United Kingdom, and Russia have helped to strengthen these actors and contributed to the circulation of similar narratives and legal models across Europe and Central Asia.


Different countries, the same legal playbook


From Hungary and Bulgaria to Slovakia, Georgia, Kyrgyzstan, Belarus and Türkiye, governments are introducing measures such as:


Defining sex strictly as male and female, based on biological characteristics


Eliminating or restricting legal gender recognition


Criminalising or banning trans-specific healthcare


Limiting rights related to family life, including marriage, parenting, and adoption


Introducing ‘anti-propaganda’ laws targeting gender diversity, sexuality, and bodily autonomy


Criminalising or restricting discussion of gender diversity


While the details differ between countries, the direction is increasingly similar: narrowing the space in law and society for people who do not fit a rigid gender binary.


For trans and gender diverse people, the consequences are exclusion from public life, forced disclosure of gender identity, greater risk of violence and shrinking spaces for trans communities. It also affects intersex people, families, and society by entrenching harmful legal and medical binaries.


get the policy brief


A warning sign for democracy


Binary laws are about more than technical legal issues. They are part of a wider process of democratic backsliding. Attacks on trans rights go hand in hand with restrictions on civic space, growing pressure on civil society, attacks on human rights defenders and efforts to weaken democratic participation and the rule of law.


This makes the rise of binary gender policies a concern not only for trans and gender diverse people, but for anyone working to protect human rights, democracy and open civic space.


Button: get the policy brief


TGEU’s position


TGEU calls on governments, institutions, and allies to:


Recognise binary gender laws as part of broader democratic backsliding


Respond early to the spread of exclusionary legal models


Ensure sustained, flexible funding for trans-led organisations


Defend legal gender recognition based on self-determination


Strengthen protection mechanisms for trans people and human rights defenders


The spread of binary gender policies is not inevitable. Understanding how these laws emerge, how they travel across borders and how they connect to wider attacks on democracy is essential to challenging them.

Your support makes change possible


We work across Europe and Central Asia to advance trans rights, build strong communities, and drive change through research, advocacy, and community-building.


Your donation helps us continue this vital work — defending trans lives, amplifying trans voices, and advocating for justice every day.

author: anred
title: Argentina adhirió al Consenso de Ginebra: organizaciones feministas denuncian un retroceso en derechos
content:
La decisión del Gobierno nacional formalizó esta semana el ingreso de Argentina al Consenso de Ginebra, una declaración política internacional impulsada por sectores conservadores. Organizaciones feministas y transfeministas cuestionaron la medida y advirtieron que, aunque no modifica la legislación vigente, expresa un alineamiento político que amenaza el acceso a los derechos sexuales y reproductivos.

Por ANRed

 


El Gobierno nacional formalizó esta semana la adhesión de Argentina al Consenso de Ginebra sobre Salud de la Mujer y Fortalecimiento de la Familia, una declaración política promovida durante la administración de

Donald Trump

 y respaldada por gobiernos y sectores conservadores a nivel internacional.


La incorporación argentina generó el rechazo de organizaciones feministas y transfeministas, que señalaron que la decisión constituye un posicionamiento político e ideológico contrario a la ampliación de derechos sexuales y reproductivos.


La adhesión, por sí misma, no modifica la legislación argentina vigente.

En el país, el aborto es legal desde 2020 a partir de la sanción de la Ley 27.610 de Acceso a la Interrupción Voluntaria del Embarazo, que continúa vigente en todo el territorio nacional.


Sin embargo, las organizaciones cuestionan que el Poder Ejecutivo adhiera a un instrumento internacional que promueve posiciones restrictivas mientras, al mismo tiempo, denuncian obstáculos para el acceso efectivo a las prestaciones previstas por la legislación nacional.


Una definición política


Desde la

Campaña Nacional por el derecho al aborto legal seguro y gratuito

, repudiaron la medida sostienen que la adhesión no puede ser interpretada únicamente como una declaración diplomática. Señalan que representa un alineamiento del Gobierno de Javier Milei con una coalición internacional de derecha que impulsa una agenda restrictiva en materia de derechos sexuales y reproductivos.


En ese sentido, advierten que una declaración política internacional no puede colocarse por encima de las leyes nacionales ni ser utilizada para limitar derechos reconocidos por el Congreso.


También cuestionan las políticas implementadas durante la actual gestión en materia de salud sexual y reproductiva, entre ellas el desfinanciamiento del Programa Nacional de Salud Sexual y Reproductiva y la desarticulación del programa Remediar, medidas que —según denuncian— afectan las condiciones materiales para garantizar el acceso a métodos anticonceptivos y otras prestaciones de salud.


El principio de no regresividad


El rechazo también incorpora una dimensión jurídica. Las organizaciones recuerdan que Argentina asumió obligaciones internacionales en materia de derechos humanos a través de tratados como la Convención sobre la Eliminación de Todas las Formas de Discriminación contra la Mujer (CEDAW) y el Pacto Internacional de Derechos Económicos, Sociales y Culturales (PIDESC).


En este marco, sostienen que los principios de progresividad y no regresividad obligan al Estado a evitar medidas deliberadas que impliquen retrocesos en derechos ya reconocidos y garantizados.


Por eso, consideran que la adhesión al Consenso de Ginebra no puede implicar un desconocimiento de la Ley 27.610 ni habilitar restricciones en el acceso a la interrupción voluntaria del embarazo.


El antecedente de la OMS


La incorporación al Consenso de Ginebra se suma a otras decisiones de política exterior y sanitaria cuestionadas por organizaciones sociales. En marzo de este año, el Gobierno nacional oficializó la salida de Argentina de la Organización Mundial de la Salud (OMS), decisión que fue criticada por sectores vinculados a la salud pública y organizaciones sociales.


Para las organizaciones feministas, ambas decisiones forman parte de una política de alineamiento internacional con gobiernos y sectores conservadores que buscan disputar los avances alcanzados en materia de derechos humanos.


Frente a este escenario, reiteraron que el aborto continúa siendo legal en Argentina y reclamaron al Estado nacional que garantice el acceso efectivo a los derechos establecidos por la Ley 27.610.


Ante dudas o barreras para acceder a una interrupción voluntaria del embarazo, se encuentra disponible la línea gratuita 0800-222-3444. También brindan acompañamiento la Red de Profesionales de la Salud por el Derecho a Decidir y Socorristas en Red.

Operasyonên Lûtkeya NATOyê: Yildiz Tar, Emel Memiş û xwebexşên TEMAyê serbest bûn


22 Tîrmeh 2026


Di çarçoveya heman operasyonê de Derhênerê Weşana Giştî yê Kaos GLyê Yildiz Tar jî hat desteserkirin û piştre hat girtin. Di dema îfadeyê de têkildarî NATOyê tişt ji Tarê nepirsîbûn lêbelê parvekirina wê ya hevpeyvîneke ku polîtîkayên "Sala Malbatê" yên desthilatdariyê rexne dike, jê pirsîn.
