Di operasyonên ku di 23ê Hezîranê de dest pê kirin de ji bo 241 kesan ku biryara desteserkirinê hatibû dayîn û  ji wan 225 kes hatin desteserkirin û 178 kes jî hatin girtin.

author: By Niko Georgiades, Unicorn Riot
title: DJ-U: Creating a Network of Non-Binary People of Color
content:
Minneapolis, MN — Inside Wax World, Rosa Garcia’s South Minneapolis record store, the DJ known as Madre Rosa reflects on DJ-U, a program built from turntables, community, and care. After losing its funding, the free program that trained more than 100 non-binary artists of color may be coming to an end.


Unicorn Riot spoke with Garcia and DJ-U alum Makeda at Wax World about the program’s history, its impact and what could be lost if it ends. See our short

video special

 below with a

20-minute version

 underneath and shorts on

Garcia’s benefit-events

 and

messaging from visiting DJs

 further down in the article.


Piloted in 2016 at the queer underground space Madame of the Arts, and officially started in 2018, Garcia described DJ-U as a “reparations program” created to “repair that bridge that somewhere had gotten broken.”


DJ-U has been

outlined

 as a “skill-sharing/support community for Black/Indigenous women, queer, femme, and non-binary people of color.” The program’s mission is “to create a network of aspiring and experienced self-identified femme, non-binary people of color that have a shared passion for music and community.”


Through the program, artists are supported and empowered by mentors while being given access to DJ equipment, instructions, and connections to local venues and institutions “to ensure success and long term impact.”


With grant funding, DJ-U has been offered as a free program. The money from the grants goes straight to the DJs who are paid for teaching classes. Garcia said she’s “trying to continue to keep the dollars flowing in our community. If I’m going to get a grant, I want to help us build money, shared power, community, space.”


“We spread $100K pretty much during our ten years with this group of people,” said Garcia, “and it is meant to continue to generate in the DJ scene and rotate through this community.” She says that DJ-U has succeeded in changing the musical landscape of the Twin Cities with its DJ economy and promoting and connecting artists of color.


“There are hundreds of people every weekend that are hearing music that might have been touched by this program.”


Rosa Garcia (DJ Madre Rosa)


Recalling her experience eight years ago in DJ-U’s first program after its pilot, Makeda said the biggest gift from the program was being around “such cool and creative” people like fellow DJ-U alums

Yonci Jameson

 and

Dua Saleh

, and meeting “ambitious Black women and Black queer people my age.” “The ambition,” she says, is “the hardest thing to come by.”


She’s still connected to the mentors and other alum. “There’s been so many cool-ass people that I was able to share space with and learn from,” Makeda said. “It’s really nice to be surrounded with people that you want to be like, or you’re happy to be like.”


It’s not been an easy decade for DJ-U, however, as the program has borne the brunt of some traumatic tribulations in south Minneapolis over the last decade, including multiple building fires.


In 2018, DJ-U programming happened in a studio space with Garcia,

Ms. Lakesha

 and other artists in the Roberts Shoes building on Chicago Ave. and Lake St. before the building burned down — a

huge loss

 to the Minneapolis arts community. This forced the program to relocate.


In 2020, DJ-U was being held in a large 5,000 sq. foot room in the Ivy Building and then came the Coronavirus pandemic. In-person programming was suspended and just a few months later in late May, the building was set aflame from falling ashes during fires from the

George Floyd Uprising

.


This time their equipment wasn’t totaled but everything needed to be dried out after the sprinkler system in the building doused everything in the rooms.


In 2026, effectively their tenth year, DJ-U was impacted by the U.S. government’s deadly

Operation Metro Surge

 and has additionally lost its funding. However, Garcia said that “if folks would like to

donate to the program

, well maybe we could” have another year of programming.


On 36th Ave. and Lake St. in south Minneapolis, Garcia’s record store Wax World, was deeply impacted by the federal occupation. She was forced to close her store for three weeks.


Despite facing the hardships, Garcia still holds Open Decks, allowing for DJs to come in and DJ at her store and she still lends out and gives away equipment.

author: Dominic Gutoman
title: Trans killings prompt call for investigation, policy review
content:
Gabriela Women's Party Rep. Sarah Jane Elago together with representative from various LGBTQIA+ groups pose for a group photo after they filed a resolution at the House of Representatives on August 13, 2026. Photo from Gabriela Women's Party

“It is imperative that those responsible for these violent acts be held accountable to end the culture of impunity.”

The Makabayan bloc on August 13 filed House Resolution No. (HRN) 1369 urging the House Committee on Women and Gender Equality to conduct an investigation and review of existing policies after a series of trans killings from June to August.

The most recent case was the killing of Jang Caes Macawili, a trans woman who was shot multiple times at an internet cafe in Cebu City on August 10.

“[T]his pattern of violence, constitutes a severe violation of the right to life and security of person, and underscores the urgent need for legislative action to address hate crimes, strengthen protective mechanisms, and dismantle systemic discrimination that fuels such violence,” the resolution stated.

On June 20, trans woman Bella Lutap, 20, was found dead in an irrigation canal in Sitio Burnao, Zaragoza after being reported missing for three days.

The Nueva Ecija police identified her ex-boyfriend as the primary suspect. He was arrested and charged with murder.

Read: Justice sought for trans woman killed in Nueva Ecija

On July 15, Teddy Federico, a trans woman, indigenous youth leader, and a barangay agricultural worker was found dead eight days after being reported missing.

The investigation into her death is still ongoing. The Sangguniang Bayan Veruela adopted Resolution No. 346, urging the Philippine National Police (PNP) Veruela to expedite the investigation and submit a progress report to the council.

On July 28, Betty Benito, a trans woman from Malaybalay City, Bukidnon, was reported dead in a dense forest. She was found by the police and community members. The primary suspect in her killing has been arrested.

The resolution took note of the spate of trans killings in recent years, including the cases of Shalani Dolina, Kierra Apostol, Ren Tampus, Ali Macalintal, and Ebeng Mayor. It also reiterated the 2025 statement of the Commission on Human Rights (CHR) that flagged the spate of trans killings as “transfemicide”— gender-based killing driven by transphobia, misogyny, or systemic hatred.

Read: Recent killings of trans women prompt groups to push for LGBTQIA protection

“It is imperative that those responsible for these violent acts be held accountable to end the culture of impunity surrounding violence against marginalized communities,” the CHR statement read.

It urged the legislators and the administration for the passage of the Sexual Orientation, Gender Identity, Gender Expression, or Sex Characteristics (SOGIESC) Equality Bill and the Comprehensive Anti-Discrimination Bill (CADB). It also demanded proper investigation from the law enforcement agencies.

Bulatlat asked the Philippine National Police (PNP) for the 10-year data of victims of homicide and murder, stratified by gender identity, including transgender people. The agency has yet to respond to the request.

Gender rights groups ASEAN SOGIE Caucus, STRAP, Bahaghari, Pioneer Filipino Trans Men Movement, Transmasculine Philippines, and Relentlessly Chase welcome the filing of the resolution. “We hope this process will provide space for meaningful dialogue, evidence-based discussion, and the perspectives of transgender communities, families of victims, civil society organizations, and other stakeholders,” the groups said.

They stressed that for the resolution to have meaningful impact, investigation must proceed promptly and transparently while involving the transgender communities and victims families to legislative, policy, and institutional change.

The SOGIESC Equality Bill and CADB are proposed legislative measures that seek to prohibit and penalize systemic discrimination against marginalized groups, including transgender individuals.

“Every life lost proves how this violence extends beyond the individual. Behind every case is a loved one being mourned, a family desperately seeking justice, and a community simultaneously living in fear under a system that fails to protect its constituents,” the groups said. (AMU, DAA)

author: Nahuel Lag
title: Dolavon Produce: una experiencia agroecológica en el Valle Inferior de Chubut
content:
Por Mauricio Amaya


En Dolavon, las heladas marcan el calendario de quienes trabajan la tierra y cada cultivo requiere paciencia. Mientras buena parte del Valle Inferior del Río Chubut espera la llegada de la primavera, Rosa Ranguileo recorre el invernáculo donde cultiva verduras junto a su hijo. Allí, entre hileras de lechuga, espinaca, rúcula, acelga y hierbas aromáticas, sostienen un proyecto que hace apenas unos años parecía impensado: producir alimentos agroecológicos para la comunidad.


Hace tres años, una convocatoria de la Municipalidad de Dolavon cambiaba la rutina de un grupo de familias de esta localidad del departamento de Gaiman. Hasta ese momento,

Rosa Ranguileo apenas hacía plantines con su hijo en su casa y tenían una huerta en el patio; de repente pasaba a tener un campo para cultivar.

"En verano se vende mucho más porque también sembramos mucho más. Además del invernáculo, tenemos dos parcelas", cuenta Rosa, que es parte del

 proyecto Dolavon Produce

 o el Nodo Productivo, como lo llaman en este pueblo de casi 4.000 habitantes.  


“Comer sano cambió nuestra alimentación y la de la comunidad. Ese sabor de las verduras es inigualable y además sabemos que lo producimos con nuestras propias manos. Y la gente ve nuestro trabajo”, sintetiza. 

 El proyecto tomó forma en 2023 como parte del

Programa de Infraestructura para Entramados Productivos Regionales,

 articulado por el Ministerio de Obras Públicas de la Nación. El de Dolavon es uno de los 12 nodos que se proyectaron en todo el país. Un año después, con la llegada de Javier Milei a la Casa Rosada, la iniciativa se desfinanció y la responsabilidad quedó enteramente en manos del municipio, que recibió el apoyo de la Federación de Asociación Mutualistas de Chubut (FAMUCH) para sostenerlo. 


Foto: Dolavón Produce / Nodo Productivo


De recuperar la tierra a construir comunidad 


El ingeniero agrónomo Luis Ñancucheo es uno de los pilares de Dolavon Produce.

 Las dos hectáreas y media donde funciona el Nodo eran terrenos municipales degradados, que no tenían antecedentes productivos. Recuperarlas fue uno de los primeros desafíos.

"Con prácticas agronómicas relativamente simples, incorporando mucho abono y materia orgánica, logramos recuperar esos suelos y ponerlos a producir con muy buenos resultados", explica Luis. 


El objetivo inicial era sencillo en su formulación, aunque ambicioso en la práctica: que familias de la localidad pudieran

producir alimentos sanos para autoconsumo y comercializar el excedente, generando un ingreso sin que el acceso a la tierra fuera una barrera

. "Empezamos con nueve familias. A cada una se le asignó una parcela y al año siguiente ya habíamos ampliado el predio. Hoy son 32 familias las que forman parte del Nodo", precisa Luis.


También instalaron un sistema de riego por goteo para optimizar el uso del agua, una decisión clave en una región donde cada recurso debe administrarse cuidadosamente y donde el riego tradicional habría dificultado la producción. Para Ñancucheo, el mayor logro del proyecto fue más allá del trabajo sobre la tierra o de la comercialización de los productos. Las familias productores recibeb cada sábado a los vecinos para realizar venta directa de la cosecha en el Nodo y coordinan visitas y pedidos vía WhatsApp.


Foto: Dolavón Produce / Nodo Productivo


"Lo productivo en estos proyectos no suele ser un problema sino las relaciones entre las personas. Y ahí fue donde el proyecto resultó altamente exitoso." Al tiempo que sus trabajadores fueron aprendiendo y mejorando las tierras, el Nodo logró un sentido de pertenencia para las familias y empezaron a tejerse redes de apoyo en torno a la producción de alimentos. 


En ese sentido, Luis marca cómo el deterioro del poder adquisitivo durante los últimos años y la necesidad de multiplicar los medios para sostener cada economía familiar resultó un obstáculo para el desarrollo del Nodo durante el 2024 y 2025.  “Algunos de los productores debían salir a hacer una changa para completar sus ingresos y no podían atender su parcela —grafica Luis y agrega—. Pero creo que en esta crisis se fortalecieron esos lazos. El gran desafío fue acompañar a cada familia, entender qué le estaba pasando y ser solidarios."


Aunque hasta el momento ninguna de las familias productoras vive exclusivamente del trabajo en el Nodo, todas aún requieren de tener otro empleo para solventarse, la dimensión colectiva resulta fundamental y despertó interés en otros …

Shakti se nutre de las voces de mujeres agricultoras orgánicas del movimiento Mahila Anna Swaraj (MAS) en toda la India. Documenta su resiliencia y determinación como guardianas y protectoras de la libertad de las semillas, y como cultivadoras de jardines de esperanza, un paradigma para la salud y la seguridad alimentaria. 


Comparte sus historias sobre cómo han desarrollado formas de agricultura sostenibles e indígenas que han combatido el legado de deuda y tragedia creado por las corporaciones de transgénicos, y han guiado a sus comunidades a través de los desafíos e incertidumbres de la pandemia.


Este cortometraje de 35 minutos es una ventana al trabajo de base de Navdanya y Mahila Anna Swaraj, sembrando un paradigma orgánico, liderado por mujeres, para nuestro futuro alimentario.


SOBRE LOS DIRECTORES


Neel Chaudhuri es dramaturgo, director de teatro y cineasta radicado en Nueva Delhi, cuyo trabajo explora la justicia climática, la ecología y la agricultura sostenible en colaboración con comunidades agrícolas locales. Entre sus documentales con Navdanya se encuentra Shakti, sobre colectivos de mujeres agricultoras y la libertad de semillas en toda la India.


Yashas Chandra es director de fotografía y cineasta, cuyo trabajo se centra en la India rural, el conocimiento indígena y la resiliencia ecológica. Ha colaborado con Navdanya en cortometrajes que documentan la agricultura orgánica, la diversidad de semillas y las respuestas comunitarias a las crisis climáticas y agrarias, entre ellos Shakti.

author: Ash Sarkar
title: Racism Pushed Jason Arday to the Top of the News Agenda
content:
On Friday 14 August 2026, Jason Arday was found dead at his home in south London. For three weeks, he had been at the centre of a campaign of public shaming that had turned every aspect of his life upside down. He is survived by his two children.


The sequence of events is important. Not long after Arday took up the post as chair of sociology of education at Cambridge in 2023,

David Harris

 (an emeritus professor at Plymouth Marjon University, whose work has been sceptical of critical race theory) contacted the university along with Martyn Hammersley, a sociologist at the Open University, about what they viewed as similarities between a paper of Arday’s from 2018, and an earlier paper led by epidemiologist Anjum Memon. A few months later, two of Arday’s papers were appended with corrections post-publication.


In September 2025, Jack Grove, a reporter at Times Higher Education (THE), was investigating claims that Arday had plagiarised parts of his PhD thesis. He contacted Arday for right of reply, and submitted a dossier of evidence to both Cambridge and the awarding university, Liverpool John Moores. THE was preparing to publish a story on the allegations. THE dropped the story after receiving a legal letter sent by notorious libel firm Carter-Ruck; in February of this year, Grove was

warned by police

 not to contact Arday again, having received a complaint of harassment.


Liverpool John Moores conducted an inquiry into academic misconduct, and characterised citation problems in Arday’s work as “

honest and reasonable error

”. 


After the THE investigation stalled,

Nathan Cofnas

 – a self-described “race realist” argued that black people “would disappear from almost all high-profile positions outside of sport and entertainment” under a meritocratic system and who was fired by his Cambridge college in 2024 – began investigating the claims against Arday after being contacted by a member of the Cambridge faculty. He wrote about Arday on his Substack, claiming he had put Arday’s work

through plagiarism detection software

. With Cofnas’ post gaining traction, the plagiarism allegations began to break into the mainstream press.


Though the initial coverage of Arday was about alleged plagiarism in academic papers, soon reporters were pulling apart his entire biography. Articles were published disputing claims he had held visiting professorships, completed a master’s at Birkbeck, published a book with Palgrave Macmillan, raised millions for charity, and undertaken extraordinary feats of endurance running.


His forthcoming autobiography,

Great and Unfortunate Things

, was another object of investigation. The Times obtained an earlier 45-page proposal containing still more extraordinary episodes (a teenage car crash left him in a coma with locked-in syndrome, that doctors wanted to withdraw life support, and that he later survived testicular cancer) which did not appear in the finished memoir. Arday resigned from Cambridge on 5 August.


Between 24 July 2026, when the plagiarism allegations were first reported by The Telegraph, and 14 August 2026, when his death was reported, the British press published

249 articles about Arday

 – most of them

after

 he had resigned from his post. The instances of alleged fabrication were expansive, and raised serious questions about whether Arday’s memoir had been properly fact-checked. But inside the raging whirlwind of articles and accusations, a man’s life was being torn apart.


“I have a family,” wrote Arday in his

resignation statement

. “I want to be present for them.” The pressure had taken him to “the limits of what any person should reasonably be expected to endure.” 


Where is the line drawn between investigative rigour and a media onslaught? Nobody who finds themselves the subject of interrogative reporting experiences it as dispassionate, neutral scrutiny. They’re having their entire world upended, their flaws and their frailties exposed for the world to see. Fundamentally, journalism is a dynamic of predator and prey, in service of the public interest. But public interest is just one consideration; there is also proportion, and due prominence, that need to be kept in mind. 


There were legitimate questions to be answered by Arday, about his research and his account of his life. But it should never have been a front-page story. Even if all the worst things that were said about him turned out to be true, he was not the biggest nor most pressing issue …

author: CMI Argentina
title: Apartheid porteño: El racismo institucional del gobierno de Jorge Macri
content:
Desalojos ilegales, perfilamiento racial, “prioridad porteña”: medidas de un gobierno que hace de la segregación práctica y propaganda. “El discurso racista es el núcleo duro de la derecha en todas sus versiones”, sostiene Federico Pita, de DIAFAR.


El jefe de Gobierno, Jorge Macri, parece decidido a correrse tan a la derecha como la ciudadanía porteña se lo permita. Lanzado en una campaña por su reelección, ha estructurado un discurso basado en la segregación de quienes su gestión clasifica como “no deseables”: migrantes, morochos, vendedores ambulantes, personas en situación de calle, habitantes de barrios populares y no porteños, por supuesto, de bajos recursos.


Esa publicidad oficial, que financian todos los vecinos y vecinas, y machaca con el latiguillo “Ley y orden”, se apoya en acciones represivas concretas: razzias, desalojos ilegales, saturación policial de espacios públicos, secuestros de mercadería a trabajadores informales, persecución a cartoneros, entre otras.


“Lo explícito del racismo de varias de las consignas de su gestión anticipa el año electoral. La derecha, después de casi dos décadas, para intentar retener su bastión, en un acto desesperado para mantenerse en el poder, está encontrando en el racismo explícito la razón de ser de su política y lo está ejerciendo de forma categórica”, sostiene Federico Pita, politólogo y columnista y editor del suplemento

Negrx

 de

Página|12

. Como activista de la afroargentinidad es fundador de

DIAFAR

 (Diáspora Africana de la Argentina) y Espacio Malcolm.


“Lo que puedo destacar es el silencio de la política en relación a este tema. La política con vocación de oposición, la política con vocación de gobernar la ciudad de otra manera, guarda un silencio sorprendente o subestima esta agenda a la que creo que hay que prestar mucha atención”, advierte Pita.


Apartheid porteño


“Un día nos llega un material en el que se ve a un joven en las afueras de la estación de Constitución contra la pared. Era un cacheo policial donde, palabras más palabras menos, el agente de la Policía de la Ciudad le decía: “¿Vos de dónde sos?”. “De Berazategui”, responde el muchacho con gorrita. “¿Qué hacés acá? Vos no tenés que estar acá en la ciudad, volvete a Berazategui”. Lo que era sorprendente es que cuando vamos a chequear la fuente de ese video, resulta que estaba posteado en las redes sociales del Ministerio de Seguridad de la Ciudad”, relata Pita. “Por lo tanto, hablamos de hostigamiento, de violencia racial y un

apartheid

 de hecho. Esta idea de que si sos de Berazategui, no tenés nada que hacer en Buenos Aires, ‘Andate de acá’, recortado por el ministerio que se supone sostiene la política de seguridad de la Ciudad, es claramente una línea roja”.


 


Ver esta publicación en Instagram


 


Una publicación compartida por Ministerio de Seguridad de la Ciudad Autónoma de Buenos Aires (@baseguridad)


“La metáfora del

apartheid

 que utilizamos no es antojadiza. El

apartheid

 fue un sistema segregacionista que rigió durante muchas décadas en Sudáfrica que planteaba la segregación racial como una jerarquía legal. Ser blanco era ser superior y ser negro era ser inferior en términos legales. Y eso, por ejemplo, implicaba una suerte de restricciones en la circulación. Si eras negro no podías habitar en determinadas zonas de las capitales de Sudáfrica. Como si acá los negros no pudiesen pasear por Palermo”.


“Había un sistema de pases. Si eras una empleada doméstica en Barrio Norte, pero vivías en Berazategui, tenías que tener un pase, un carnet que acreditase que vos trabajabas en ese lugar porque si te paraba en la calle una autoridad, te pedía el pase para justificar por qué estabas en ese lugar vedado”.


El 21 de marzo de 1960, en Sharpeville, Sudáfrica, “hubo una protesta y una quema pública de pases a las afueras de una comisaría. La policía abrió fuego matando a 69 de hombres, mujeres y niños”. En conmemoración de este hecho, la ONU estableció el Día Internacional de Lucha por la Eliminación de la Discriminación Racial.


“Aunque el negro vista de seda, negro queda”


La aplicación de este

apartheid

 se basa en la aplicación del semblanteo o el perfilamiento racial, “nosotros diríamos, la portación de rostro. Vos ves un pibe morocho con gorrita y salta la alerta. Al morocho le pedís el documento para, acto seguido, justificar la violencia y en este caso su color es suficiente prueba para el maltrato y el hostigamiento”.

author: infolibre
title: Όταν το Ισραήλ εφευρίσκει ψεύτικους «αντισημίτες», οι αληθινοί ετοιμάζονται να χτυπήσουν
content:
Του

Γιώργου Μητραλιά


Χωρίς αμφιβολία, ο κατά Νετανιάχου «αντισημιτισμός» κάνει θραύση στις μέρες μας! Απόδειξη; Το Ισραήλ, το εβραϊκό κράτος που ισχυρίζεται ότι εκπροσωπεί όλους τους Εβραίους στον πλανήτη, είναι «το πιο μισητό κράτος στον κόσμο», όπως διαπιστώνει ο J.D. Vance, ο αντιπρόεδρος του Τραμπ, ο οποίος αρέσκεται να επισημαίνει ότι η κυβέρνησή του είναι η πιο φιλοϊσραηλινή στην ιστορία των Ηνωμένων Πολιτειών! Αυτή η διαπίστωση είναι αρκετά σοβαρή ώστε να αξίζει μια εξήγηση, καθώς μάλιστα οι ηγέτες αυτού του ισραηλινού κράτους δεν σταματάνε να λένε ότι όσοι επικρίνουν, και πόσο μάλλον «μισούν» τη χώρα τους, είναι ορκισμένοι «αντισημίτες». Πώς, λοιπόν, φτάσαμε να έχουν γίνει σχεδόν οι πάντες «αντισημίτες»; Και ποιος φέρει τη μεγαλύτερη ευθύνη γι’ αυτό;


Προφανώς, κύριος υπεύθυνος είναι το κράτος του Ισραήλ, οι πολιτικές του και κυρίως οι πράξεις του. Και αναμφισβήτητα, είναι η συνεχιζόμενη ακόμα και τώρα γενοκτονία των Παλαιστινίων της Γάζας, που συγκλόνισε και συγκίνησε τόσο πολύ ολόκληρη την ανθρωπότητα ώστε να της ανοίξει τα μάτια μια για πάντα για την πραγματική αποικιακή, ρατσιστική και βάρβαρη φύση του σιωνιστικού κράτους. Ωστόσο, η γενοκτονία – σε ζωντανή μετάδοση– των Παλαιστινίων δεν εξηγεί τα πάντα. ‘Έπαιξαν ρόλο και οι πολύ «κακές συναναστροφές» αυτού του ισραηλινού κράτους και των ηγετών του. Ηγετών, όπως ο ίδιος ο Νετανιάχου, που δεν δίστασαν να συμμαχήσουν με κάθε λογής ρατσιστικά αποβράσματα, νοσταλγών ή κληρονόμων γενοκτονικών αντισημιτικών καθεστώτων του παρελθόντος, προκειμένου να εφαρμόσουν τις πολιτικές τους, μεταξύ των οποίων και εκείνη που συνίσταται στον πόλεμο που έχουν κηρύξει σε όσους βαφτίζουν «αντισημίτες» επειδή «τολμούν» να επικρίνουν τις εγκληματικές, ρατσιστικές και δολοφονικές τους πολιτικές. Δεν αποτελεί λοιπόν έκπληξη το γεγονός ότι είναι ακριβώς η «ελίτ» της ευρωπαϊκής ακροδεξιάς με το βίαιο αντισημιτικό παρελθόν, όπως η γερμανική νεοναζιστική AFD, το ισπανικό φρανκιστικό VOX ή το γαλλικό πεταινιστικό RN της Λε Πεν, που γίνονται οι καλύτεροι υποστηρικτές του Ισραήλ και οι πρώτοι που δυσφημούν και σέρνουν στα δικαστήρια χαρακτηρίζοντας «αντισημίτη» οποιονδήποτε, συμπεριλαμβανομένων και Εβραίων, που τολμά να επικρίνει τις εγκληματικές πολιτικές αυτής της χώρας. Εν ολίγοις, ο κόσμος ανάποδα…


Όπως, για παράδειγμα, το έκαναν εναντίον του (Εβραίου)

Edgar Morin

 με καταγωγή από την Θεσσαλονίκη

, του μεγάλου Γάλλου κοινωνιολόγου και φιλόσοφου, του οποίου το έργο, η ζωή και οι πράξεις σημάδεψαν το δεύτερο μισό του 20ού αιώνα, κατηγορώντας τον για «αντισημιτισμό» επειδή τόλμησε να συνυπογράψει το 2002 ένα κείμενο με τίτλο «

Παλαιστίνη-Ισραήλ: ο καρκίνος

», που περιλάμβανε φράσεις όπως η εξής: 

«Οι

Εβραίοι

 του

 Ισραήλ

, απόγονοι των θυμάτων ενός

απαρτχάιντ

 που ονομάζεται

γκέτο

, γκετοποιούν τους

Παλαιστινίους.

 

Οι Εβραίοι, θύματα της απανθρωπιάς, επιδεικνύουν τρομερή απανθρωπιά. Οι Εβραίοι,

αποδιοπομπαίοι τράγοι

 για όλα τα δεινά, κάνουν «αποδιοπομπαίους τράγους»

 τον Αραφάτ

 και την 

Παλαιστινιακή Αρχή

, τους οποίους καθιστούν υπεύθυνους για επιθέσεις που τους εμποδίζουν να αποτρέψουν.

 » (1) Οι δίκες που έστησαν τα τσιράκια του σιωνιστικού κράτους, σε διατεταγμένη υπηρεσία, κράτησαν τέσσερα χρόνια πριν καταλήξουν στην αθώωση των τριών κατηγορουμένων, μεταξύ των οποίων και ο Εντγκάρ Μορέν, που έφυγε πριν λίγο από τη ζωή έναν μήνα πριν από τα 105

α

 γενέθλιά του, όχι όμως χωρίς να επαναλάβει ότι ήταν «

αποσβολωμένος και αγανακτισμένος

» από τη «

σφαγή

» που διέπραξε το Ισραήλ στη Γάζα.


Όμως, αυτή που έμεινε στην ιστορία ως «υπόθεση Μορέν» δεν θα έπρεπε πια να προκαλεί έκπληξη. Η φάμπρικα παραγωγής ψεύτικων αντισημιτών κάνει στις μέρες μας υπερωρίες. Ο λόγος απλός: οι Εβραίοι που ασκούν έντονη κριτική στο Κράτος του Ισραήλ ή είναι ακόμη και αντισιωνιστές, είναι πλέον μιλιούνια στη Διασπορά. Σε τέτοιο βαθμό ώστε οι αντιισραηλινοί και αντισιωνιστικοί φιλιππικοί ενός πρώην προέδρου του ισραηλινού κοινοβουλίου (!) και πρώην προέδρου της Παγκόσμιας Σιωνιστικής Οργάνωσης (!) όπως ήταν ο

Avrum Burg,

 να μην προκαλούν πια την εντύπωση που θα . άξιζαν να .προκαλέσουν. Έναν Αβρούμ Μπουργκ που δεν φοβάται να δηλώσει ότι «ο

σιωνισμός είναι ρατσισμός

» και ο οποίος ορίζει, με τις ακόλουθες λακωνικές φράσεις, τις απαραίτητες προϋποθέσεις για μια διαρκή ειρήνη στη Μέση Ανατολή:

author: Luis Feliz Leon
title: Federal Spies Hunt Minnesota Unions in Search of Conspiracy, But Find Solidarity
content:
Yesterday

news broke

 of a sweeping undercover investigation by the Department of Homeland Security in Minnesota early this year to infiltrate and surveil meetings and obtain the financial records of nonprofit groups and two of the country’s largest unions, the Communications Workers (CWA) and the Service Employees (SEIU). This investigation was behind the

indictments

 of 15 people in June.


The news should unite the labor movement in defense of constitutional rights and democracy as its members face what one defendant’s attorney calls “

political prosecution

.”


“CWA 7250 has learned that we have been subject to an illegal and aggressive federal investigation that used undercover agents to enter our office, infiltrate meetings we co-sponsored, subpoena our finances, and surveil one of our officers,” said  CWA Local 7250 President Kieran Knutson.


“We know that this is because our members, from across the workplaces we represent,


were active in the fight against the federal occupation and racist campaign of terror by ICE. CWA 7250 members joined neighborhood rapid-response groups, distributed warning whistles, protested at the Whipple Federal Building, marched in the streets and the snow, and helped build the January 23rd Day of Truth and Freedom.


“We are proud of our work and will never apologize or back down because of these dirty tricks and intimidation.”


“The most notable revelation to me was their infiltration of the February 15th Workers Assembly to Defeat ICE, a great event that brought over 300 unionists and community members together to democratically debate on next steps for the movement,” said UFCW Local 663 executive board member Paul Kirk-Davidoff, a meat cutter at Cub Foods supermarket.


“I helped put this together, and multiple unions sponsored the event.

Four

 undercovers attended, and made sure to take detailed notes of all the speakers and political positions. This, along with the surveillance of unions, leads me to believe that the feds were frightened by the January 23rd mass strike and the possibility of more labor action.”


BOGUS CONSPIRACY


Federal Deputy Attorney General Brian Lynch

participated

 in the January 6 insurrection at the Capitol. Now he is leading a taskforce dedicated to prosecuting left-wing activism, which the administration calls political violence. The taskforce is using Trump’s

National Security Policy Memorandum

 (NSPM-7) to investigate the funding sources of the president’s opponents.


Lynch is casting a wide net to go after Trump’s perceived enemies. The investigation targets, among others, the AFL-CIO, the Minnesota Association of Professional Employees, and the Minneapolis Federation of Educators. A

slide

 that prosecutors showed to a grand jury portrays the unions, along with some nonprofits, left groups, and a bike shop, as part of an antifa conspiracy.


Minnesotans are responding with solidarity.


“This winter, Minnesotans stood together in rejecting the Trump regime’s occupation of Minnesota,” said a

statement

 from a broad coalition of unions and nonprofit organizations, including many who had not been targeted in the investigation so far.


“Trump’s ICE and Border Patrol agents broke countless laws while kidnapping Minnesotans based on racial profiling, violating our constitutional rights, and murdering our neighbors… Across the state, Minnesotans joined with community, faith, labor, and neighborhood organizations to build networks that protected our neighbors and defended our constitutional rights.”


“Minneapolis educators worked in union to exercise our constitutional rights to peacefully protest Operation Metro Surge and other discriminatory policies of the president—and we will continue to do so,” said Minneapolis Federation of Educators Teacher Chapter President Marcia Howard in a statement. “For now, we have no further comment about this so-called investigation into whatever they’re calling ‘Antifa’ today.”

title: Appel à contre-rassemblement antiraciste et antifasciste contre l'extrême-droite dimanche 16 août à 18h
content:
Les identitaires européens de la campagne raciste

Save Europe Act

 organisent une tournée européenne pour propager en toute impunité leur projet de durcissement des politiques migratoires et de «

 

remigration

 

» c'est-à dire littéralement la déportation des personnes immigrées. Ce projet ne surgit pas dans le vide. Partout en Europe, les politiques migratoires se durcissent, les discours racistes se banalisent, ce qui était hier porté par les marges de l'extrême droite est aujourd'hui repris dans les discours politiques et médiatiques et se traduit dans les politiques publiques. Le Parlement européen a adopté en mars un texte ouvrant la voie à un renforcement des procédures d'expulsion, à la possibilité de recourir à des «

 

plate formes de retour

 

» et à l'utilisation accrue des centres de rétention administratifs.


La déshumanisation des personnes migrantes se banalise, entraînant une multiplication des agressions racistes, comme à Belfast où des milices d'extrême droite ont attaqué et incendié des maisons de familles immigrées. Pendant ce temps, les frontières européennes continuent de tuer. Quand les voies légales sont fermées, celles et ceux qui cherchent refuge sont contraintes de prendre des routes toujours plus dangereuses. À Ceuta comme en Méditerranée, les morts et les drames humains se succèdent. Et à chaque nouvelle tragédie, l'extrême droite réclame davantage de frontières alors que celles-ci sont déjà bien verrouillées.


Nous refusons cette logique, d'autant plus si l'on tient compte de la responsabilité de l'Etat français dans ces mouvements migratoires, à travers son soutien aux projets coloniaux et impérialistes, sa complicité aux crimes de guerres et génocides et son inaction face à la crise climatique. L'internationalisme demeure la meilleure réponse au nationalisme et la libre circulation des personnes est la seule réponse désirable aux questions migratoires. Après Utrecht aux Pays-Bas où les fascistes ont pu parader, puis Lille où leur rassemblement a été annulé par la préfecture, et avant de passer en Espagne où ils vont continuer d'instrumentaliser le drame humanitaire de Ceuta à des fins racistes, les fascistes prévoient de venir déployer leur banderole «

 

Remigration saves Europe

 

» à Lyon ce dimanche 16 août à 18h place Saint-Jean.


Nous appelons à un

contre-rassemblement antiraciste et antifasciste contre l'extrême-droite ce dimanche à 18h devant la Cour d'Appel de Lyon

. Soyons plus nombreuxses qu'eux

 

! Face à leur horizon mortifère, notre horizon sera toujours la solidarité, le respect de la dignité humaine, et l'anéantissement de tous les systèmes d'oppression

 

!


Antifascistes tant qu'il le faudra

 

!

author: Mekong Review 2
title: Stand and fight Calum Stuart
content:
Credit: Ivan Weiss


T

he day I interviewed Daniel York Loh, there was news of anti-immigration protests—some of which turned violent—erupting across Belfast, Northern Ireland. The BBC reported that people had been targeted simply for having “a different skin colour”.


In recent years, xenophobic and racist rhetoric has been on the rise in the UK. This has manifested alongside right-wing politicians and political parties (such as Nigel Farage, leader of Reform UK, and Tommy Robinson, a far-right activist) moving from fringe entities into mainstream influence. For Loh—an actor, writer, and filmmaker of Singaporean and British heritage who has been a vocal supporter of left-wing causes—these developments have been equal parts alarming and maddening.


Based in London, Loh has been working in the performing arts in both the UK and Asia for more than forty years. In that time, he’s become increasingly invested in working to improve Asian representation on stage and on screen. He was a founding member of BEATS (British East and Southeast Asian in Theatre and on Screen), a not-for-profit, volunteer-based advocacy group for British East and Southeast Asians working in theatre, film, or television. He’s also a member of the Race Equality Committee of Equity, the trade union for performers and creatives in the entertainment and performing arts industry. In 2016, he was one of twenty-one contributors to the anthology

The Good Immigrant

, reflecting on issues of race, immigration, identity, and Othering in the UK. A tenth anniversary issue of the book was launched this year.


More recently, Loh appeared in the true crime drama

I Fought The Law

, a four-part series following the determined struggle of Ann Ming—played by the award-winning British actor Sheridan Smith—a former nurse who campaigned for seventeen years to overturn the UK’s double jeopardy law after the murder of her daughter in 1989. Loh stars as Ming’s mixed-race husband, Charlie, in a story that examines grief and trauma, while not shying away from the racial politics of Britain in the 1980s and 1990s.


I’d like to start with

I Fought The Law

, which was based on a true story. It received rave reviews and you were nominated for an award at the 2026 Royal Television Society North East and the Borders Awards. What was it like taking on this role and playing a character based on a real person?


Daniel York Loh with Sheridan Smith in I Fought The Law. Credit: Anastasia A Arsentyeva


Charlie Ming, he was like me. He was mixed race but, essentially, very, very British. Very, very Middlesbrough [a town in North Yorkshire, England]. Ann Ming was kind of an advisor on the series, but [Charlie’s] not around anymore.


I Fought The Law

 was based on Ann Ming’s book [

For the Love of Julie

, published in 2009]. It was a real privilege to do it. It was such a good script and an amazing story. Sheridan Smith is an amazing actor and we had a great director [Erik Richter Strand]. I can’t speak highly enough of the whole thing, really.


I got the impression that it resonated with people because, right now, there’s a widespread sense of cynicism in many places. But in the series you have an ordinary person who’s taking on a massive system and prevailing.


I’m told the viewing figures were very high for the modern era. I think people were very taken with [the story]; it was a genuinely huge achievement. Ann Ming kept on going, she was very dogged, which I think people really admire… when you win in the end. If you’re very dogged and you don’t win, they kind of think you’re mad.


How do you feel the series dealt with the issue of racism?


There was a scene that flashed back to when Ann and Charlie were younger, and the racist neighbour comes around and there’s graffiti with racist slurs on the wall outside. And there were a few people online going, “Oh, typical ‘woke’ ITV.” But that’s in her book! It’s in Ann Ming’s book, and it was actually much worse. They suffered terrible racism when they first got together. I wanted that stuff in there. It’s important in social history and it resonates with what’s going on now.


There’s always people who want to blame migrants for anything and everything. If you put one foot out of line, your entire ‘community’—in inverted commas, because people don’t know each other a lot of the time—suffers. It reminds me of my own childhood. My childhood was basically [full of] racist abuse and my dad coming up to the school; the teachers …

author: Julius Gavroche
title: Reflections on a decade of UK Black Lives Matter
content:
From

Freedom News

 (

09/08/2026

)


This racist violence we experience is an active race?making project serving the interests of capital


Kojo


Black Lives Matter UK was founded by activists who had worked together on previous deaths in police custody, both in the US and Britain.


In the US, it had started as a love letter to Black people in the aftermath of George Zimmerman’s acquittal – who killed 17-year-old Trayvon Martin in 2012 for the crime of carrying Skittles while Black in a gated community.


In Britain our martyr was Mark Duggan, killed by the Met in 2011. We not only remember the anti-Black propaganda about his criminality, how even some radical leftists argued he needed to die, how the army needed to be brought in to control rioters. We remember the public disregard of his and Black life in general. We live with the reality of State harassment and violence in terms of stop and search, legal sexual assault in terms of strip searches. State racist violence is not only structural, it structures the British economy and State legitimacy.


Today, which is worse than in 2011, almost one in two Black children do not get three meals a day. Ethnically Black African children do better than white British children in GCSEs, but are less likely to get a paid job. All of this motivates us because it is our lived reality.


“I can’t breathe” was said 11 times by Eric Garner, a father of four, who was strangled to death, on camera, by a New York cop in 2014. His death sparked the second iteration of Black Lives Matter protests across the US, and in Britain that became the 2014 Westfield protest.


Sean Rigg, who died in police custody at Brixton Station in 2008, Roger Sylvester in Tottenham in 1999. Jimmy Mubenga in 2010. Those names were with us as we decided to form 

Black Lives Matter UK

.


The US has always been used as a way to paint Britain as moderate, because “we’re not like America.” British policing is seen as sensible. We don’t have guns.


So part of the struggle was not only to continue the fight for accountability, but also about how to make these struggles more visible. How do we honour the lives that have been lost, which continue to be discarded by the State? The thing about Mark Duggan’s death wasn’t just that the police were seen as heroic, they were seen as doing what needed to be done. What that says is when you are stopped and searched, or your home is raided on spurious grounds, when children are asked to be undressed in front of police officials, this is for the public good. You deserve this.


And we wanted a politics of refusal.


We came from different traditions. We weren’t all from one Trotskyist group, some were more liberal, I’m from a more anarchist strand. These tensions played out in asking who do we appeal to? In 2016, all of us came to a conclusion on the day after the Brexit referendum, when we saw on the front page of The Sun newspaper, actual neo-Nazis wearing Vote Leave T-shirts celebrating their victory. For us that was indicative of what was to come. A new revived form of White supremacy. Ten years on, you can judge for yourselves if that’s accurate.


So we agreed to protest on the fifth anniversary of the police killing of Mark Duggan. On Friday August 5th 2016, to the soundtrack of Skepta’s Shutdown, we were going to shut down Heathrow Airport, Birmingham Airport, Nottingham Central. With the motivation of Brexit and police State violence. The impunity with which the police could kill and be told it’s good.


We did disrupt these things. We had people ready to go to the media to explain Britain is not innocent. That Britain’s imperial legacy is framed to perpetuate its present, where Black people are systematically discriminated against. Not only in the criminal punishment system but in education, employment, housing, health outcomes. Every facet of life.


The liberal framework


The liberal arguments that we normally hear are around unconscious bias, unintended consequences, the lag of the State to modernise in a multi-racial democracy and as a result, that policies designed to benefit all people have a disproportionate effect on minoritised groups who live mostly in deprived areas – i.e. State violence towards the working class is normal, it just happens to particularly affect Black and Asian people.


We reject this. While it is true that Black and Asian people live in more deprived areas. It’s not happenstance. The way the economy is structured means there …

author: Andrea DiP
title: Maria da Penha, 20 anos: Alta de feminicídios revela fracasso estatal em proteger mulheres
content:
O Brasil segue sendo um país violento, especialmente para as pessoas negras e para as mulheres. Pelo quarto ano consecutivo, o país registra índices recordes de feminicídios e tentativas de feminicídio, de acordo com o

Anuário Brasileiro de Segurança Pública 2026

.

Apenas no ano passado, foram 1.571 vítimas desse crime, a maioria mulheres negras, assassinadas dentro de casa. A Lei Maria da Penha completa 20 anos, mas a violência contra as mulheres permanece como um dos principais desafios na segurança pública.


Nesta semana, o Pauta Pública recebe Juliana Brandão, advogada e coordenadora de Gênero e Raça do Fórum Brasileiro de Segurança Pública. Em entrevista a Andrea Dip, ela analisa os dados do Anuário Brasileiro de Segurança Pública, o impacto do racismo nas taxas de violência, e defende a importância de políticas públicas voltadas à prevenção e ao fortalecimento da rede de proteção às vítimas.

“Quando a gente se abstém de pensar em saídas preventivas, a gente está consentindo com essa escalada”

, afirma.


Juliana Brandão é advogada e coordenadora de Gênero e Raça do Fórum Brasileiro de Segurança Pública


Leia os principais pontos da conversa e ouça o podcast completo abaixo.


EP 228


											O fracasso do Estado em proteger mulheres – com Juliana Brandão


7 de agosto de 2026


					·


				Coordenadora de gênero e raça do Fórum Brasileiro de Segurança Pública analisa as falhas de crimes contra a mulher


0:00


-:–


15


15


Veja mais episódios desta série


Segundo dados do último Anuário Brasileiro de Segurança Pública, em 2025, o Brasil registrou o maior número de feminicídios da série histórica iniciada em 2015, quando a tipificação do crime foi criada no país. De que tipo de violência de gênero estamos falando?


Estamos falando de uma violência que interrompe a vida das mulheres, uma violência que pode ser evitada. Porque o feminicídio, na verdade, é o ápice de um ciclo de violência que se inicia com um empurrão, um tapa, uma humilhação, com a violência psicológica, patrimonial e perseguição.

Essas violências acabam sendo naturalizadas e desconsideradas como tal. Com isso, a mulher vai se sentindo cada vez mais enredada nesse ciclo

, muitas vezes envergonhada e até se sentindo culpada por estar nessa situação.


Porque estamos falando de uma violência que é cometida por alguém que é do círculo muito próximo dessa mulher. Essa violência do feminicídio, que os dados do anuário trazem agora, é uma violência que acontece na maior parte das vezes dentro de casa, entre quatro paredes. Então, o problema está no ambiente doméstico. O problema está naquilo que acontece quando ninguém vê, quando a porta está fechada.


Quando falamos da violência que atinge também crianças e adolescentes, é também praticada por alguém que é do círculo muito próximo delas e a maior parte das vítimas são meninas negras, que repetem também o perfil das vítimas de feminicídio.

 Então, temos um endereçamento muito certo dessa violência, que já devia ser um sinal pra gente, um farol para onde a gente tem que olhar se a gente quer de fato mudar essa essa situação que a gente está vivendo.


Houve também um número alto de tentativas de feminicídio. Quer dizer que há falhas na prevenção?


Olhando para os dados, a gente vê uma escalada. Então, um recrudescimento da violência contra as mulheres, que não se explica tão só por uma melhora de enquadramento penal, mas por uma situação mais geral. Um caldo mesmo de violência que é expresso por um Brasil que é muito inseguro para as mulheres.


É muito difícil ser mulher no Brasil, porque as mulheres são vítimas de ameaça, as mulheres são vítimas de agressão, as mulheres são vítimas de perseguição. E se a gente levar em conta que essa mulher tem denunciado esses preditores de feminicídio, significa que ela vai e faz um boletim de ocorrência. Ali, por exemplo, já seria um momento de a gente dizer: “Olha, essa mulher aqui a gente tem que olhar com mais cuidado, porque ela conseguiu vencer essa barreira, ela conseguiu entender que não é culpada, ela conseguiu entender que não está sozinha. E o que acontece dentro do lar dela é algo que importa para o nosso coletivo. Vamos trazê-la para mais perto, vamos olhar o que está acontecendo, que rotina é essa, que autonomia ela tem, como é que ela sai desse enredo”, que é um enredo que vai, de alguma forma, dizimando as possibilidades de a mulher, de fato, encontrar uma saída.

title: ABD: "Sosyalistler halka kulak verdikleri için kazanıyor"
content:
2026 ara seçimlerine bir kaç ay kala, ABD siyasetinde bir sosyalist heyula kol geziyor. İki partili Trump ve MAGA Cumhuriyetçilerin popülist sağcılığı karşısında bir dönem bocalayan Demokrat Parti'nin 2024 yenilgisi sonrasında muhalefette yeniden başını kaldırmasında sosyalistlerin rolü giderek belirginleşiyor. New York Belediye Başkanlığını Trump'ın desteklediği Demokrat Partili rakibini yenilgiye uğratarak kazanan Mamdani'nin zaferinden sonra sosyalistlerin başını çektiği, tabanın söz ve kararına dayalı çalışma tarzı gitgide partinin yönünü daha derinden belirlemeye başlıyor. 


Toplumsal sorunlar üzerine çarpıcı denemeleriyle tanınan New York Times köşe yazarı, sosyolog ve kültür eleştirmeni Profesör Tressie McMillan Cottom, bu süreci çevirisini sunduğumuz "Sosyalistler halka kulak verdikleri için kazanıyor" başlıklı makalesiyle değerlendiriyor.


Amerikan siyasetinde sosyalist bir canlanmaya mı tanık oluyoruz?


Zohran Mamdani'nin New York Belediye Başkanı seçilmesinden bu yana yapılan siyasi tahlilleri toparladığınızda solculuğun altın çağında yaşadığınıza ya da komünistlerin gelmekte olduğuna inanasınız gelebilir.


Solcu adayların önseçim başarıları


Bu tablo, gün gelip seçim sonuçlarına da yansıyabilir; ama o gün bugün değil. Evet, bu hafta pek çok solcu aday başarılı oldu; Michigan ve Kansas'ta dikkat çekici ön seçim zaferleri kazanıldı, ama yarışı kazananların arasında pek çok ılımlı Demokrat da vardı. Kazanan adaylardan bazılarının kampanya bütçesi oldukça yüksekti. Diğerleri ise son derece büyük bir mali sıkıntıyla başa çıkmak zorundaydı. Ancak içlerindeki en iyiler, Demokratların kazanmak için yalnızca seçmenlerden bağış toplamakla kalmayıp onları örgütlemeleri gerektiğinin idrakinde kampanya yürütenlerdi.


Demokrat Partinin yapısal sorunları


Demokrat Parti derin bir yapısal sorunla karşı karşıya. Bir yanda özlemini duyduğu geçmiş, öte yanda ise henüz kuramadığı bir gelecek var. Şimdilik bunun farkında olan yalnızca partinin ilerici kanadı gibi görünüyor.


Düzen içi Demokrat Partililer, solcu adayların seçilebilirliği konusunda istedikleri kadar gürültü koparsalar da, partinin halletmesi gereken daha büyük meseleleri var. Demokratların seçim gücünün iki kaynağından biri olan işçi hareketi, New Deal'den sonraki on yıllar boyunca işçi sınıfından erkeklerin oylarını güvence altına almış ve kırsal bölgelerde, ABD'nin kuzeydoğusu ile Büyük Göller çevresinde yer alan, 20. Yüzyılın büyük bölümünde ülkenin ağır sanayi merkezi olan, ancak 1970'lerden itibaren hızlı sanayisizleşme yaşayan bölgelere verilen adla Rust Belt'te (Pas Kuşağı) Demokratların ana damarı olarak iş görmüştü. Sivil haklar örgütleri ise, Kennedy’nin öldürülmesinden sonra başa geçen Demokrat Başkan Lyndon B. Johnson’ın Sivil Haklar Yasası'nı imzaladığı günden beri bekleceği şekilde Siyahların oylarını güvence altına alarak Demokratların Güney'de rekabeti sürdürebilmesini sağlamıştı. Uzun yıllar boyunca sıradan Demokrat adaylar, karmaşık siyasal mesajlarını seçmene ulaştırma işini büyük ölçüde bu iki örgütlü toplumsal güce bıraktı.


Demokrat Parti'nin kendi sınırlarına varması


Anlaşılması gereken en önemli şey, peş peşe  60 yıl boyunca biriken ekonomik, hukuksal, siyasal ve kültürel zorlukların sendikalar ve sivil hak gruplarının bu görevi yerine getirmesini artık imkânsız değilse de çok güç kılmış olması.


Özellikle siyah sivil haklar örgütleri uzun zamandır Demokrat Parti'nin örgütlenmesi  için büyük çaba gösteriyor. Sadece sandığa gitmekle kalmıyor, seçmen yetiştiriyor, ulusal platformları yerel mesajlarla dönüştürüyor ve adaylarla çalışanları eğitiyor. Demokrat Parti'nin seçim makinesini ayakta tutanlar, kiliselerde ışıkları söndürmeyenler, minibüsleri kullanan, mahalle mahalle dolaşan, mitinglere katılan ve seçim günü seçmeni güvenle sandığa taşıyanlar siyah kadınlardı. Güney'deki siyah örgütçüler, Yüksek Mahkeme tarafından Oy Hakkı Yasası’nın budanmasından sonra Demokratların bir süvari kıtası gibi yardıma koşmasını bekliyordu. Oysa şimdi kendilerini terk edilmiş hissediyorlar. Muhafazakârların savunuculuk ve lobi örgütü Heritage Action ile kampüslerde ve seçim kampanyalarında faaliyet gösteren gençlik ve siyasi aktivizm örgütü Turning Point USA gibi gruplara bakıp, bakıp, "Bizim de böyle kurumlarımız olsaydı" diye hayıflanıyorlar.


Sendikalı işçilerin oranı da rekor düzeyde düşük. Demokratlar işçi sınıfı seçmenlerini geri kazanacak ve Güney'i harekete geçirecek, seçim kazandıracak merkezci bir mesaj bulsalar bile, seçmeni …

title: Abschiebeoffensive und/vs Arbeitsmarkt (am Beispiel der Landwirtschaft) in den USA – und der Schlingelkurs von Trump
content:
Dossier


„

Für einen kurzen Moment schien Präsident Donald Trump es verstanden zu haben. Landwirtschaftsministerin Brooke Rollins erklärte Trump, dass Landwirte aufgrund der verschärften Kontrollen von Einwanderern ohne Papiere Schwierigkeiten hätten, Arbeitskräfte zu finden. Daraufhin schrieb Trump am vergangenen Donnerstag in den sozialen Medien, dass Landwirte und Hotelbetreiber „darauf hingewiesen haben, dass unsere sehr aggressive Einwanderungspolitik ihnen sehr gute, langjährige Arbeitskräfte wegnimmt, die kaum zu ersetzen sind“. Infolgedessen stellten Beamte der US-Einwanderungs- und Zollbehörde die Verhaftungen in landwirtschaftlichen Betrieben, Hotels und Restaurants ein (…) Die Aussetzung dauerte ganze drei Tage

…“ engl.

Artikel von McClatchy California Editorial Boards vom 20.6.2025 in Fresno Bee


 (maschinenübersetzt) – siehe mehr zum Dilemma auch der Gewerkschaften:


Gewerkschaftsfeinde nutzen die ICE, um Wanderarbeiter*innen in der kalifornischen Weinindustrie einzuschüchtern – diese schließen sich zu Gewerkschaften zusammen


„

Die kalifornische Weinindustrie basiert auf der Ausbeutung von Einwanderern. Nun schließen sich die Wanderarbeiter zu Gewerkschaften zusammen.


Ende Juli berief Raul Calvo, ein bekannter Gewerkschaftsgegner aus Kalifornien, die Arbeiter von Rodney Strong Vineyards zu einer Besprechung ein. Salvador Ramirez, der seit 12 Jahren zwischen den großen Weintanks arbeitete, sagt, er sei schockiert gewesen von dem, was er hörte. „Er sagte, er wolle uns lediglich die Information weitergeben, die er vor drei Tagen per E-Mail erhalten habe, nämlich dass die ICE [Immigration and Customs Enforcement] hier draußen sei“, erinnert sich Ramirez und merkt an, dass Calvo den Beschäftigten erklärte, das Weingut befinde sich aufgrund seiner Nähe zum Meer technisch gesehen in einer Grenzzone.


Ramirez sagt, die Beschäftigten seien sehr verärgert gewesen – nicht nur wegen Calvos angedeuteter Drohung, sondern auch, weil sich die Haltung des Unternehmens drastisch gewandelt hatte. Im vergangenen Oktober, als Gerüchte kursierten, dass ICE-Beamte eine Welle von Razzien in der San Francisco Bay Area planten, ähnlich wie sie derzeit in Los Angeles stattfinden, hatte das Unternehmen alle zu einer Besprechung einberufen. Ramirez erinnert sich: „‚Ihr seid unsere Mitarbeiter‘, sagten sie uns. ‚Wir müssen euch unterstützen und wir werden nicht zulassen, dass sie hereinkommen [ohne richterlichen Durchsuchungsbefehl]. Wir werden uns gegenseitig schützen.‘“


In den folgenden Monaten begannen die Beschäftigten jedoch, miteinander zu sprechen. Sie wandten sich daraufhin an „North Bay Jobs with Justice“ (JwJ), einen Zusammenschluss von Bürgerinitiativen und Gewerkschaften in den Bezirken Sonoma und Napa, der seit langem für Arbeitnehmerrechte kämpft. North Bay JwJ half ihnen bei der Gründung eines Betriebsrats und stellte den Kontakt zur Teamsters Local 665 her, einer Gewerkschaft, die mit Vertretern im Vorstand der Organisation vertreten ist.


Ramirez und 31 der 50 Beschäftigten des Weinguts unterzeichneten eine Petition, in der sie das Unternehmen aufforderten, einem „Card-Check“-Verfahren zur Anerkennung der von ihnen gegründeten Gewerkschaft zuzustimmen und ein „faires Verfahren zur Ausübung unseres Rechts auf Vereinigungsfreiheit und Gewerkschaftsgründung ohne Drohungen und Einschüchterung“ zu gewährleisten. Anfang Juni legten sie diese der Geschäftsleitung vor. Rafael Malfavon, den die Beschäftigten „Junior“ nennen, überreichte sie und forderte das Unternehmen auf, ihre Entscheidung zu akzeptieren. Führende Persönlichkeiten der Gemeinde – darunter Chris Herrod, der Bürgermeister von Healdsburg – begleiteten sie, um sie zu unterstützen.


Die Reaktion des Unternehmens bestand darin, einen lokalen Gewerkschaftsgegner namens Jesse Rojas einzustellen, der zwei Treffen mit den Beschäftigten abhielt. Dann tauchte Calvo, Rojas’ Chef, auf. Als er Calvo bei einem Treffen wegen falscher Aussagen über Gewerkschaften zur Rede stellte, wurde er laut Malfavon verspottet. „Das hat uns nur bewiesen, dass das Unternehmen nicht darauf hört, was die Beschäftigten sagen und was wir fordern, und diesen Typen engagiert hat, der mich einen Lügner nennt“, sagte er. (…)


Ramirez und seine Kollegen begannen unter anderem deshalb mit der Organisierung, weil das Unternehmen langjährige Mitarbeiter entließ. „Sie begannen, Besprechungen mit uns abzuhalten“, erinnert sich Malfavon, „und sagten, sie müssten ihr Budget kürzen …

author: Soraya Kishtwari
title: US Immigration Agents Caught Spying on Leftwing Activists
content:
US Homeland Security agents have been engaged in a widespread spying operation this year against labour unions, a climate change group and socialist collectives, as well as other left-leaning organisations.


Operation Puppet Master, the

 first

 of two surveillance campaigns, began four days after intensive care nurse

Alex Pretti was shot dead by ICE agents

 during January’s protests against Donald Trump’s crackdown on immigrants in Minneapolis,

the New York Times reports

.


In the aftermath of Pretti’s death,


Homeland Security officials turned their attention to leftwing activists. Investigators were tasked with looking into funding to see if organisations had provided “

violent opportunists and agitators

” with resources for protests.


Undercover agents infiltrated events – including meetings held online and at churches, parks and libraries – to spy on protesters and organisers. Agents also went as far as

summoning

 three years worth of financial records from some of its surveillance subjects, including environmental direct action group Sunrise Movement and the Communication Workers of America, a labour union. 


The Service Employees International Union, the largest union representing healthcare workers, also had three years of wire transfers investigated. The AFL-CIO, the largest union federation, the Democratic Socialists of America and Showing Up for Racial Justice were also investigated. 


None of the organisations has been charged with a crime, but the investigations have led to the prosecution of 15 people accused of conspiring to obstruct federal immigration officers.


Court filings reveal that the covert operations continued for months after the immigration crackdown in Minnesota had ended.


The investigations were made public after a defence lawyer representing one of the Minneapolis protesters facing criminal charges filed a request calling on the court to compel the government to hand their reports over as evidence.


Kevin Riach, the lawyer who filed the request, pointed to the “de-humanising terms” used by the Trump administration to describe leftwing organisers. “These wild conspiracy allegations are born from the fantasies of political retribution that animate the Trump administration,” Riach

wrote in a court filing

.  


“President Trump and senior administration officials routinely speak of the political left in de-humanising terms – as ‘deformed, ‘scarred,’ and ‘filled with ugliness,’ for example. The administration has crystallised these sentiments into policies that encourage and authorise political prosecutions like this one.”

author: Elizabeth Weill-Greenberg, Ethan Corey
title: Deportation Dollars: ICE Contracts With More Than 1,000 Businesses Across the U.S.
content:
With billions of dollars to spend, the Trump administration has entered into contracts with hundreds of companies, both big and small, to execute its deportation agenda. Since January 20, 2025, Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) has awarded $8.4 billion dollars to more than 1,100 companies, according to The Appeal’s analysis of data available on the government spending website

usaspending.gov

. 


The Appeal’s investigation reveals a widespread web of public and private entities enabling Trump’s deportation machine. We’re publishing the results of our investigation

in a database

 so users can identify companies and governments in their area working with ICE. 


Find ICE Contractors Near You


Our investigation found ICE contractors in nearly every state. Use our searchable database to browse contracts in your state, county, or ZIP code.


Search the full database.


ICE has awarded approximately $154 million in contracts for combat training, weapons, and related items, such as restraints, handcuffs, leg restraints, and belly chains. The agency also entered into contracts worth about $77,000 for “Sniper Training Equipment,” and a

contract for about $19,900 with a company called ShivWorks

 for “Defensive Tactic Knives for law Enforcement Training courses.” Last week, the Associated Press reported that the agency was

planning to purchase gloves

 that deliver electric shocks. 


The largest recipient of weapons spending, Atlantic Diving Supply, has received nearly $100 million. 


But much of ICE’s spending involves more banal goods and services essential to the everyday functioning of the agency, including approximately:


$52 million for office furniture; 


$4.3 million for roofing contractors;


$1.2 million for interior design services; and


$2.1 million for parking space leases.


The One Big Beautiful Bill Act, signed into law last year,

allocated $75 billion to ICE

, to be disbursed over the course of four years, or about $18.7 billion a year. That funding was on top of the $10 billion Congress had already given to ICE for fiscal year 2025. ICE now has a

larger budget

 than any other federal law enforcement agency. 


In addition to private companies, ICE has also entered into contracts with several local governments. 


Last year, the City of Arlington in Texas

entered into an about $50,000 contract

 to provide the “ICE Office of Human Capital with a 3-day venue” for a hiring expo for law enforcement candidates. Earlier this year,

ICE entered into a contract

 with the

town of Lancaster, New York

 for “a rental of a secured parking facility … for storage and deployment of up to 164 government vehicles.” 


The agency also

contracted with the City of Cottage Grove

 in Minnesota for the rental of a firearms range facility to train law enforcement officers in the “St. Paul Area of Responsibility.” The contract was for about $118,000 and ran from August 1, 2025 through July 31, 2026. Earlier this year, immigration officers shot and killed two protesters in Minneapolis, Renee Good and Alex Pretti, in addition to

shooting Julio Cesar Sosa-Celis

, who survived.. Since last year, federal immigration officers have

shot at least 23 people

 nationwide, according to a New York Times investigation.


The summary of a contract for

medical supplies with Altitude Technologies

 states that the “the purpose of this contract award is to provide compact trauma kits essential for medical emergencies and critical incidents to enhance ICE personnel survival during encounters involving severe hemorrhage or penetrating chest wounds.” 


There is no mention of using the supplies for people who are injured by ICE officers.


ICE did not respond to The Appeal’s request for comment on this contract.

 outside the hotels where they were staying. Protesters banged pots and pans, chanted, and played music in hopes that the hotels would kick out the ICE agents.

author: David Swanson
title: How Finland Destroyed Itself For NATO
content:
By

Nate Bear

, Aug 18, 2026


Finland, often known as the happiest country in the world, now has the

highest unemployment rate in Europe

,

demand for food aid

 has exploded by more than 70%, and homelessness, which had been declining for more than ten years, has

increased 34% in just two years

. Conditions in the country are so bad that almost 20% of Finland’s population is now

considered at risk of poverty

,


Once considered the standard bearer for the good life, for competent governance and a strong social state, Finland is unravelling at warp speed. What has gone wrong so quickly?


In three words, NATO, austerity, and Russophobia.


All are linked. Finland is slashing its social state to the bone to meet NATO’s 5% GDP military spending target, a target which became necessary after the country abandoned neutrality and swapped the welfare state for the warfare state after Russia’s invasion of Ukraine.


The speed of the collapse has been stunning.


In 2019, the at-risk of poverty rate

was 11%

 and by 2022 the country was on course to hit record low unemployment.


Everything changed after Russia’s invasion of Ukraine and the country’s hysterical over-reaction to an imagined threat. This is not just my judgement. A number of Finnish academics, including

Heikki Patomäki

, professor of world politics at the University of Helsinki, have said that the conditions simply did not warrant Finland joining NATO, cutting off its economically valuable links to Russia and militarising its border.


The facts support this.


At the time of its invasion of Ukraine, Russia had just

a couple of thousand troops

 spread out across various bases on its 1,340 km border with Finland. The bases were home to handful of missile defence batteries and a few dozen tanks. Many of the troops and much of the equipment was subsequently deployed to Ukraine,

leaving the bases empty

. There was obviously no invasion threat, and Putin in May 2022 emphasised this

in a phone call

 to Finland’s then-president Sauli Niinistö.


But by this point, the Russophobia and hysteria for NATO membership had begun to take on a life of its own. Sanna Marin, Finland’s young female prime minister at the time, and a liberal media darling, was a particularly effective saleswoman. Despite claiming in the days following Russia’s invasion that there was no threat, her tone became decidedly more hawkish in the months that followed. She said Russia “poses a threat to all of us” and began talking like a war-time leader,

saying in September 2022

that “Russia may challenge Finland, blackmail us and threaten us, but we will not give in.” Bear in mind, Russia at this point had practically zero troops and equipment on its western border with Finland. The Russian threat she was invoking was entirely imagined, an hallucination.


Nevertheless, in April 2023, Finland joined NATO, just days after Marin was defeated by the right and far-right in an election where the policy choice on Russia was one of uniformity, with the conservatives, the ethno-nationalists and Marin’s social democrats all singing the same tune.


After her defeat, Marin

scuttled off to work for Tony Blair

, while the new conservative-nationalist government set about decimating Finland’s welfare state to pay for the privilege of NATO membership.


The Finnish government is now a substantial way through its programme to cut

€9 billion of public spending by 2027

, including

large reductions to social security

 (including housing, child, and unemployment benefits) healthcare, education, and municipal funding budgets, while it also increasing taxes on average earners. Cuts to healthcare provision have been

particularly brutal

, including a large reduction in hospital staff numbers, elderly care and disability services while redefining “minimum service obligations” to justify providing patients with lower quality care. The government has also slashed funding for organisations

working on peace

 and initiatives which would address the new cold war-style relations with Russia.


In addition, the new government fully closed all the border crossings with Russia that Marin’s Social Democrats had partially closed, and began building large sections of a border fence, securitised with troops, night vision cameras and motion detectors.


And while the entire country is now suffering as a result of the pro-war paranoia that has gripped Finland’s leaders, its border towns have taken a particular …

author: Unknown
title: Kurdish kolbar dies one year after being shot by Iranian border guards
content:
Milad Tabad, a 28-year-old kolbar from Marivan, Kurdistan Province, has died from injuries sustained when Iranian border guards shot him in the head around a year ago.


A source in Marivan told the Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN): “On 25 August 2025, border guards opened fire on the kolbar in the Tateh border highlands of Hawraman [in Sarvabad County, Kurdistan Province] while he was not carrying any goods, wounding him in the head.”


According to the source, he was initially taken to Bou Ali Hospital in Marivan before being transferred to medical facilities in Sanandaj due to the severity of his injuries.


Tabad spent several months in intensive care, but after his condition improved to some extent, his family were forced to take him home because of the high cost of keeping him in hospital.


He remained in poor physical condition over the following year and was recently readmitted to medical facilities in Sanandaj after his condition deteriorated. He died from his injuries on 18 August.


Tabad was a father of one from the village of Geleyeh in Marivan County.

author: Zora
title: 100 Leute protestieren gegen die Ausschaffung von Bahar Yalçınkaya und Dilan Özgun.
content:
Bahar Yalçınkaya wurde am 4. August gewaltsam zusammen mit ihren beiden Kindern aus dem Rückkehrzentrum Oberhalden Finkenried im Kanton Zürich in die Türkei abgeschoben. Sie befindet sich mit ihrem 15 Monate alten Baby im Frauengefängnis Bakirköy in Istanbul. Ihre 5-jährige Tochter wurde von ihr getrennt. Yalçınkaya Anwalt hat das SEM (Staatssekretariat für Migration) vor einer möglichen Festnahme und Inhaftierung bei einer Abschiebung gewarnt. 


Am Morgen des Protesttages wurde im gleichen Camp eine weitere Ausschaffung versucht:  Dilan Özgun und ihre Familie aus dem Camp Hinteregg sollte ebenfalls in die Türkei ausgeschafft werden. Die Familie wehrte sich jedoch so stark, dass die Ausschaffung abgebrochen wurde. Viele Campbewohner*innen halfen ebenfalls, die Ausschaffung zu verhindern: mit Protestrufen und Diskussionen mit der Polizei, bis diese abzog. 


Dass das SEM, zwei Wochen nach Ausschaffung von Bahar Yalçınkaya und deren sofortigen Inhaftierung in der Türkei eine weitere kurdische Familie in Erdogans Regime zurückschaffen wollte, zeugt von der Härte des Asylregimes, aber auch davon, dass die Bundesbehörde die Umstände nicht zugunsten der Betroffenen berücksichtigt. Die Rede des kurdischen Frauenrates an der Kundgebung bringt dies auf den Punkt:


„Die Fälle Bahar Yalçınkaya und Dilan Özgün reihen sich in ein dokumentiertes, wiederkehrendes Muster ein und machen deutlich, dass im Schweizer Asylsystem Menschenverachtung längst zum System geworden ist. Gewaltsame Zwangsausschaffungen als «notwendige Verwaltungspraxis» zu verharmlosen, normalisiert Gewalt und die Missachtung von menschenrechtlichen Mindeststandards.“ (Kurdischer Frauenrat Bern)


Eine sofortige Praxisänderung hinsichtlich der Ausschaffungen in die Türkei wäre die einzig angemessene Reaktion.


Der Protest richtete sich gegen alle Ausschaffungen, gegen die angewendete psychische und physische Gewalt bei den Ausschaffungen aber auch gegen die psychisch krankmachenden Bedingungen des schweizerischen Asylsystems und den Asylunterbringungen.
