title: Toscana sacrificata
content:
Ripubblichiamo questo testo originariamente apparso su Scrivania Autogestita di Informazione che ha il pregio di tessere i fili di ciò che si sta verificando sulla regione Toscana, individuando le tendenze e gli interessi in campo.


La Toscana si sta consolidando come hub militare ed energetico sacrificando persone e territori a discapito di un modello che vede militarizzazione ed estrattivismo al primo posto.


Riprendendo l’ultimo capitolo dell’articolo che abbiamo pubblicato pochi giorni fa sul nuovo progetto eolico flottante offshore che vorrebbero costruire tra l’isola di Capraia e l’isola di Gorgona proviamo a mettere insieme un pò di elementi per descrivere come le opere e le attività legate alla guerra e all’energia stiano modificando irreversibilmente il territorio toscano. 


Hub militare


Tramite il bollettino 

HUB – Bollettino della militarizzazione e delle resistenze dei territori

, nato a partire dal campeggio organizzato dal 

Movimento No Base

 nel 2025, abbiamo e stiamo descrivendo, insieme a tutte le realtà che partecipano alla stesura, la militarizzazione nel territorio toscano. 


Nel 

primo numero

, dedicato all’hub toscano – ligure, sono state descritte le principali infrastrutture presenti tra Pisa e Livorno. Dalla base statunitense di Camp Darby fino alla nuova base del CISAM si è visto come il territorio si sta rafforzando come piattaforma di guerra del Mediterrano. La presenza del porto di Livorno, che vedrà un importante ampliamento tramite la costruzione della nuova Darsena Europa, il canale dei Navicelli, l’aeroporto militare e i collegamenti ferroviari, costituiscono insieme alle basi militari una rete logistica fondamentale per la guerra. 


Nel 

secondo numero

, pubblicato a fine luglio scorso, si è fatto un approfondimento proprio sull’utilizzo di infrastrutture dual use. Che dovrebbero cioè essere di utilizzo esclusivamente civile ma che invece si stanno sviluppando anche come snodi militari. Porto di Livorno, canale dei Navicelli e collegamenti ferroviari si stanno potenziando pure in questa ottica. Si è poi analizzata la situazione delle fabbriche di armi, con un focus sulla Leonardo S.p.A. L’azienda non è solo fabbrica di morte complice con Israele del genocidico palestinese, ma un vero e proprio sistema che si è insediato nei luoghi dove si sviluppano conoscenze e tecnologie, come le Università. Non solo Leonardo. Ci sono altre fabbriche di armamenti presenti sul territorio livornese come DRASS – produttore di sottomarini -, Wass – produttore di siluri e droni subacquei-  e la Cheddite – produttore di munizioni.


Insomma un quadro a dir poco preoccupante, in un contesto mondiale di guerre che non accenna a placarsi e che proietta il territorio toscano come punto di riferimento fondamentale, andando così a mettere in pericolo la popolazione e sfruttando i territori per favorire l’economia bellica. 


Hub energetico


L’ultimo progetto energetico in fase di valutazione di impatto ambientale è quello dell’enorme parco eolico flottante offshore Atis che vorrebbero costruire tra l’Isola di Capraia e l’isola di Gorgona. In questo 

articolo

 ne abbiamo descritto le caratteristiche. La panoramica è preoccupante visto che l’impatto sull’ambiente sarà enorme. Questa operazione incarna perfettamente il modello energetico che anche questo governo sta portando avanti. Territori sacrificati per far spazio ad enormi impianti a beneficio di grandi gruppi industriali e multinazionali senza considerare le conseguenze. Il carico territoriale energetico sulla Toscana, in particolare sulla Val di Cornia e sull’area costiera livornese, sarà ulteriormente gravoso, data già l’elevata presenza di grandi impianti siderurgici, discariche e gestione rifiuti, infrastrutture energetiche di rilevanza nazionale, incluso il rigassificatore.


A Livorno è presente la raffineria Eni, che sta vivendo in questo periodo la conversione parziale a bioraffineria, (ennesima operazione di greenwashing) situata in un’area SIN – Sito di Interesse Nazionale – e che dovrebbe quindi essere bonificata a causa del suo impatto altamente inquinante. 


C’è anche il rigassificatore situato a circa 22 km dalla costa e attivo dal 2013.


A Piombino troviamo lo storico stabilimento siderurgico per la lavorazione dell’acciaio. Inoltre, anche qui, dal 2023 è stato posizionato un rigassificatore all’interno del porto. Un’operazione che negli anni scorsi ha visto l’opposizione trasversale della popolazione locale ma che …

author: David Swanson
title: Statement of the Ukrainian Pacifist Movement: Defending Human Rights and Ending Lawlessness in Territorial Recruitment Centers (TCCs)
content:
By

IPB

, August 21, 2026


We support Ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets and his representative Andriy Kryuchkov in their resistance to the lawlessness of territorial recruitment centers (TCCs). We are concerned about the information attacks on the Ombudsman’s institution and the attempts by offending commanders to shift responsibility for their unlawful actions onto the human rights defenders who exposed them.


As a reminder, in April of this year, Lubinets finally acknowledged that TCC premises have effectively turned into places of detention without any legal grounds. He cited examples of the illegal detention of people in unsanitary and degrading conditions at the Uzhhorod District TCC for up to 50 days, the confiscation of documents and phones, and the deprivation of the right to legal aid and medical assistance. The photos and videos published by Lubinets shocked the nation.


Pacifists have many questions regarding formal brush-offs instead of human rights work by the Secretariat of the Commissioner and Lubinets personally in cases of brutal violations against conscientious objectors in general and our members in particular. We understand the pressure the Commissioner’s institution faces from the army and security service. We remember how he was summoned to the Ministry of Defense in 2024 and pressured not to insist on the unacceptability of legislation regarding tough mobilization that allowed systemic violations of fundamental rights.


However, it deserves respect and support that in some of the most egregious cases, the Commissioner and his representatives still dare to fight against gross and systemic human rights violations by the Armed Forces of Ukraine, or at least publicly tell the truth about terrible abuses, arbitrariness, inhumanity, legal nihilism, deaths, and severe injuries in TCCs.


The fact that after these illegalities are exposed, the perpetrators remain unpunished, investigations are formalistic, victims and human rights defenders face retaliation, and temporarily suspended officers return and continue in the same vein is utterly mind-boggling and demands louder public calls for reform.


We urge the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine and the Ministry of Defense to review mobilization approaches that are incompatible with Ukraine’s obligations under Articles 3, 5, and 9 of the European Convention on Human Rights, and to stop obstructing the implementation of alternative non-military service in Ukraine during wartime, in line with Ukraine’s EU accession commitments. Pacifists cannot be forced into becoming part of the system of industrialized mass murder that is war and the armies that wage it. Kidnapping and torture should have no place in a democratic state governed by the rule of law, even during wartime.


We can and must defend Ukraine through peaceful, lawful means.

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: Meet Loui Ridi: Palestinian American Returns to West Bank Home Besieged by Israeli Settlers
content:
Loui Ridi, a Palestinian American man who lives in Ohio, traveled to the occupied West Bank on Monday to help relatives defend their family home in the village of Qusra, south of Nablus. Israeli settlers have surrounded the home, which Ridi owns, for more than a week. Settlers have besieged several Palestinian houses in the village, trapping people inside and cutting off water and electricity in some cases.


“I’m not getting no protection here. I still fear for my life. I still fear for my family’s life here,” says Ridi, who joins

Democracy Now!

 from the occupied West Bank. Ridi has raised an American flag on his home and reached out to the U.S. Embassy for help. “The

IDF

 is not even making it better here. They’re not allowing us to leave the house. They’re not allowing anyone to come to my house freely,” says Ridi, explaining that getting food to the house takes “hours, if not days.”


The settlers “can act like this because of the active support from the Israeli government that gives them weapons, gives them ATVs,” says Israeli reporter Oren Ziv, who has traveled to Qusra twice in recent days. Ziv says the Israeli government also supports “the establishment of more and more [settler] outposts that are kind of front bases for these terror attacks.”

author: Daron Letts
title: Arctic Talent: The art of athletics
content:
Art and athletics are Blair Boiteau’s passions. She found a way to pair them together.


The Chesterfield Inlet seamstress and former Arctic sports competitor designs decorative and practical sealskin targets.


These sealskin targets for Arctic sports, such as the Alaskan high kick, swing kick, and two-foot high kick are the creations of Chesterfield Inlet artist Blair Boiteau. Boiteau competed in Arctic sports throughout her youth at the Kivalliq Summer Games and Arctic Winter Games. (Photo courtesy of Blair Boiteau)


The targets are used in events such as the two-foot high kick, the one-arm reach, and the Alaskan high kick, together called Arctic sports and also referred to as Inuit games.


“I used to enjoy kicking those targets and I love keeping the Arctic sports alive, so I use my art to share that,” Boiteau said.


A bit smaller than a softball, the targets are fashioned from shaped strips of sealskin and leather sewn into a tight sphere. Boiteau adds leather designs showing the silhouette of Arctic sports athletes in action, and other shapes.


She has sold the targets to customers across Nunavut.


The targets are used in competition at the Arctic Winter Games and in the recently revived

Kivalliq Summer Games

.


Boiteau helped coach the athletes during the first Kivalliq Summer Games to be held in 12 years, from Aug. 14 to 16 in the Chesterfield Inlet community hall. The event brought about two dozen athletes from Arviat, Baker Lake, Rankin Inlet and Whale Cove to Chesterfield Inlet to compete in 14 traditional Inuit competitions.


Boiteau’s 14-year-old daughter, Ashlynn Boiteau, was one of those athletes.


Ashlynn earned nine medals throughout the weekend.


Sports is not all mother and daughter share in common. Ashlynn is creative as well as athletic, and is beginning to draw, her mom said.


Boiteau described her path from sports to art during a recent interview.


Winter 1993:

 Boiteau learns to sew in junior high at Victor Sammurtok School, back when several cultural studies teachers worked there.


As a student she makes parkas, mitts, and kamikpak – cozy duffle socks

. She keeps sewing into adulthood.


”I’m always learning,” she said.


Winter 1993-Summer 2012:

 Boiteau competes in Arctic sports in every Arctic Winter Games and Kivalliq Summer Games except for 2010, when she studied at Ottawa’s Nunavut Arctic College.


Summer 2019

:

 Boiteau creates her first tapestry. It depicts a woman facing the horizon with a bright sun above. Other symbols include fish, ulus, and a bird in flight.


“It’s to show that the future is bright,” she said.


It goes on permanent display at Rankin Inlet’s Sakku Office Building.


Winter 2023:

Boiteau wins her first logo-design contest. Her winning logo is adopted by the Foxe Basin Kivalliq North Sapujiyiit Society. The Inuit-led organization provides environmental monitoring services for the hamlets of Chesterfield Inlet, Coral Harbour, and Naujaat.


Summer 2024:


Boiteau wins a second logo contest, for the Inuit Association of Manitoba.


The logo features an ulu framed by a drum.


Summer 2025:

 Boiteau wins another logo-design contest, this one for a local daycare. She also names the business, Iglu Tots. The logo includes two children with an igloo between them.


”It’s really cute,” said daycare staff member Francine Alogut.


”It’s nice and colourful.”


Spring 2026:

 One of Boiteau’s sealskin targets goes on display in the permanent art exhibit in the Chesterfield Inlet airport terminal.


Talent Tip:

 “We learn from our mistakes,” she said. “Just keep trying.”

author: anred
title: El Estado promueve un salto en la escalada represiva contra la clase obrera y la izquierda
content:
La nueva guía antiterrorista -de la Procuración General de la Nación- blinda el ajuste criminalizando la organización popular.


El pasado 14 de agosto, la Procuración General de la Nación dictó la 

resolución interna 56/2026

 para unificar el criterio de las fiscalías federales y reforzar la acción de las fuerzas de seguridad contra la organización popular, el movimiento obrero, piquetero y los organismos de derechos humanos. Al ordenar la aplicación obligatoria de la “Guía para la investigación de incidentes terroristas previos a un ataque”, habilita a intervenir asambleas, plenarios, charlas y actividades de todo tipo, abriendo las puertas a la infiltración de las fuerzas represivas. Estamos ante un salto cualitativo en la ofensiva contra las libertades democráticas y políticas de la población.

Por Demian Maciel, para Prensa Obrera.


El terrorismo político: de la ley al salto operacional


Hace una década, el kirchnerismo introdujo el concepto de «terrorismo» en el ordenamiento penal mediante la Ley Antiterrorista, una exigencia del Grupo de Acción Financiera Internacional (Gafi) utilizada por sucesivos gobiernos patronales para perseguir organizaciones populares. La resolución PGN 56/2026 profundiza esta dirección al incorporar el «terrorismo político» como categoría operacional para los fiscales federales, facultando la intervención sobre organizaciones e individuos bajo criterios de excepcionalidad basados en «modelos de personalidad», discursos y debates que el poder considere peligrosos. Este documento consuma casi ocho años de espionaje sobre el movimiento popular. El trabajo conjunto se inició en 2018, bajo el gobierno de Macri, cuando el Ministerio de Seguridad y la inteligencia estatal comenzaron a monitorear a las fiscalías en las causas contra quienes enfrentaron la reforma previsional de diciembre de 2017. Años más tarde, este andamiaje sirvió para perseguir, allanar e intervenir a las organizaciones piqueteras que combaten el hambre en los barrios populares.


La necesidad de blindar el ajuste con represión


La aplicación de planes de ajuste salvajes y de hambre contra los trabajadores, que el gobierno nacional de Milei aplica con la complicidad directa del peronismo y la burocracia sindical, solo puede sostenerse mediante un salto en la regimentación estatal, la intimidación preventiva y la represión directa de los sectores que salen a luchar. Como la capacidad de contención del peronismo, la CGT y la CTA se desgasta aceleradamente por abajo, el Estado necesita compensar ese vacío de control mediante el uso directo de la fuerza estatal. La publicación de esta Guía, apenas días después de las jornadas contra la reforma de la «ley de tierras» donde la juventud resistió heroicamente la represión policial hasta altas horas de la noche, expone con claridad la urgencia del régimen por blindar judicialmente su plan de guerra contra la población.


La superestructura judicial corre en auxilio del capital: la «prevención del terrorismo» es la excusa jurídica que han encontrado para intentar maniatar a la vanguardia obrera, estudiantil y piquetera antes de que logre canalizar y organizar el descontento de las masas. La incorporación del «terrorismo» como eje de intervención fiscal en un país sin atentados contra civiles desde hace treinta años constituye la formalización de este salto represivo. Implica un deslizamiento flagrante e inconstitucional hacia el derecho penal de autor, violatorio del principio de inocencia que surge del artículo 18 de la Constitución Nacional.


El «ciclo terrorista»


Para justificar este atropello, la resolución ordena actuar bajo el concepto de “ciclo terrorista”, un modelo de «justicia preventiva» elaborado por agencias de inteligencia de Estados Unidos y de Israel. Sostiene que existe una «unidad de acción» entre la movilización popular y la actividad política previa (charlas, reuniones, convocatorias, etc.), y por lo tanto, la Guía declara que “no estamos en presencia de un delito aislado ni de un hecho instantáneo, sino de un proceso complejo, organizado y permanente, que se desarrolla a lo largo del tiempo y a través de múltiples fases funcionalmente coordinadas e intrínsecamente conectadas”.


La consecuencia es que faculta a los fiscales a investigar penalmente conductas lícitas que no constituyen ningún delito, violando el principio procesal penal de legalidad (dar una charla, debatir en un foro, organizar un comedor o expresar una opinión en redes), bajo la teoría …

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: As International Pressure Grows, Israel Finally Opens Probe into 2024 Killing of Hind Rajab in Gaza
content:
Israel’s military on Wednesday admitted that its soldiers opened fire in January 2024 on a car trying to flee Gaza City following Israel’s evacuation orders. The car was carrying 5-year-old Palestinian Hind Rajab and six of her relatives. They were all killed, as were Palestine Red Crescent Society medics dispatched to rescue them. The Israeli military said it would also investigate the killing of 15 Palestinian paramedics whose bodies and crushed emergency vehicles were recovered from a mass grave in Rafah in March 2025. It made no mention of thousands of other incidents where Palestinian civilians were killed by Israeli forces.


“This seems to be nothing more than political theater,” says Sharif Abdel Kouddous, the Middle East and North Africa editor at

Drop Site News

. He was a correspondent on the Al Jazeera

Fault Lines

 documentary

The Night Won’t End

 that investigated the killings of civilians in Gaza by the Israeli military, including Hind Rajab.


“Israel’s internal investigations into the criminal conduct of its own soldiers … can’t be regarded as credible mechanisms for accountability,” says Abdel Kouddous. “They instead function primarily to shield Israel from international tribunals or prosecution abroad.”

author: Shan Kenshin Ecaldre
title: BPO worker’s dismissal as retaliation for labor organizing
content:
Photo from Center for Trade Union and Human Rights

The termination of Kyle Enero is a textbook case of how corporations use vague allegations and administrative procedures to silence labor leaders.

LAGUNA — Labor and human rights groups denounced the dismissal of a business process outsourcing (BPO) worker who happens to be a labor organizer.

They stressed that the dismissal reflects a pattern of retaliation against workers who organize, speak out, and demand safer workplaces and higher wages.

Azpired Inc. fired BPO worker and organizer John Kyle Enero on August 11, according to the Center for Trade Union and Human Rights (CTUHR), after months of disciplinary actions and heightened scrutiny that labor groups said were linked to his involvement in workers’ rights campaigns.

Enero, a customer service representative who had worked in the BPO industry for three years, is also president of the BPO Industry Employees Network (BIEN)-Cebu and vice president for Visayas of BIEN Pilipinas.

“The termination of Kyle Enero is a textbook case of how corporations use vague allegations and administrative procedures to silence labor leaders,” said Kamz Deligente, CTUHR executive director. “They want to instill a culture of fear to stop BPO workers from demanding their basic rights to safety and fair wages.”

Enero’s conflict with management reportedly intensified after a 6.9 magnitude earthquake struck Cebu on September 30, 2025.

As an employee representative during Occupational Safety and Health (OSH) inspections, Enero and BIEN-Cebu raised concerns over BPO companies allegedly requiring employees to report to work despite questions surrounding workplace and building safety.

BIEN-Cebu pushed for OSH inspections across BPO workplaces and filed complaints concerning alleged safety violations.

According to CTUHR, Enero became a prominent workers’ advocate during the aftermath of the earthquake when employees raised concerns about being made to work onsite amid safety risks.

BIEN said that management later warned Enero to “tread carefully” after the organization filed complaints over OSH concerns.

The labor group said disciplinary actions against Enero continued and intensified following his organizing activities.

The conflict escalated when BIEN-Cebu campaigned for a P1,200 ($19) increase in the regional minimum wage in Central Visayas, alongside consultations with workers and engagement with the Regional Tripartite Wages and Productivity Board VII.

For BIEN-Cebu, the timing of Enero’s disciplinary actions and dismissal raises concerns that his labor organizing and advocacy were targeted.

“The dismissal of a worker who exercises his right to organize and raise legitimate labor concerns sends a chilling message to employees across the industry: Speak up about your rights, and you risk losing your livelihood,” BIEN-Cebu said in its August 15 statement.

Enero was terminated after being accused of “unauthorized disclosure” involving the facilitation of system access for a former employee.

He denied the allegations, according to CTUHR, and questioned the company’s failure to provide evidence of the alleged violation.

BIEN-Cebu said that the dismissal followed a 12-day suspension that it considered illegal and part of a series of disciplinary measures it described as baseless and retaliatory.

The organization said that Enero documented workplace harassment, repeated disciplinary notices, and increased scrutiny of his activities as a worker-organizer.

The groups stressed that the allegations remain disputed and that Enero challenged the disciplinary actions.

CTUHR also criticized an alleged settlement agreement offered by the company that included a provision restricting Enero from speaking publicly about his termination.

For the labor rights group, such restrictions can prevent workers from bringing alleged labor violations into public scrutiny.

Enero’s dismissal drew solidarity from workers’ groups and unions, including the Gabay ng Unyon sa Telekomunikasyon ng mga Superbisor (GUTS) PLDT which warned that punishing a worker for his or her advocacy could intimidate workers across industries.

BIEN-Cebu said that the case goes beyond an individual employment dispute, stressing that BPO workers’ right to organize, raise workplace concerns, and demand better wages and working conditions without fear of retaliation.

“When one worker is punished for advocacy, it is a warning shot against all of us. We refuse to be …

author: Dominic Gutoman
title: US sanctions vs. ICC hinders victims’ quest for justice
content:
MANILA – The United States (US) announced sanctions on International Criminal Court (ICC) President Judge Tomoko Akan and Abdoulaye Seye, a senior trial lawyer at the Office of the Prosecutor, on August 19 amid an ongoing campaign to dismantle the Court.

The sanctions aim to impose legal, financial, and travel restrictions to the targeted individuals. As of this writing, the US has sanctioned nine judges, two deputy prosecutors, a former Prosecutor and a staff of the ICC.

“When judicial actors are threatened for applying the law, it is the international legal order itself that is placed at risk. Threats and coercive measures also impact the ability of victims to seek justice, as they turn to the Court when all other avenues have been exhausted,” the ICC said in a statement.

The ICC is prosecuting the case of Rodrigo Duterte. The ICC Pre-Trial Chamber I found reasonable grounds to believe that Duterte is responsible as an indirect co-perpetrator for the crimes against humanity of murder when he was Davao City Mayor and, later on, President of the Philippines.

Read: Timeline: ICC case against Rodrigo Duterte

“As previously stated, the Court remains undeterred and stands firmly behind its personnel and behind victims of unimaginable atrocities,” the ICC said. “The Court will continue to fully discharge its mandate with independence and impartiality, in full accordance with the Rome Statute and in the interest of victims of international crimes.”

Cristina Palabay, secretary-general of Karapatan, told Bulatlat that the US government’s actions expose its disregard for international human rights law “while it commits the most horrific crimes against humanity in its role in the mass murders of the people of Palestine, Iran, and other countries subject of the US wars of aggression.”

US is the largest provider of military aid of Israel in its ongoing genocide to the people of Palestine in Gaza. According to policy analyst William Hartung of Quincy Institute, the US spent $21.7 billion on military aid to Israel which does not include the tens of billions of dollars in arms sales agreements that have been committed for weapons and services. Seventy-eight percent of Israel’s arms imports since 2000 came from the US, the Council on Foreign Relations reported.

The US and Israel launched a military attack on Iran on February 28 which killed Iranian Supreme Leader Ali Khalemenei and dozens of students in an all-girls primary education school. In a previous Bulatlat report, it was reported that this attack violates the right to self-determination enshrined in the United Nations Charter and the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights.

Read: US–Israel violates UN Charter, international law in strikes on Iran

As of this writing, the war continues and the impact extends to the neighboring countries in Asia like the Philippines through increases in the prices of petroleum products. An additional 1.34 million Filipinos became poor due to the oil price shocks since the US-Israel aggression on Iran.

Read: Oil price shocks push more than 1M Filipinos to poverty – study

“It does not only show the extent of the US’ undermining the Rome Statute and the ICC. It likewise speaks to its unabashed temerity to use its tools to evade accountability,” Palabay said. (DAA)

title: Mazlûm Ebdî: Entegrasyon dawî bû
content:
Mazlûm Ebdî amaje bi rejîma Baasê û desthilatên xwedî siyasetên şovenîst kir ku di dirêjahiya salan de wan siyasetên guhertina demografiya herêmê û erebkirina wê kirin. Ebdî da zanîn ku Rêveberiya Xweser di dirêjahiya 15 salan de li hember van siyasetan û vegerandina nasnameya herêmê xebitî.


Encama berxwedana gel


Ebdî, got herêm di salên borî de şahidê şerekî hovane kir û xelkê jî li hember êrişan xwe parast. Bi wê re QSDê hat damezrandin.


Di axaftina xwe de Ebdî destnîşan kir ku hilweşîna rejîma Baasê û destpêkirina avakirina Sûriyeya nû qonaxeke cuda ava kir û got biryara tevlêbûna li Sûriyeya nû li ser bingeha peymana 29ê Çileyê hat.


Entegrasyona saziyên ewlehî, leşkerî û îdarî yên ku di salên borî de hatine avakirin tev li saziyên dewletê dibin, nasname û destkeftiyên xwe parastî ne.


"Entegrasyon dawî bû"


Ebdî got “Qonaxa entegrasyona saziyên leşkerî, ewlehî û îdar di nava saziyên dewletê de bi dawî bû û ji îro pê ve dest bi qonaxeke nû bû.”


Ebdî bang li xelkê herêmê kir ku saziyên bi fedakariyên şehîdan hatin damezrandin biparêzin, xebata piştigirya wan bikin.


Mazlûm Ebdî şervanên hêzên Kurdistanî yên li kêleka QSDê li dijî êrişên li ser herêmê sekinîne bi bîr anîn û tevahî kesên li kêleka gel sekinîne û di oxira parastina wî de şehîd ketine silav kir.


Di dewama axaftina xwe de Mazlûm Ebdî diyar kir ku têkoşîna di oxira misogerkirina mafên gelê Kurd û tevahî pêkhateyan de dê bidome û dê qonaxa bê şahidê xebata siyasî ya zêde be ku mafên rewa di destûra Sûriyeyê de werin misogerkirin.


Fermandarê Giştî yê QSDê Mazlûm Ebdî di dawiyê de got Qamişlo dikare bibe navenda çand, siyasî û pirrengiyê û bang li tevahî pêkhateyên herêmê kir ku bi hev re di oxira siberojeke aştiyane bixebitin.

title: O que é o Partido Digital Bolsonarista? – com Marcos Nobre
content:
Os eleitores da família Bolsonaro são “gado”? Os apoiadores da extrema direita são apenas pessoas “imbecis”? Para o professor e pesquisador Marcos Nobre, reduzir adversários políticos a uma massa hegemônica é um erro da esquerda que leva à derrota nas disputas de ideias, afetos e até mesmo de

eleições

.


Atualmente, o Brasil tem 30 partidos registrados, e outros 23 em formação. Mas também existem organizações não oficiais que vêm influenciando o campo político: os chamados

partidos digitais

, que vêm sendo estudados por Marcos Nobre, convidado do Pauta Pública desta semana.


Na entrevista com Andrea Dip ele explica o que é um partido digital e suas principais diferenças em relação aos partidos tradicionais, com foco no Partido Digital Bolsonarista. Marcos Nobre também compartilha quais são suas perspectivas para as eleições deste ano.


Entenda o significado dessas mudanças no cenário político brasileiro e deixe seu comentário sobre o que você acha que podemos esperar da campanha política, que acaba de começar oficialmente.

author: A.N.A.
title: [EUA] O que é ação direta?
content:
Parece haver alguma confusão recentemente sobre o significado do termo ação direta.


Seu uso entre radicais ampliou a definição a ponto de torná-la sem sentido. Da maneira como é usada, alguém poderia pensar que significa simplesmente militante ou intenso, uma forma mais agressiva de manguear. Essa distorção do termo levou muitos a acreditar que algumas ações são ações diretas quando não são e vice-versa.


Ação direta significa o uso não mediado (também conhecido como direto) do poder (também conhecido como ação) para resolver um problema. O que significa não mediado? Significa eliminar o intermediário, não recorrer à autoridade, negociar, convencer ou pedir. Aqui está um exemplo: um grupo de amigos está com fome. Para resolver essa necessidade com ação direta, eles podem cultivar, colher, caçar ou roubar algum alimento e comê-lo. Isso é ação direta porque eles não buscam a ajuda ou permissão de ninguém responsável. Se eles marchassem pela rua com cartazes sobre como estão com fome, isso seria um protesto. Se eles pressionassem políticos ou capitalistas para lhes dar comida, isso seria 

lobby

: eles estariam apelando às autoridades para alcançar seu objetivo, em vez de fazer isso eles mesmos.


Algumas pessoas podem querer abolir a polícia, então elas marcham pelas ruas fazendo discursos exigindo o fim do policiamento e bloqueando o trânsito, e algumas delas são presas após alguns empurrões com os policiais. Isso parece um protesto militante, mas não é ação direta. Se as mesmas pessoas começassem a desmontar a infraestrutura policial, ou atrapalhar o trabalho da polícia, ou ignorar as ordens policiais, isso seria ação direta. O que torna a segunda ação direta e não a primeira é que o segundo exemplo envolve pessoas começando a desmontar a própria polícia. No primeiro exemplo, os manifestantes não aboliriam a polícia por conta própria; em vez disso, eles agitariam as coisas e exigiriam que outra pessoa abolisse a polícia. O caráter chamativo, ilegal ou intenso de uma ação não é o que a torna uma ação direta. O que torna algo uma ação direta é a natureza imediata e auto-organizada do ato. É por isso que, quando os trabalhadores ocupam um local de trabalho com a intenção de administrá-lo eles mesmos, isso é considerado uma ação direta, mas se os trabalhadores ocupam um local de trabalho para influenciar políticas, isso é uma forma extrema de 

lobby

. O mesmo pode ser dito sobre a destruição de propriedade: se alguém quebra a janela de um banco para pressionar os banqueiros a parar de investir nas forças armadas, é um protesto agressivo; se a mesma janela é quebrada com a intenção de causar danos ou interromper os negócios do banco, então é uma ação direta.


Quando os termos usados por rebeldes e ativistas têm definições e usos pouco claros e confusos, torna-se mais difícil comunicar, quanto mais compartilhar análises e discutir objetivos e intenções. Chamar os protestos de ação direta tem o potencial de limitar a imaginação, afinal, se alguém pensa que gritar e segurar cartazes é a maneira mais direta de participar da luta, essa pessoa exclui todas as possibilidades de assumir a responsabilidade de mudar literalmente a situação ou o ambiente que a oprime e explora. Quando há uma compreensão clara do que significa ação direta, fica mais difícil usar o termo para fazer algo parecer duro ou militante, e mais fácil olhar honestamente para as táticas usadas na luta e decidir por si mesmo se elas parecem eficazes (independentemente de serem ou não ações diretas).


Fonte: zine “Words Mean Things-A Compilation of Anarchist Articles”

title: David Wengrow sends letter of support for the Peace and Democratic Society Process
content:
Archaeology Professor David Wengrow has penned a letter supporting the Peace and Democratic Society Process.


Wengrow's letter reads as follows:


"Thank you for asking me to reflect on this significant moment in world history. On 7 March 2014, the late anthropologist David Graeber emailed me a draft of the foreword he was writing for Abdullah Öcalan's book, 'Manifesto for a Democratic Civilization: The Age of Masked Gods and Disguised Kings.' At the time, I was in Kurdistan, carrying out archaeological fieldwork near the town of Halabja, close to the border between Iran and Iraq, at the foot of the Zagros Mountains.


It was the right place to be reading Graeber's reflections on 'the historical tragedy of a region whose women once made contributions to human civilization without parallel, but which has since been reduced to a bloody plaything of empire.' My own research there focused on the Neolithic past — the very period in which Öcalan's writings search for the roots of alternatives to patriarchal civilization. To the west, in the Darband-i Gawr (Infidel Pass) range in Karadağ, there stands an ancient trace of that later civilization: a monumental figure of a king carved into the rock, crushing the mountain people beneath his feet like a terrifying Leviathan. This relief dates back more than four thousand years — a fairly long time for anyone to remain under someone else's foot. These systems of domination, which first emerged in the Middle East roughly five thousand years ago, have continually resurfaced in one form or another ever since. For many people, this is indeed what the word "civilization" has come to mean (to borrow George Orwell's phrase, "a boot stamping on a human face — forever").


And yet every new form of human society is also unique in its own right. Social forms developed under certain technological conditions can re-emerge under quite different ones. Today, for instance, it has become fairly common to speak of the age we live in as one of "managerial feudalism," or sometimes "techno-feudalism." To my mind, one of Öcalan's key intellectual and political contributions is his argument that this logic does not apply solely to systems of domination — the same logic can apply to forms of human freedom as well. This view is often dismissed as utopian or idealistic. For a university academic like myself, even entertaining such ideas is enough to draw immediate ridicule from one's colleagues. According to Öcalan, the Neolithic is where the Mother Goddesses were born. Universities are where they died.


Why? No serious scholar denies that the Neolithic Middle East was the source of the material innovations that shaped the modern world: from plant and animal domestication to weaving, metallurgy, culinary culture, and architectural techniques — all of it laid the foundations of urban life. Such innovations spread across areas far larger than those later occupied by the kingdoms, empires, and nation-states that followed — without any coercive apparatus to direct them, and without any significant material infrastructure to sustain their advance.


What kind of mindset created this world — one in which "social relations" could carry meaning outside the logic of the market or of "growth," yet in which societies could nonetheless spread across continents? Why have we so thoroughly forgotten this?


The critical moment in the Middle East that you've asked me to reflect on carries a tragic significance. For this region of the world is not only where some of humanity's most enduring cultural revolutions took place, but also where those revolutions were first placed in the service of an apparatus of coercion and exploitation. For the vast majority of the people native to it, this has meant the longest uninterrupted experience of invasion, annexation, and exploitation in history: more than four thousand years as "a bloody plaything of empire."


Today, this is also the place where the masks of the "masked gods" have fallen away, where the king no longer disguises himself, and where the true, jarring face of our present world order is laid bare. It therefore seems hard to argue against Öcalan's central claim — made, fittingly, in this very place — that we might finally be able to discover, with certainty, whether this way of being in the world is truly the only option available to us. Thank you again for inviting me to share my thoughts."

title: Bayındır: This is a process to participate in and shape
content:
The process concerning the Kurdish question has entered a new phase with the removal of arms from the equation and the passage of legal measures in parliament. Debate continues over how this phase will progress, the participation of Kurdish society in the process, the scope of a democratic solution and the steps that need to be taken in the period ahead.


ANF spoke to Keskin Bayındır, Co-Chair of the Democratic Regions Party (DBP), about the next stage of the process, the building of a democratic society and democratic republic, the expectations of Kurdish society, local democracy and equal citizenship, the impact of developments in the Middle East on the process, and his observations from the field. Bayındır also discussed the public meetings organized by the DBP and said: “People want to be part of decision-making mechanisms. Society wants peace, but people also want to know how peace will change their lives.”


The passage of the legal regulation in parliament marked an important legal threshold in the process. However, a significant section of Kurdish society still has questions such as: “Where is this process heading? What will it bring for the Kurds? What will be the scope and guarantees of the democratic solution?” What concrete steps need to be taken in the next stage for the Kurdish people to feel that they are subjects of the process and for trust in the process to be strengthened?


I think we first need to properly define what we call “confusion” here. I do not see this as society distancing itself from the process or as reluctance towards peace. On the contrary, there is a very strong desire for peace within Kurdish society. But alongside this desire, there is also a very strong memory. Therefore, the question society is actually asking is not, “Should there be peace or not?” It is rather, “What will be the institutional framework for peace this time?”


I think this is where the main tension emerges today. Some elements of the process have become concrete; an important threshold has been crossed in terms of taking arms out of the equation and the related legal regulations. However, an equally concrete framework has not yet emerged regarding the mechanisms through which the political and democratic demands of Kurdish society will be addressed. Therefore, it is entirely natural for society to ask, “What will happen next?”


I see this as a demand for guarantees rather than a crisis of trust. It would be wrong to treat trust merely as a psychological issue. Political trust is created through the predictability of institutions. If a citizen’s rights depend on the government’s preferences, the political circumstances or day-to-day balances of power, what exists is not trust but expectation. A genuine relationship of citizenship emerges where rights are guaranteed by law. Therefore, simply telling Kurdish society, “Trust us,” is not enough.


What needs to be said is, “Let us together create the legal and political mechanisms that will enable you to trust.” From my perspective, there are three fundamental issues here: predictability, participation and guarantees. By predictability, I mean that the roadmap of the process should be understandable to society. What stage are we at? What is the next stage? Which institution will do what? What legal regulations will be on the agenda? These need to be as clear as possible.


The second is participation. We say that the Kurdish people must cease to be the “subject matter” of the process and become its subject. But being a subject does not simply mean being asked for an opinion. Being a subject means having an influence on the formation of decisions and being able to oversee the outcome of the decisions taken. If you listen to the people but keep the decision-making mechanism closed, that is consultation, not participation.


Therefore, permanent and institutional mechanisms involving political parties, municipalities, women’s organizations, youth organizations, labour organizations, professional associations, academia, intellectuals and civil society should be established. The third issue is guarantees. No democratic achievement can become permanent without constitutional and legal guarantees.


For example, on local democracy, it is not enough simply to say, “Municipalities will be strengthened.” Legal mechanisms are needed to protect the will of elected representatives, clarify the distribution of powers between the central administration and local governments …

title: Luigi Mangione: η ώρα της απολογίας
content:
Στις 4 Δεκεμβρίου 2024 ο Brian Thompson, 50 ετών, δέχεται θανατηφόρους πυροβολισμούς έξω από ξενοδοχείο στο Μανχάταν, καθώς κατευθύνεται προς την ετήσια επενδυτική διάσκεψη της εταιρίας που UnitedHealth Group. Αργότερα εντοπίζεται ένα σακίδιο με μασκότ χρήματα Monopoly και μαύρο μπουφάν Tommy Hilfiger σε πάρκο της πόλης.


Ο Brian Thompson ήταν ο Διευθύνων Σύμβουλος (CEO) της UnitedHealthcare, του ασφαλιστικού σκέλους του ομίλου UnitedHealth Group. Είχε αναλάβει τα ηνία της εταιρείας το 2021. ‘Ήταν επικεφαλής μιας επιχείρησης που παρείχε ασφαλιστική κάλυψη υγείας σε περισσότερους από 49 εκατομμύρια Αμερικανούς, με τα έσοδα του τομέα αυτού να φτάνουν τα 281 δισεκατομμύρια δολάρια τον προηγούμενο χρόνο. Το πακέτο αποδοχών του ανερχόταν σε 10,2 εκατομμύρια δολάρια ετησίως.


NYPD


Ο

 Luigi Mangione

 πιθανότατα γνώριζε πού έμενε ο Thompson, επειδή η τοποθεσία συνδεόταν δημόσια με την προγραμματισμένη εταιρική εκδήλωση καθώς είχε ανακοινωθεί δημοσίως ανακοινωθεί ότι θα πραγματοποιηθεί στο ξενοδοχείο New York Hilton Midtown, όπου σημειώθηκε ο πυροβολισμός


9 Δεκεμβρίου 2024

 — Ύστερα από ανθρωποκυνηγητό, ο Luigi Mangione εντοπίζεται και συλλαμβάνεται σε εστιατόριο McDonald’s στην Πενσυλβάνια,. Στο σακίδιό του εντοπίζεται τρισδιάστατα εκτυπωμένο πιστόλι που, σύμφωνα με την εισαγγελία, ταιριάζει με το όπλο του εγκλήματος, καθώς και σημειωματάριο με αναφορές στην πρόθεσή του να στοχεύσει στέλεχος ασφαλιστικής εταιρείας υγείας.


11 Δεκεμβρίου 2024

 — Ο Mangione οδηγείται σε δικαστήριο της Altoona για ακρόαση έκδοσης, φωνάζοντας δημόσια για «προσβολή στη νοημοσύνη του αμερικανικού λαού.


 


17 Δεκεμβρίου 2024

 — Ο εισαγγελέας του Μανχάταν, Alvin Bragg, ανακοινώνει ότι στον Mangione έχουν απαγγελθεί σε 11 κατηγορίες σε πολιτειακό επίπεδο, μεταξύ των οποίων ανθρωποκτονία εκ προμελέτης πρώτου βαθμού και ανθρωποκτονία ως πράξη τρομοκρατίας, μεταξύ πολλών άλλων.


19 Δεκεμβρίου 2024

 — Ο Mangione παραιτείται από το δικαίωμα αντίστασης στην έκδοσή του στην Πενσυλβάνια και μεταφέρεται στη Νέα Υόρκη, όπου εμφανίζεται σε δικαστήριο του Μανχάταν.


Αύγουστος 2026

 — Ο Mangione ομολογεί ενοχή σε δύο ομοσπονδιακές κατηγορίες παρακολούθησης, κλείνοντας οριστικά την ομοσπονδιακή υπόθεση εναντίον του. Η δικηγόρος του καταθέτει αίτημα απόρριψης της παράλληλης πολιτειακής υπόθεσης, επικαλούμενη τη συνταγματική αρχή του «διπλού κινδύνου», η οποία απαγορεύει τη διπλή δίωξη ενός ατόμου για το ίδιο αδίκημα (ακόμα και σε πολιτειακή δίωξη).


 


Όταν ο Mangione είπε ψύχραιμα στο ομοσπονδιακό δικαστήριο

«εγώ πυροβόλησα και εκείνος πέθανε»

, δεν παραδέχθηκε απλώς έναν φόνο. Αποκάλυψε την πληγή που αιμορραγεί εδώ και δεκαετίες στην Αμερική — ένα σύστημα υγείας που βάζει το κέρδος πάνω από την ανθρώπινη ζωή.


Όταν η “άρνηση” γίνεται επιχειρηματικό μοντέλο


Μετά τη δολοφονία εντοπίζονται οι κάλυκες στο σημείο και γίνεται γνωστό πως ήταν χαραγμένες τρεις λέξεις:

“Καθυστέρηση”

 (Delay),

“Άρνηση”

 (Deny),

“Εκθρόνιση”

 (Depose). Οι λέξεις αυτές περιγράφουν με ακρίβεια το

επιχειρηματικό μοντέλο της αμερικανικής ασφαλιστικής βιομηχανίας,

 με τακτικές όπως καθυστέρηση της πληρωμής, άρνηση κάλυψης, και αν ο ασθενής επιβιώσει, σύρε τον στα δικαστήρια. Τα νούμερα είναι ενδεικτικά:


Το ποσοστό απόρριψης ασφαλιστικών απαιτήσεων στις ΗΠΑ κυμαίνεται σταθερά μεταξύ 14% και 16%.


Μόνο στη Μέριλαντ, οι απορρίψεις εκτοξεύθηκαν κατά 40% από το 2019.


Μια έρευνα του 2024 έδειξε ότι το 73% των παρόχων υγείας δηλώνουν ότι οι απορρίψεις αυξάνονται συνεχώς.


Η ίδια η UnitedHealthcare, η εταιρεία του θύματος, έχει ποσοστό απόρριψης 32% — διπλάσιο από τον μέσο όρο του κλάδου (16%).


Και η κοινωνία έδωσε απαντήσεις:


Δημοσκόπηση του Emerson College έδειξε ότι το 41% των Αμερικανών κάτω των 30 ετών θεωρεί τη δολοφονία του Thompson “αποδεκτή”.


Σχεδόν 7 στους 10 Αμερικανούς πιστεύουν ότι τα κέρδη και οι απορρίψεις των ασφαλιστικών εταιρειών φέρουν “μεγάλη” ή “μέτρια” ευθύνη για τον θάνατο του Thompson.


Στα social media, η ανάρτηση της UnitedHealthcare για το θάνατο του CEO της συγκέντρωσε 75.000 αντιδράσεις γέλιου — ένα ανελέητο χλευασμό προς μια εταιρεία που αρνείται την περίθαλψη σε όσους την έχουν ανάγκη.


Ο Mangione δεν είναι φτωχός, απελπισμένος, ή βαριά ασθενής. Είναι απόφοιτος του Πανεπιστημίου της Πενσυλβάνια με την ειδικότητα του μηχανικού λογισμικού και προερχόταν από εύπορη οικογένεια. Υπέφερε για χρόνια από έντονους πόνους στην σπασμένη του πλάτη, και όπως εκατομμύρια άλλοι Αμερικανοί, βρέθηκε αντιμέτωπος με ένα σύστημα που τον …

title: Hatimoğulları visits prisoners in Silivri Prison
content:
Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) Co-Chair Tülay Hatimoğulları visited prisoners in Silivri Prison. Hatimoğulları made the following statement after the visit:


“Today, we are addressing the entire public in Turkey from Silivri Prison. We have just met with our imprisoned friends. We met with Socialist Party of the Oppressed (ESP) Co-Chair Murat Çepni, former Peoples’ Democratic Party (HDP) municipal co-mayor Bekir Kaya, and political prisoner Nasrullah Kuran. We held the meeting together with our Bitlis MP Hüseyin Olan. Of course, we mutually assessed the process during this meeting. We discussed both the recently adopted framework law and what political openings, what expected democratic openings, will follow this framework law in Turkey.


 


I would like to begin by recalling the major operation against our component, the ESP, on 3 February, which resulted in detentions and arrests. On the 200th day since this operation, we once again reiterate our call from here for the release of our ESP comrades. Detention orders were issued for 110 people in the operation against the ESP, and 84 socialists were arrested at the time. Forty-eight of our friends, including ESP Co-Chair and former HDP MP Murat Çepni, remain imprisoned. ESP Deputy Co-Chair Sezin Uçar, DEM Party Women’s Coordination member Fatma Çelik and Limter-İş President İleri Devrim Yurtsever have also been imprisoned for exactly 200 days.


Why were ESP members, socialists, revolutionaries and patriots detained? Why were they arrested? Prisons in Turkey today are overflowing with political prisoners simply for exercising freedom of thought and expression and the right to democratic action. Why? Because they want a fair and democratic order in Turkey. Because they demand an end to violence against women and femicides in Turkey. They are now in prison because they defend the rights of workers, labourers, the poor, farmers and tradespeople against rising unemployment and poverty in Turkey. They are in prison because they stood alongside people searching for their disappeared relatives and showed solidarity with Emine Ocak and others like her. They are in prison because they opposed the 10 October Ankara Train Station Massacre, when the doves of peace and democracy were massacred. They are in prison because they defended the right to life. ESP and Socialist Refoundation Party (SYKP) youth who wanted to take toys to children in Kobanê were subjected to the brutality and violence of ISIS in Suruç, where we experienced a major massacre. We lost many of our comrades there. Today, revolutionaries and socialists in Turkey are in prison because they defended the right to life against the massacres carried out by ISIS, those bloodstained murderers. Look at what is in the case file of ESP Deputy Chair Uğur Ok. They are being prosecuted because they said, ‘The Kurdish question must be resolved through a just and democratic peace,’ and because they established the ‘Tribune of the Oppressed’ in connection with this.


There are very important developments in Turkey today. On 10 August, a framework law was adopted with the support of a large majority in Parliament. We regard the framework law as a first step against the approach that has confined the Kurdish question within the framework of ‘terrorism’, against 50 years of war and conflict in this country and the unresolved Kurdish question. Today, we are talking about peace. Today, while negotiating for peace, we are also struggling for it. At every opportunity, we stress that while negotiating for the Kurdish question to be resolved through peaceful and democratic means in these lands, the struggle for democracy must also be strengthened across the broadest possible spectrum. Because we know that the adoption of this law alone will not democratize Turkey, but it can open the way wide for democratization. That is why we value this law and consider it important.


At a time when this law has been adopted and the dialogue process is continuing, Figen Yüksekdağ, Selahattin Demirtaş and our Central Executive Board members from that period are still in prison because of the Kobanê Case. We happened to see them in the prison just a short while ago and exchanged greetings. Osman Kavala, Can Atalay, Çiğdem Mater and Tayfun Kahraman are still imprisoned here in Silivri behind us. Once again, we want to convey this message to the government, the state and the entire public in Turkey: At a time when the peace and …

title: Another protester executed in Iran
content:
Iran’s semi-official Tasnim news agency reported that a foreign national had been executed over charges related to the January protests.


Ghaem Hosseini, who was accused of being involved in the killing of four police officers during protests in Malekshahr, Isfahan, on 8 January, was reportedly executed this morning.


The report also stated that Erfan Esfandiari, Gol Mohammad Mohammadi, Amir Hossein Safari and Abolfazl Sepahi had previously been executed in connection with the same incident.

author: Unknown
title: Mine workers’ protest enters its 12th day
content:
Workers from Doruk Mining and Elazığ Eti Gümüş, companies affiliated with Yıldızlar SSS Holding, are continuing their protest in front of the Ministry of Energy and Natural Resources on its 12th day, demanding unpaid wages and compensation, under the leadership of the Independent Mine Workers’ Union.


On Thursday night, almost 100 miners were taken into custody. They were released this morning and said they will go to the Ministry of Energy and Natural Resource. 


Speaking at the press statement held in front of the ministry on Thursday, Başaran Aksu, an organizing specialist with the Independent Mine Workers’ Union, said: “We will not leave here; we will wait. The result may be another detention, so be it. We are trying to meet with the deputy minister, but there is a wall in front of us.” He added: “When the Interior Minister spoke by phone with Union General President Gökay Çakır, he said that he was ‘under pressure to resolve the problem.’ The deputy energy minister had thanked us before; now, for 11 days, he has been avoiding meeting with us.” Aksu was one of the miners taken into custody.


Murat Çelik, a worker at Elazığ Eti Gümüş, reacted to the fact that they had been detained five times since arriving on August 10 to demand all their employment rights. He said: “I am married and the father of four children. Three of my children have to go to the hospital, and I cannot send them money. Am I the heartless one, or is it Sebahattin Yıldız, or the Ankara Police Chief? I am calling out to those who are treating us heartlessly: our children are in a terrible situation. One of our friends who is resisting here has a son whose wedding he could not attend; another friend’s wife is pregnant and he cannot take care of her. We have friends here whose children are sick. They need to take care of their children, but those children see on the news that their fathers have been detained. Have you ever questioned Sebahattin Yıldız?”

title: Majid Maleki Meighani: Social power in Middle East must be democratized - Part One
content:
Majid Maleki Meighani is an Iranian writer, political analyst, translator, and photographer whose work explores the relationship between capitalism, imperialism, class, and political power. Writing from a critical Marxist perspective, he is particularly interested in the political and social dynamics of Iran, West Asia, and the wider Global South, with a focus on societies located within the periphery and semi-periphery of the world-system. His writing brings together political economy, geopolitics, and the experiences of ordinary people and social movements, shaped in part by years of travel and direct engagement with communities across Iran, Turkey, Iraq, and Syria. His own experience of political imprisonment in Iran has also informed his understanding of state power, repression, resistance, and the possibilities of political transformation. He has translated Walter LaFeber’s 

Inevitable Revolutions: The United States in Central America

 and 

Voices of the Arab Spring

 into Persian. His writings have appeared in ZNetwork, Akhbar-e Rooz, Tribune Zamane, and other independent publications.


Majid Maleki Meighani, who analyzes developments in the Middle East, emphasizes that events in the region need to be examined on three levels: the global political economy, geopolitical competition between states, and social struggles within individual countries. Meighani notes that, in the Middle East’s current landscape, states occupy different positions within the hierarchy of the world system, and that each is part of a global capitalist order built on inequalities. For this reason, he points out that understanding the conflict-ridden and crisis-stricken processes in the Middle East requires examining who controls capital accumulation, trade, technology, security mechanisms, energy corridors and political decision-making processes. Drawing on his experience as a political prisoner in Iran, Meighani highlights the power of the state, repression, resistance and the possibilities for political transformation. In our interview, in which he discusses the uprisings that have developed across the region stretching from Morocco to Pakistan, the consequences of the Arab Spring, the competitive multipolar dynamics among actors such as Iran, Turkey, Israel and Saudi Arabia, as well as the Abraham Accords and the Mecca Pact, he points to the democratization of social power as the central issue.


The writer argues that a transformation must take place by transferring part of the power concentrated in states, armies, major concentrations of capital and geopolitical networks to organized society. Otherwise, he says, even if the wars come to an end, this will not mean that the crisis in the Middle East has ended; rather, the form of the war will simply change.


The Middle East, stretching from Morocco to Pakistan, is at the center of wars, crises, and conflicts. Can this situation be explained simply through the plunder of resources?


In my view, no. Reducing the crisis of the Middle East to the plunder of resources explains part of the reality, but it is not sufficient to understand the structure of the region. Oil, gas, trade routes, ports, water, and other natural resources are undoubtedly important, but the problem goes deeper than the direct appropriation of resources. What we are witnessing in the Middle East is part of an unequal global capitalist system in which states occupy different positions within the hierarchy of the world-system.


The Middle East has to be understood simultaneously at three levels: the global political economy, geopolitical competition among states, and social struggles within individual countries. If we look only at geopolitics, people become spectators while regional and global powers compete over them. If we look only at economics, we lose sight of the role of the state, ideology, religion, nationalism, and history. And if we look only at domestic politics, we overlook its relationship with the global structure of power.


In this sense, the central question in the Middle East is not simply, “Who controls the oil?” It is also: Who controls the processes of capital accumulation, trade, technology, security, energy corridors, and political decision-making?


The United Arab Emirates is an interesting example. It is a small country that has acquired influence far beyond its demographic weight through capital, ports, financial networks, technology, relations with major powers, and military projection …

title: İşkenceye uğrayan mahpus, suç duyurusunda bulundu
content:
Van F Tipi Yüksek Güvenlikli Cezaevinde tutulan Nevzat Öner, 11 Ağustos'ta gittiği Van Yüzüncü Yıl Dursun Odabaş Tıp Merkezi'nde kelepçeli muayeneyi kabul etmediği gerekçesiyle görevli askerler tarafından darbedilerek işkenceye maruz bırakıldı. İşkence, Öner'in haftalık telefon görüşmesinde durumu ailesine aktarmasıyla ortaya çıktı. Yaşadığı sağlık problemi sebebiyle gittiği hastanede jandarma tarafından kelepçeli muayene dayatmasına maruz kaldığını aktaran Öner, dayatmaya karşı çıktığı için hastaneden ring aracına oradan da cezaevine getirilene kadar işkenceye maruz bırakıldığını aktardı.

Mezopotamya Ajansı'ndan Ceylan Şahinli'nin haberine göre, cezaevinde görüşmeye giden avukatların edindikleri bilgilere göre Öner, hekimin kelepçelerin çıkarılması yönünde aksi bir talebi bulunmamasına rağmen, görevli jandarma personeli tarafından "Kelepçeli muayene olacaksın" denilerek muayene olmaya zorlandı. Öner’in kelepçeli tedaviyi reddetmesi üzerine hastane koridorunda darbedilmeye başlandığı belirtildi. Bindirildiği ring aracında yetersiz hava şartlarına ve taleplerine rağmen kapıları açılmayan Öner, götürüldüğü cezaevinde idarenin darp izlerini fark etmesi üzerine mahpusu o halde içeri almayı reddetti. Öner, cezaevine götürülmeden yeniden hastaneye götürülerek darp raporu aldı. Öner’in uğradığı darp ve işkence, sevk edildiği hastaneden alınan sağlık raporuyla da belgelendi. Öner uygulanan işkenceye dair suç duyurusunda bulundu.

Eşini ayda sadece 2 kez görebildiklerini ve ayda sadece 2 haftada bir yapabildikleri telefon görüşmesiyle sesini duyabildiklerini belirten Adalet Öner, "O gün de bizi telefonla aradı. Hastaneye götürüldüğü günü anlattı. Eşim, 'Kelepçeli tedaviyi kabul etmeyince, onu kelepçeyle sürükleyerek elini kanatıyorlar. Eşimin durumundan telefonda haberdar olduk. Eşim 7 yıldır cezaevinde. Bizle, avukatla görüş hakları kısıtlı" dedi.

Cezaevinde yaşanan işkencenin ardından ailenin başvurusu üzerine cezaevine gittiklerini ifade eden Özgürlük İçin Hukukçular Derneği (ÖHD) Van Şube üyesi Murat Özçiçek, Öner'in düşme sonucu kolunun ezilmesi üzerine revir doktorunun hastaneye sevki yaptığını aktardı. Özçiçek, jandarmanın muayene olması gereken Öner ile birlikte odaya girdiğini ve kelepçeli muayeneyi dayattığını belirterek, "Jandarma, Öner'e kelepçe ile muayene olacağını başka türlü izin vermeyeceklerini söylemiş ve onu zorlamış. Nevzat, bunu kabul etmeyince darbedip ring aracına götürmüşler. Darp sırasında Nevzat'ın kol, bilek ve ellerinde sıyrık ve çizikler oluşmuş. Özellikle kelepçe bileklerinde yaralanmalara sebep olmuş. Bunun yanı sıra vücudunun başkaca bölgelerinde de darp izleri mevcut. Nevzat, ringe bindirildiğinde astım hastası olduğunu ve içerinin havasız olduğunu jandarmaya söylemiş. Buna rağmen uzun bir süre ring aracında kapılar kapalı bir şekilde bekletilip cezaevine geri götürülmüş" dedi.

Cezaevi girişinde haber verilen cezaevi müdürünün, Öner'in darbedildiğini fark etmesi üzerine "Onu bu halde cezaevine almam" diyerek hastaneye geri gönderdiğini söyleyen Özçiçek, Öner'in geri gönderildiği hastanede darp raporu aldığını aktardı. Birçok mahpus hastalığı ne kadar ağır olursa olsun bu uygulama sebebiyle tedavi olmadan dönüyor. Bu uygulamalar işkenceye varmış durumda. Defalarca kez bu yönlü şikayetlerde bulunduk. Fakat ne bakanlığın ne de başkaca bir kurum veya kişinin bu duruma yönelik bir çalışması olmadı" diye konuştu.

Kelepçeli muayene dayatmasının insan hakkı ihlali olduğunun altını çizen Van-Hakkari Tabip Odası ve Türkiye İnsan Hakları Vakfı (TİHV) Van Temsilcisi Hüseyin Yaviç, tabip odasına kelepçeli muayene dayatmasına dair çok sayıda suç duyurusu geldiğini kaydetti. Yaviç, uzun yıllardır buna karşı mücadele verdiklerini ancak yeniden aynı hak ihlalini protesto etmek zorunda kaldıklarını söyledi. Yaviç, "Sağlık hakkı ihlali kabul edilir bir durum değil. Kelepçeli muayene, ağız içi dayatması gibi durumlar insan onurunu zedeleyen ve mahpusların sağlık haklarını ellerinden alan uygulamalardır. title: Nijerya'da çiftçi ve işçileri taşıyan tekne alabora oldu: 52 kişi yaşamını yitirdi
content:
Nijerya'nın kuzeybatısındaki Sokoto eyaletinde çiftçi ve işçilerin bulunduğu teknenin alabora olması sonucu 52 kişi hayatını kaybetti.

Nijerya Ulusal Acil Durum Yönetim Ajansının (NEMA) Sokoto Operasyon Başkanı Tukur Abubakar, bu sabah itibarıyla kazada 52 kişinin öldüğünü açıkladı.

Abubakar, ölenler arasında aynı aileden 11 kişinin de bulunduğunu belirtti.

Kaza, perşembe günü Sokoto eyaletine bağlı Goronyo bölgesindeki Gorau kasabasında meydana geldi. Yaklaşık 70 kişiyi taşıyan tekne, çiftçi ve işçilerin pirinç tarlalarına gitmek için su yolundan geçtiği sırada alabora oldu.

Sokoto Eyalet Meclisi Üyesi Nasiru Adamu, yaptığı açıklamada 40'tan fazla kişinin öldüğünü, ekiplerin 16 kişiyi kurtardığını ve teknedeki yolcuların çoğunun 10 ila 15 yaşlarındaki çocuklardan oluştuğunu söylemişti.

Nijerya'da aşırı yolcu taşınması, teknelerin bakımsızlığı ve güvenlik kurallarına yeterince uyulmaması nedeniyle özellikle yağışlı mevsimde tekne kazaları sık yaşanıyor.

author: Unknown
title: The reality of change and transformation
content:
The bill widely referred to as the “Framework Law” was passed by parliament on the night of 10 August, shifting attention to the practical steps that will follow and to the political forces responsible for taking them. The law itself is intended to open the way for politics and place responsibilities on political institutions. This means that all political institutions now face the task of correctly understanding these duties and responsibilities and undergoing the change and transformation necessary to fulfil them.


The parties concerned are well aware that the Peace and Democratic Society Process is not based on an agreement or a give-and-take arrangement, but is instead the product of a profound transformation in mentality and political approach. The parties are taking steps required by the changes they have made in their understanding and methods. Those that have undergone a fundamental transformation in their approach and methods are therefore taking more determined and effective steps, while those that struggle with such change and remain weak in this respect appear to be doing little more than taking certain steps out of necessity.


Abdullah Öcalan, who is well aware of this reality, defines change and transformation as the first truth in the Manifesto for a Democratic Communal Society, in which he sets out the theoretical foundations and framework of the Peace and Democratic Society Process. He regards dialectical materialism’s definition of change alone as truth as incomplete. Öcalan argues that change by itself has no direction and that its outcome cannot be known in advance, whereas considering change together with transformation means moving towards something new. On this basis, he argues that dialectics should be understood not merely through its destructive dimension, but above all through its constructive dimension.


The Peace and Democratic Society Process was developed not only as a result of the pressures and requirements created by political and military developments, but also as the outcome of such a transformation in mentality and political approach. Despite all the difficulties and obstacles, the successful completion of the first stage of the process and the step towards the second stage taken with the Framework Law adopted on the night of 10 August were essentially made possible by this change and transformation in political thinking. Almost everyone who has reflected on and debated the process recognizes this reality and acknowledges that Abdullah Öcalan was the driving force behind it. 


The practical steps required for the second stage must now be taken one after another. Indeed, there is already widespread debate over what these steps will or should entail. The Kurdish side and consistent democratic circles do not consider the law sufficient and have voiced criticism. They argue, for example, that as a foundational law, it should explicitly provide the basis for further legislation on freedom and democracy aimed at democratizing Turkey and resolving the Kurdish question. They also stress that the status of Abdullah Öcalan, the architect of the Peace and Democratic Society Process, should be clearly defined, including conditions in which he can live and work freely. Criticism and proposals have also been put forward regarding the language and structure of the law.


The law passed parliament with a record number of votes and, with the exception of some racist-fascist circles and certain social-nationalist groups, its historic significance and importance have been openly acknowledged and supported. This places a responsibility on political institutions, both government and opposition, right and left, to take new and creative practical steps. For this to happen, politics itself must undergo a profound and multidimensional transformation in both mentality and approach. The need for a new democratic breakthrough in politics has therefore become more urgent than ever.


The first significant development in this context was the split within the Republican People’s Party (CHP) and the establishment of a new party under the name YENİ Party. Led by Özgür Özel, YENİ Party has to some extent maintained the enthusiasm it generated within the CHP. However, its approach to the Framework Law has raised serious doubts about whether it can become the kind of social democratic party required by the new process. Social-nationalist influences appear to be placing pressure on YENİ Party, while it has yet …

title: CItizens in Mazıdağı block construction machinery brought in for solar power plant
content:
Residents continue to oppose a Solar Power Plant (GES) project planned on pastureland in the rural Girêsor neighborhood of Şemrex (Mazıdağı) district in Mêrdîn. Construction machinery was brought back to the area today to begin work as part of the project.


Villagers opposed to the GES project blocked the machinery from entering the construction site. The machinery was halted following the villagers’ intervention, while gendarmerie units were also dispatched to the area. Villagers, who make their living from livestock farming, gathered in the area to oppose the opening of the pastureland they use to the GES project. As the machinery and gendarmerie continue to wait in the area, the villagers have said they will not allow work to begin and are continuing their vigil at the site.

author: Tom Midlane
title: Israel Is Trying to Game ChatGPT Results About Gaza and the IDF
content:
Israel is planting sanitised PR stories online in an apparent attempt to influence how ChatGPT and other LLMs answer questions about the genocide in Gaza, the IDF and Zionism. 


More than 100 anonymous articles on Israel and Palestine were posted online within a week earlier this month by a new think tank connected to the Israeli government’s favoured PR firm in the US.


The articles are framed as questions that might be asked of a search engine or LLM, such as ‘

Who Is the Aggressor in the Israel-Palestine Conflict?

’

 and ‘

Does Hamas Account for Deaths Caused by Hamas Itself?

’ 


The ‘data reports’ appeared on the website of the Hanover Institute for Public Policy, a body created by a boutique ad agency called Piro as part of its work for Havas Media, the French PR company that handles most of Israel’s foreign influence work in the US,

Politico reports

.


Other LLM-friendly articles published on the Hanover website are titled ‘

Is There a Policy of Starvation in Gaza?

’ and ‘

Is the IDF the World’s Most Moral Army?’

 None of the AI-optimised articles have bylines, and no researchers are named on the website.


In public US records filed in August, the articles were described as being part of a $100,000 campaign aimed at “the creation and dissemination of factual, source-supported informational materials intended to educate the US public regarding Israel”.


Piro co-founder Daniel Rosenberg confirmed to Politico that his ad agency was retained by the Israeli state “to put accurate, sourced facts into the public record and to counter misinformation about Israel with verifiable information.” Havas Media and the Hanover Institute did not respond to Politico’s request for comment.


According to tests run by Piro, LLMs including ChatGPT were found to be drawing on articles published by the Hanover Institute when responding to questions about Gaza, the IDF, anti-Zionism and antisemitism. 


When Novara Media ran similar tests on ChatGPT, Claude and Perplexity, none used Hanover as a source when asked similar questions. However, reporters at the

Jerusalem Post

 found that Perplexity, an AI aggregator, did rely heavily on Hanover when asked ‘Is the IDF the most moral army?’

author: Unknown
title: Japonya'da oyun salonunu yakarak 5 kişiyi öldüren fail idam edildi
content:
Fotoğraf: Christopher Politano/Unsplash

Japonya’da 2009 yılında Osaka kentindeki bir oyun salonunu ateşe vererek 5 kişinin ölümüne neden olan Sunao Takami’nin idam edildiği bildirildi.

Japonya Adalet Bakanı Hiroshi Hiraguchi, 58 yaşındaki Takami’nin ölüm cezasının infaz edildiğini açıkladı. Böylece ülkede geçen yıl haziran ayından bu yana ilk kez bir mahkumun idam cezası uygulanmış oldu.

Takami’nin infazı, Başbakan Sanae Takaichi’nin görev döneminde gerçekleştirilen ilk idam olarak da kayıtlara geçti.

Takami, 2009 yılında Osaka’daki bir oyun salonunun zeminine benzin dökerek yangın çıkarmıştı. Yangında biri oyun salonu çalışanı, 4’ü müşteri olmak üzere toplam 5 kişi yaşamını yitirmiş, 10 kişi de yaralanmıştı.

Olayın ardından yakalanan Takami hakkında cinayet ve kundaklama suçlarından dava açıldı.

Yargılama sırasında Takami’nin olay sırasında akıl sağlığının yerinde olmadığı yönündeki savunma mahkeme tarafından kabul edilmedi.

Mahkeme, 2011 yılında Takami hakkında ölüm cezası verdi. Karara yapılan temyiz başvurusunun Japonya Yüksek Mahkemesi tarafından reddedilmesinin ardından ölüm cezası 2016 yılında kesinleşti.

Japonya, idam cezasını uygulamaya devam eden sınırlı sayıdaki gelişmiş ülkeler arasında bulunuyor. Takami’nin infazıyla ülkede geçen yıl haziran ayından bu yana ilk kez bir ölüm cezası uygulanmış oldu.

author: Dominic Gutoman
title: Right(s) Up: Spy-tagging as deflection tactic
content:
Photo by Raymun B. Villanueva/Kodao Productions

Context: The National Task Force to End Local Communist Armed Conflict (NTF-ELCAC) submits cases of “spy-tagging” to the United Nations Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights (UN-OHCHR) despite their bloody credibility on red-tagging and human rights violations

Human rights: Civil and political rights, international humanitarian law

Rights-holder: Public, human rights defenders, civil society

Duty-bearer: Armed Forces of the Philippines, Administration of Ferdinand Marcos Jr., United Nations

MANILA – The term “spy-tagging” is a deflection tactic, according to Amnesty International Philippines, as it is being used by the NTF-ELCAC to shift the accusation of human rights violations to non-state actors.

The statement came after the NTF-ELCAC published a post, with a photo showing UN Senior Adviser for Human Rights Signe Poulsen receiving a document from an NTF-ELCAC representative.

Cristina Palabay, secretary general of human rights group Karapatan, said that the recent post of the NTF-ELCAC is an act of “desperation for legitimacy when there is none at all.”

“International human rights mechanisms including UN Special Procedures, treaty bodies and the OHCHR itself have either questioned or called for the NTF-ELCAC’s abolition – a major indication that its existence is most unwanted,” Palabay said.

United Nations Special Rapporteurs Irene Khan and Ian Fry previously supported the call for the NTF-ELCAC’s abolition.

National Union of Peoples’ Lawyers President Ephraim Cortez said in a Facebook post that it was “misrepresented as proof of an alleged agreement for collaborative work.”

“Any collaborative work with a red-tagger like NTF-ELCAC will violate [UN] OHCHR’s very reason for existence. Its mandate is to promote and protect human rights by monitoring violations and assisting the government to strengthen its capacity to uphold international human rights standards,” Cortez said.

The UN OHCHR coordinates human rights activities throughout the United Nations System and acts as the secretariat of the Human Rights Council in Geneva, Switzerland. Its mandate includes assisting governments in fulfilling their human rights obligations, as well as providing assistance for the implementation of the international human rights laws.

Amnesty International Philippines reminded the NTF-ELCAC that under international law, the government is responsible for human rights violations committed, not only by its own state actors but also by non-state actors.

For the Commission on Human Rights, the two types of human rights violations are commission which refers to the violations perpetrated by state actors and omission which refers to the government’s failure to address violations committed by non-state actors.

“Government forces, led by NTF-ELCAC and recently DND Secretary Gilbert Teodoro, accuse communities of supporting rebel insurgency, a blatant practice of red-tagging which President Marcos, Jr. continues to condone,” said Ritz Lee Santos III, section director of Amnesty International Philippines, in a statement. He said that red-tagging has already resulted in deaths and destruction for the marginalized.

Under the Marcos Jr. administration, Karapatan documented 137 extrajudicial killings related to the government’s counterinsurgency program, 85 frustrated extrajudicial killings, 16 enforced disappearances, and 53 torture cases. There were hundreds more illegally arrested and searched.

Red-tagging has also been declared a threat to the right to life, liberty, and security, based on a Supreme Court decision in 2024.

“Their failure to take reasonable steps to prevent or respond to abuses committed by non-state actors is in itself a human rights violation. But framing criticisms of the government as communist propaganda while publicly tagging activists as terrorists are equally violations of international human rights laws as well,” Amnesty International-Philippines said in a social media post.

The group repeated the call to abolish the NTF-ELCAC as part of the human rights legislative agenda for the 20th Congress. In a press conference, Karapatan also called on the abolition of the task force for vilifying the victims of the April 19 massacre in Toboso, Negros Occidental and for continuously red-tagging individuals, organizations, and communities.

The UN OHCHR has yet to release a statement on this issue. (DAA)
